questions.text: What's the use of IAM allows the granting of temporary permits to a service of the AWS to access other resources on behalf of the user?
options: User IAM
Paper (Role) IAM
Customer-Managed Policy
Group IAM
questions.explanation: A Role of IAM can be assumed by services or users to obtain temporary credentials with specific permissions, without needing to share long-term credentials.
questions.hint: Think about the resource of IAM which may be temporarily assumed by a service to obtain short-term credentials.
optionRationales: A User IAM represents a long-term identity (usually a person or application) with permanent credentials — it has not been designed to be temporarily "absorbed" by a service of the AWS.
A Group IAM is just a way to group users to apply policies together — it cannot be assumed by a service nor generates temporary credentials.
Right. IAM can be assumed by services or users to obtain temporary credentials with specific permissions, without needing to share long-term credentials.
A customer-managed policy defines a reusable set of permissions, but needs to be attached to a user, group or role — it cannot itself be "assumed" to generate credentials.

questions.text: What's a Security Group in one VPC of AWS?
options: A Disk Encryption Service
A stateless firewall applied to sub-networks
A state-of-the-art firewall that controls input and output traffic
A repository of access keys
questions.explanation: Security Groups act as stateful state firewalls at the instance level, controlling the allowed in and out traffic.
questions.hint: Think of the firewall that operates at the instance level (ENI) and automatically remembers the return traffic of a permitted connection.
optionRationales: The non-stated firewall description applied to sub-networks corresponds to a Network ACL, not to one Security Group, which has been and acts at the instance level.
Correct.. Security Groups act as stateful state firewalls at the instance level, controlling the allowed in and out traffic.
Disk encryption is function of AWS KMS combined with EBS — is not the purpose of a Security Group, controlling network traffic, not encryption.
A repository of access keys would be something like the AWS Secrets Manager or IAM — is not related to the network traffic control of a Security Group.

questions.text: Which service allows you to store and manage secrets, such as database passwords, with automatic rotation?
options: AWS CloudFormation
Amazon Route 53
AWS Secrets Manager
Amazon S3 Glacier
questions.explanation: The AWS Secrets Manager allows you to store, retrieve and rotate secrets automatically as database credentials.
questions.hint: Think of the service created specifically to store sensitive credentials and rotate them automatically in integration with databases such as the RDS.
optionRationales: Correct. AWS Secrets Manager allows you to store, retrieve and rotate secrets automatically as database credentials.
The Amazon S3 Glacier is a low-cost storage class for data archiving — it has not been designed to manage secrets nor offers automatic credential rotation.
The AWS CloudFormation is an infrastructure service such as code (IaC) to provide resources via templates — it does not store or rotate secrets automatically.
The Amazon Route 53 is a service of DNS and traffic routing — not related to storage or rotation of credentials.

questions.text: What is the fundamental difference between a Network ACL (NACL) and one Security Group?
options: NACLs Cannot support exit rules
There's no difference, they're the same resource with different names.
Security Groups are unstated and NACLs have been
NACLs operate at the sub-network level and may have explicit rules of denial; Security Groups operate at the instance level and only allow permission rules
questions.explanation: NACLs are stateless, act at sub-network level and can explicitly deny traffic; Security Groups have been, act at the instance level and only allow rules of 'allow''.
questions.hint: Think of which of these two features operates at the sub-network level (with numbered rules of "allow" and "deny") and which operates at the instance level (only "allow"").
optionRationales: Correct.. NACLs are stateless, act at sub-network level and can explicitly deny traffic; Security Groups they've been, they've been at the instance level and they only allow rules of "allow"".
This option reverses reality: it is the Security Group which has been (stateful) and NACL which is stateless — the opposite of the option states.
NACLs support both entry and exit rules (and, because they are stateless, return traffic needs to be explicitly allowed in both directions) — the claim that they do not support exit is incorrect.
NACLs and Security Groups are distinct resources, with scopes (sub-network vs. instance), state behavior and capabilities of different rules—are not the same resource.

questions.text: What is the Amazon Route 53 health check used for?
options: Create VPCs automatically
Monitor endpoint health and route traffic only for healthy resources
Managing policies of the IAM
Encrypt records DNS
questions.explanation: The health checks of Route 53 monitor the availability of endpoints and can be used in routing policies to divert traffic from unhealthy resources.
questions.hint: Think of a periodic check that confirms if an endpoint is responding correctly before including it in the responses of DNS.
optionRationales: Right. Route 53 monitor the availability of endpoints and can be used in routing policies to divert traffic from unhealthy resources.
The Route 53 does not encrypt records DNS — DNS is a public protocol by nature; data encryption is treated by other services, such as the AWS KMS or TLS/HTTPS.
Creating VPCs is a network operation done via Amazon VPC (console/API/CLI) — is not a function of health checks of Route 53.
Managing policies of the IAM is the function of the service IAM — o Route 53 health check has no relation to identity and access permissions.

questions.text: What's the use of Amazon RDS allows to have a replica in standby in another Availability Zone for automatic failover?
options: Read Replica
Manual Snapshot
Multi-AZ Deployment
Parameter Group
questions.explanation: The Multi-AZ of RDS maintains a standby synchronous replica in another AZ, automatically promoting it in case of failure of the main instance.
questions.hint: Think about the resource of RDS which maintains a synchronous copy of the seat in another AZ, automatically promoted in case of failure.
optionRationales: A Read Replica is asynchronous and used primarily to scale readings or to disaster recovery between regions — it does not perform transparent automatic failure like Multi-AZ.
Right. RDS maintains a standby synchronous replica in another AZ, automatically promoting it in case of failure of the main instance.
A manual snapshot is a point-in-time copy of the database stored in S3 — restoring it creates a new instance, but does not provide automatic failover for a replica already in standby.
A Parameter Group defines database mechanism settings (e.g. memory parameters) — has no connection to standby or failover replicas between AZs.

questions.text: To ensure high availability of a web application in EC2, which practice is recommended?
options: Disable the Auto Scaling to avoid costs
Install all instances in a single Availability Zone
Distribute instances to multiple Availability Zones behind a Load Balancer
Use only one instance as large as possible
questions.explanation: Distribute instances in multiple AZs behind an Elastic Load Balancer increases availability, because failure of an AZ does not bring down the entire application.
questions.hint: Think of how to prevent the failure of a single physical location of AWS drop all application.
optionRationales: Concentrating all instances into a single AZ means that the failure of this AZ (energy, network, etc.) would make the entire application unavailable — the opposite of high availability.
Correct. Distribute instances in multiple AZs behind an Elastic Load Balancer increases availability, because failure of an AZ does not bring down the entire application.
A single instance, even large, represents a single point of failure — if it fails or AZ has problems, the application is completely unavailable.
Disable the Auto Scaling reduces the ability of the application to automatically recover from instance failures and to deal with load peaks — impairs availability, does not help.

questions.text: What is the service of AWS is used to automatically distribute input traffic between multiple instances EC2?
options: Elastic Load Balancing (ELB)
Amazon SQS
AWS Direct Connect
Amazon CloudFront
questions.explanation: Elastic Load Balancing automatically distributes input traffic between multiple targets, such as instances EC2, improving availability and performance.
questions.hint: Think of the service whose main function is to receive incoming traffic and distribute it between several healthy destinations (targets).
optionRationales: Correct. Elastic Load Balancing automatically distributes input traffic between multiple targets, such as instances EC2, improving availability and performance.
The Amazon CloudFront It's a CDN distributing content (cache) from edge locations close to users — does not distribute requisition traffic between instances EC2 of an application.
The AWS Direct Connect establishes a dedicated network connection between a data center on-premises and the AWS — has no relation to traffic distribution between instances EC2.
The Amazon SQS is a message queue service to uncouple components — it does not distribute traffic HTTP/HTTPS users between instances.

questions.text: What storage class of the Amazon S3 offers the shortest access time (millimeters) for frequently accessed data?
options: S3 Standard
S3 Flexible Retrieval Glacier
S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval only for archiving
S3 Deep Archive Glacier
questions.explanation: The S3 Standard is designed for frequently accessed data, offering low latency and high transfer rate with millisecond access.
questions.hint: Think about the standard storage class of S3, designed for the most common use case: data that need to be available instantly, at any time.
optionRationales: The S3 Glacier Deep Archive is the lowest cost class and longest recovery time (up to 12 hours) — the opposite of the "less access time" requested for frequently accessed data.
Correct. S3 Standard is designed for frequently accessed data, offering low latency and high transfer rate with millisecond access.
The S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval is an archive class with recovery times ranging from minutes to hours — does not offer access in milliseconds as the S3 Standard.

Despite the name "Instant Retrieval", this class is still focused on archiving rarely accessed data (with recovery rates) — for frequent access in milliseconds without rates, the S3 Standard is the right option.

questions.text: What resource allows you to Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling add or remove instances automatically based on usage metrics, such as CPU?
options: IP Elastic
Investment Group
Launch Template only
Scaling Policy based on CloudWatch
questions.explanation: Scalability policies of the Auto Scaling, based on metrics of the CloudWatch (as a use of CPU), determine when to add or remove instances.
questions.hint: Think about the component of Auto Scaling which defines when to scale, based on continuously monitored metrics by another service.
optionRationales: A Launch Template defines how a new instance should be configured (AMI, type, etc.) when launched — but in itself does not decide when to add or remove instances based on metrics.
Correct. Scalability policies of the Auto Scaling, based on metrics of the CloudWatch (as a use of CPU), determine when to add or remove instances.
An Elastic IP is a static IPv4 address that can be associated with an instance — has no relation to automatic metric-based scaling decisions.
A Placement Group controls how instances are physically positioned in the infrastructure of the AWS (ex: for low latency) — does not control automatic meter-based scaling.

questions.text: What kind of instance EC2 is more suitable for work loads tolerant to interruptions, with the aim of significantly reducing costs?
options: On-Demand Entities
Entities reserved
Fora Dedicated Hosts
Courts Spot
questions.explanation: Courts Spot offer great discounts in relation to the On-Demand price, but can be interrupted by AWS, being ideal for interrupt-tolerant loads.
questions.hint: Think of the purchase model that offers the biggest discounts in exchange for the possibility of AWS interrupt the instance with little warning.
optionRationales: On-Demand cases have the highest price (no discount per commitment) — they are not the lowest cost option between alternatives for interrupting loads.

Reserved Entities offer discount in exchange for a commitment to use 1 or 3 years — suitable for stable and continuous loads, not for the scenario of reducing costs by taking advantage of interruption tolerance.
Correct. Spot offer great discounts in relation to the On-Demand price, but can be interrupted by AWS, being ideal for interrupt-tolerant loads.
Dedicated Hosts offer dedicated physical hardware, usually for licensing/conformity requirements — have higher cost than shared On-Demand instances, no lower.

questions.text: What service helps to identify idle or underutilized resources, such as instances EC2 low use, to reduce costs?
options: Amazon GuardDuty
Amazon Route 53
AWS Direct Connect
AWS Trusted Advisor
questions.explanation: The AWS Trusted Advisor analyzes the account and provides recommendations in categories such as cost optimization, identifying idle or underutilized resources.
questions.hint: Think of the service that analyzes the entire account and generates recommendations organized by categories, including a specific category of cost optimization.
optionRationales: Correct. AWS Trusted Advisor analyzes the account and provides recommendations in categories such as cost optimization, identifying idle or underutilized resources.
The Amazon GuardDuty is a security threat detection service — it identifies malicious/suspected activities, not idle resources for cost optimization.
The AWS Direct Connect establishes dedicated network connectivity between on-premises and AWS — has no relation to identifying idle or underutilized resources.
The Amazon Route 53 is a service of DNS — does not analyze the use of account resources nor generates cost recommendations.

questions.text: A company hired a consulting firm that owns its own account AWS. Consulting needs to access specific resources in the company's account, without user creation IAM The European Commission has been working on a proposal for a Council Directive on the approximation of the laws, regulations and administrative provisions of the Member States relating to the approximation of the laws of the Member States relating to the IAM allows this access between accounts safely?
options: Create a IAM Role in the company account that can be assumed by the users of the consulting account
Create a user IAM with password for each consultant in the company account
Making public the resources the consultancy needs to access
Share the company administrator's access keys with the consulting
questions.explanation: Roles between accounts (cross-account roles) allow identities from another account to temporarily assume a set of defined permissions, without creating permanent credentials — the recommended way of granting access between accounts.
questions.hint: Think about the resource of IAM which may be temporarily 'absorbed' by identities of another account.
optionRationales: Roles between accounts (cross-account roles) allow identities from another account to temporarily assume a set of defined permissions, without creating permanent credentials — the recommended way of granting access between accounts.
Sharing credentials is a serious security breach: keys are long-term, unauditable per person and give wide access without control.
Creating permanent users runs counter to the scenario requirement and increases the attack surface, requiring management of external credentials.
Exposing resources publicly to solve a problem of punctual access would open the data to the whole internet — the opposite of a secure solution.

questions.text: A company already has a corporate directory (such as Microsoft Active Directory) with all its employees. AWS using your existing corporate credentials, without needing to create a user IAM for each. As this objective is called and enabled in the AWS?
options: Creation of permanent key accesses for each employee
Sharing of root credentials between departments
Identity Federation, allowing authenticated users in the corporate directory to assume roles in AWS
User replication, automatically copying each AD account to the IAM
questions.explanation: The identity federation integrates an external identity provider (such as the AD) to AWS: the user authenticates in the corporate directory and receives temporary credentials via roles, eliminating the duplication of users in the IAM.
questions.hint: The key concept is to trust the authentication done by an external identity provider — what is called?
optionRationales: The identity federation integrates an external identity provider (such as the AD) to AWS: the user authenticates in the corporate directory and receives temporary credentials via roles, eliminating the duplication of users in the IAM.
There is no recommended mechanism for copying AD users to the IAM; the correct approach is to federate authentication, keeping the identities only in the directory of origin..
Root credentials should never be shared or used on a daily basis — this practice is unrelated to corporate directory integration.
Permanent access keys for each employee is precisely the scenario that the federation avoids, reducing risks and work of managing credentials.

questions.text: An organization owns 15 accounts AWS and wants its employees to log in once on a central portal and, from it, access all accounts and applications allowed, without managing users IAM separate in each account. AWS provides this unique login experience (SSO)?
options: AWS Secrets Manager
Amazon Cognito
AWS IAM Identity Center
AWS Certificate Manager
questions.explanation: The IAM Identity Center (successor to AWS SSO) centralizes staff access to multiple accounts AWS and applications in a single login portal, with centrally managed permissions.
questions.hint: Think of the service whose name unites 'identity' and 'centre': the central point of the workforce's login.
optionRationales: The IAM Identity Center (successor to AWS SSO) centralizes staff access to multiple accounts AWS and applications in a single login portal, with centrally managed permissions.
The Cognito manage user authentication FINAIS of web and mobile applications (clients), and not the access of employees to multiple accounts AWS.
The Secrets Manager store and rotate application secrets (signs, tokens), without any unique login portal function for accounts AWS.
The ACM issue and renew certificates TLS/SSL for cryptography in transit, does not manage logins or access to accounts.

questions.text: A startup is building a mobile app and needs a managed service to take care of the registration, login and password recovery of the end users of the app, with support for social login (Google, Facebook) and integration with protected APIs. AWS meets this need?
options: AWS IAM
AWS IAM Identity Center
Amazon Cognito
AWS Directory Service
questions.explanation: The Cognito provides registration, authentication and end-user management for web and mobile applications (user pools), including social login and token issuance for secure API access.
questions.hint: Differentiate who makes login: employees at AWS (IAM/Identity Center) versus clients of your application (which service?).
optionRationales: The Cognito provides registration, authentication and end-user management for web and mobile applications (user pools), including social login and token issuance for secure API access.
The IAM manage identities and permissions to access resources from AWS (administrators, developers, services), and no end-customer accounts of an application.
The Identity Center centralizes labour force access to accounts AWS and corporate applications, not the login of millions of end users of an app.
Directory Service provides Active Directory managed for Windows corporate scenarios, not authentication of mobile app clients with social login.

questions.text: In a multi-account architecture with AWS Organizations, the governance team has applied a policy that prevents all accounts of the organizational unit 'Development' from excluding tracks from CloudTrail, regardless of permissions IAM What kind of policy does this control?
options: Network ACL of VPC
Service Control Policy (SCP)
Bucket policy of S3
Identity-based policy of the IAM
questions.explanation: SCPs are applied at the level of the organization (root, OOs or accounts) and define the maximum limit of permissions: actions denied by the SCP are blocked even for administrators with full access via IAM.
questions.hint: It is the 'guarda-chuva' policy of the Organizations that even the account administrator can't get around.
optionRationales: SCPs are applied at the level of the organization (root, OOs or accounts) and define the maximum limit of permissions: actions denied by the SCP are blocked even for administrators with full access via IAM.
Policies IAM act within a single account and can be changed by local administrators — do not impose an inviolable organizational limit on all accounts.
Bucket police control access to a specific Bucket S3, without the ability to restrict actions on the CloudTrail in multiple accounts.
NACLs filter network traffic in sub-networks and are not related to API or account governance.

questions.text: Courts EC2 in private sub-networks need to access the Amazon S3 and the DynamoDB without the traffic passing through the public internet and without using NAT Gateway. What's the use of VPC creates this private path for these two services, without additional cost?
options: Internet Gateway
Gateway VPC Endpoint
Second NAT Gateway redundant
VPC Peering
questions.explanation: Gateway Endpoints are offered specifically for S3 and DynamoDB: add a private route in the route table of the VPC, allowing access to these services through the internal network of the AWS, without internet, without NAT and no cost.
questions.hint: There are two services AWS which have gained a special type of 'gateway' endpoint, free, configured in the route table.
optionRationales: Gateway Endpoints are offered specifically for S3 and DynamoDB: add a private route in the route table of the VPC, allowing access to these services through the internal network of the AWS, without internet, without NAT and no cost.
The Internet Gateway provides just access to the public internet — the opposite of the private path desired for private sub-networks.
The peering connects two VPCs to each other, but does not create a private path between a VPC and regional services such as S3 and DynamoDB.
The NAT Gateway would route traffic to the public internet at a cost per hour and per GB — the scenario asks exactly to eliminate this dependence.

questions.text: A software company wants to expose its service hosted at AWS for customers to consume privately, directly from their VPCs, without the traffic crossing the public internet and without creating peering between networks. AWS enables this private exposure of services between VPCs?
options: Amazon CloudFront with geographical restriction
Internet Gateway with restrictive rules Security Group
AWS Direct Connect among the customers' VPCs
AWS PrivateLink VPC Endpoints)
questions.explanation: PrivateLink allows you to post a service behind a Network Load Balancer and consume it from other VPCs by means of endpoints interface with private IPs, keeping all traffic within the network of AWS no peering or internet.
questions.hint: Think of the 'private link' that turns your service into an endpoint within the VPC of the customer.
optionRationales: PrivateLink allows you to post a service behind a Network Load Balancer and consume it from other VPCs by means of endpoints interface with private IPs, keeping all traffic within the network of AWS no peering or internet.
Even with restrictive rules, traffic would cross the public internet — what the scenario wants to avoid altogether.
The Direct Connect link data centers on-premises to AWS; is not the mechanism for private consumption of services between cloud VPCs.
The CloudFront content delivery on the edge of the public internet; geographical restrictions do not make the private path within the AWS.

questions.text: An architect created a new Security Group in one VPC and attached it to a court EC2 without adding any rules. What is the standard behavior of this Security Group newly created?
options: All incoming traffic is denied and all outgoing traffic is allowed
All inbound and outbound traffic allowed
Only traffic SSH (door 22) is allowed at the entrance
All incoming and outgoing traffic is denied
questions.explanation: By default, a Security Group new has no entry rules (logo, implicitly denies all entry traffic) and has a rule releasing all exit traffic.
questions.hint: Remember the standard posture: closed doors for those who arrive, free passage for those who leave.
optionRationales: By default, a Security Group new has no entry rules (logo, implicitly denies all entry traffic) and has a rule releasing all exit traffic.
If everything was allowed by default, newly created instances would be exposed; the entry starts completely blocked until Allow rules are added.
The output is released by default to allow the instance to start connections (updates, APIs); only the input starts blocked.
No input door is automatically released — not even SSH; the administrator needs to explicitly create each entry rule.

questions.text: Administrators need access via SSH cases EC2 which are in private sub-networks, without exposing these instances directly to the internet. A traditional practice is to place a reinforced intermediate instance in a public sub-network, which serves as the only entry point to reach private instances. As this component is called?
options: Internet Gateway
Bastion host)
NAT Gateway
Elastic Load Balancer
questions.explanation: The bastion host is a hardened instance in the public sub-network that concentrates and controls administrative access (SSH/RDP) to private sub-networks, reducing the area exposed to the internet.
questions.hint: The name comes from the fortifications: the reinforced tower where everyone must pass to enter the castle.
optionRationales: The bastion host is a hardened instance in the public sub-network that concentrates and controls administrative access (SSH/RDP) to private sub-networks, reducing the area exposed to the internet.
The NAT Gateway allows private bodies INICIEM exit connections to the internet; it does not accept administrative entry connections as SSH.
The Internet Gateway is the routing component that connects the VPC internet — is not a controlled administrative access body.
The ELB distributes application traffic between instances, not administrative sessions SSH for private server management.

questions.text: Courts EC2 in a private sub-network need to download internet security updates, but can not, under any circumstances, receive connections started from outside. Which component meets this exit requirement without allowing entry into the network.?
options: Internet Gateway directly attached to the private sub-network with public IPs in the fora
VPC Peering with a VPC public
AWS WAF applied to bodies
NAT Gateway in a public sub-network, referenced in the route table of the private sub-network
questions.explanation: The NAT Gateway allows private instances to start output connections to the internet (such as downloading patches) while blocking externally initiated connections, preserving sub-network isolation.
questions.hint: Think of the component that works as 'one-handed swivel door': inside you can exit, outside you can't enter.
optionRationales: The NAT Gateway allows private instances to start output connections to the internet (such as downloading patches) while blocking externally initiated connections, preserving sub-network isolation.
Assign public IPs and route to Internet Gateway would make the instances reachable from the internet — decharacterizing the private subnet and violating the requirement.
Peering connects VPCs to each other; it does not provide translation of addresses to controlled output to the internet.
The WAF filter web requests that reach CloudFront, ALB or API Gateway; does not provide way out to the internet from private sub-networks.

questions.text: A company needs to quickly connect its office to its VPC the AWS with encrypted traffic, using the internet as a means of transport and IPsec tunnels, without waiting for the installation of physical circuits. What hybrid connectivity solution meets this scenario?
options: AWS Direct Connect
VPC Peering
AWS Site-to-Site VPN
Amazon Route 53
questions.explanation: The Site-to-Site VPN establishes encrypted IPsec tunnels between the company's local gateway and the VPC through the internet, it can be provided in hours — ideal when speed and encryption are the priorities.
questions.hint: The combination 'internet + IPsec tunnel + activation speed' describes the classic encrypted connectivity option.
optionRationales: The Site-to-Site VPN establishes encrypted IPsec tunnels between the company's local gateway and the VPC through the internet, it can be provided in hours — ideal when speed and encryption are the priorities.
The Direct Connect uses dedicated physical circuits that take weeks to provide; it offers consistent band, but does not meet the requirement of fast deployment via internet.
The peering connects two VPCs inside the AWS, and not an on-premises office to a VPC.
The Route 53 solve names DNS; does not establish encrypted network tunnels between environments.

questions.text: No. AWS KMS, a team evaluates using keys managed by AWS or customer-managed keys (customer managed keys). What is the main advantage of choosing a customer-managed key?
options: They are totally free, unlike keys managed by AWS
They're the only ones who can encrypt data on S3
Eliminate the need for permissions IAM for key use
Total control over key policy, rotation, enable/disable and who can use it
questions.explanation: Client-managed keys give complete administrative control: defining key policies, managing rotation, disabling and scheduled exclusion — necessary for rigid governance and audit requirements.
questions.hint: The central difference is who runs the key: think about politics, rotation and life cycle under your command.
optionRationales: Client-managed keys give complete administrative control: defining key policies, managing rotation, disabling and scheduled exclusion — necessary for rigid governance and audit requirements.
It's the opposite: customer-managed keys have monthly cost per key, while those managed by AWS do not generate direct storage charge.
The S3 can use both keys managed by AWS the customer (and SSE-S3); cryptography is not exclusive to a type of key.
The use of any key KMS remains subject to permissions (key policies and IAM); access control is never eliminated.

questions.text: By creating a volume EBS for a new instance EC2, the architect has marked the encryption option. What protections this automatically activates choice?
options: Only Internet traffic that reaches the instance
Only manual backups, requiring recryption of automatic snapshots
Only files manually marked as sensitive within the operating system
The data at rest in the volume, the snapshots created from it and the data in transit between the volume and the instance are encrypted
questions.explanation: The cryptography of the EBS protects the data recorded in the volume, is inherited by snapshots (and their restored volumes) and also covers the traffic between the instance and the volume — all in a transparent way via KMS.
questions.hint: The protection follows the given along the block path: on the disk, on the copies (snapshots) and on the path to the instance.
optionRationales: The cryptography of the EBS protects the data recorded in the volume, is inherited by snapshots (and their restored volumes) and also covers the traffic between the instance and the volume — all in a transparent way via KMS.
The cryptography of the EBS acts at block level, especially volume, without depending on file marking on operating system.
Internet traffic is protected by TLS in the application layer; the encryption of the EBS it deals with storage and the way between instance and volume.
Snapshots of encrypted volumes are automatically encrypted without any manual recryption step.

questions.text: A team wants to encrypt objects in S3 and requires that each use of the encryption key be recorded for audit, with control over the policy and key rotation. SSE-S3 and SSE-KMS, which option meets these requirements and why?
options: Neither; cryptography in S3 requires third-party software
SSE-S3, because it's the only option that encrypts at rest
SSE-KMS, because you use keys from the AWS KMS with controllable policies and records each key use in CloudTrail
SSE-S3, because it allows you to define custom key policies by bucket
questions.explanation: No. SSE-KMS, the encryption uses keys from the KMS: the client controls policies and rotation (in keys managed by him) and all use of the key is auditable in the CloudTrail — resources that SSE-S3 does not offer.
questions.hint: Key use audit + policy control point to integration with key management service.
optionRationales: No. SSE-KMS, the encryption uses keys from the KMS: the client controls policies and rotation (in keys managed by him) and all use of the key is auditable in the CloudTrail — resources that SSE-S3 does not offer.
No. SSE-S3, the keys are fully managed by the S3, without configurable key policies or individualised key-use trail.
Both options encrypt the objects at rest; the difference is in key control and auditability, not in the existence of encryption.
The S3 offers native server side encryption (SSE-S3, SSE-KMS), without the need for external solutions.

questions.text: An architect needs to ensure that a new database Amazon RDS store all encrypted data at rest, including automatic backups and snapshots. What is the correct way to enable this protection?
options: Install an encryption agent within the operating system of RDS
Use only certificates SSL in the connections with the bank
Enable encryption option at any time in the settings of the instance running
Enable encryption with KMS at the time of the creation of the instance RDS
questions.explanation: Cryptography at rest of RDS is defined in the instance creation: once enabled, it covers data, automatic backups, snapshots and replicas — it is not possible simply to 'connect' then in the existing instance.
questions.hint: For the RDS, the decision to encrypt the storage needs to be made at a specific time of the life cycle.
optionRationales: Cryptography at rest of RDS is defined in the instance creation: once enabled, it covers data, automatic backups, snapshots and replicas — it is not possible simply to 'connect' then in the existing instance.
There is no button to encrypt an instance RDS already existing; the path involves creating a snapshot, copying it with encryption and restoring a new instance.
The RDS is managed and does not give access to the operating system; rest encryption is a resource of the integrated platform to KMS.
SSL/TLS protects the data in transit between the application and the bank, but does not encrypt storage, backups and snapshots at rest.

questions.text: A web application behind a Application Load Balancer needs to meet users exclusively via HTTPS. The team wants to get the certificate TLS without cost and with automatic renewal, integrated directly into the balancer. Which service solves this need?
options: AWS Certificate Manager (ACM)
AWS KMS
Amazon GuardDuty
AWS Secrets Manager
questions.explanation: The ACM issue certificates TLS free public with automatic renewal and native integration with ALB, CloudFront and API Gateway, enabling HTTPS without manual management of certificates.
questions.hint: HTTPS in the balancer asks for a certificate: what service the AWS emits and renews them for free?
optionRationales: The ACM issue certificates TLS free public with automatic renewal and native integration with ALB, CloudFront and API Gateway, enabling HTTPS without manual management of certificates.
The KMS manage encryption keys for data, but do not issue or renew certificates TLS for web endpoints.
The Secrets Manager keep credentials and application secrets; is not a certificate issuing authority TLS.
The GuardDuty detects suspicious threats and activities in the account, unrelated to certificates or cryptography in transit.

questions.text: The website of a virtual store, served by a Application Load Balancer, you are receiving malicious requests with patterns of injection of SQL and cross-site scripting (XSS). The architect wants to filter these requests in the application layer before they reach the servers. What service should be associated with ALB?
options: AWS WAF
Amazon Macie
AWS Firewall Manager
Network ACL
questions.explanation: The AWS WAF is the firewall of web applications of AWS: associated with ALB (or CloudFront/API Gateway), inspect requests HTTP/HTTPS and blocks malicious patterns like SQL injection e XSS by means of managed or custom rules.
questions.hint: Attacks that live DENTRO of the request HTTP require a firewall that understands the application layer.
optionRationales: The AWS WAF is the firewall of web applications of AWS: associated with ALB (or CloudFront/API Gateway), inspect requests HTTP/HTTPS and blocks malicious patterns like SQL injection e XSS by means of managed or custom rules.
NACLs filter by IP, port and protocol at the sub-network level; cannot inspect the contents of requests HTTP in search of attack patterns.
The Macie discover sensitive data stored in S3; does not filter real-time web traffic.
The Firewall Manager centrally administers rules of WAF and other protections in various accounts, but who inspects and blocks requests is the WAF.

questions.text: An architect explained to the board that all the charges on AWS already have an automatic and free protection against the most common DDoS attacks of network and transport (layers 3 and 4), no need for configuration. Which service he refers to?
options: AWS Shield Standard
AWS WAF
Amazon Inspector
AWS Shield Advanced
questions.explanation: The Shield Standard is automatically and cost-free enabled for all customers AWS, Mitigating the most common volumetric DDoS attacks on network and transport layers.
questions.hint: It's the basic shield that every client AWS already owns without asking or paying.
optionRationales: The Shield Standard is automatically and cost-free enabled for all customers AWS, Mitigating the most common volumetric DDoS attacks on network and transport layers.
The Shield Advanced is the paid level, with advanced detection, response team and financial protection — not the free auto protection cited.
The WAF requires rules configuration and acts in the application layer (7), not being the automatic layer protection 3 and 4.
The Inspector sweep workloads in search of software vulnerabilities; does not mitigate DDoS attacks.

questions.text: A payment platform considers its site a high-risk target for sophisticated DDoS attacks. In addition to basic protection, the company wants access to 24/7 to a specialized response team of the AWS and protection against extra scalability costs generated during attacks. Which service should be hired?
options: AWS Shield Advanced
AWS Configure
AWS Shield Standard
Amazon GuardDuty
questions.explanation: The Shield Advanced adds advanced detection and mitigation, access to Shield Response Team (SRT) 24/7 and financial protection against cost peaks caused by DDoS attacks — the appropriate level for high-risk targets.
questions.hint: Dedicated response team + bill protection during attacks = premium shield level.
optionRationales: The Shield Advanced adds advanced detection and mitigation, access to Shield Response Team (SRT) 24/7 and financial protection against cost peaks caused by DDoS attacks — the appropriate level for high-risk targets.
The Shield Standard automatically protects against common attacks, but does not include dedicated response team or financial safeguards.
The GuardDuty is threat detection based on log analysis — does not mitigate DDoS or offers attack response team.
Config audits resource settings against compliance rules, without any role in DDoS defense.

questions.text: An application needs to store non-sensitive configuration values (such as internal API URLs and functionality flags) centrally and hierarchically, with the option of encrypting the few confidential values, all at no additional cost for standard parameters. What service meets this usage case?
options: AWS KMS
AWS Secrets Manager
Amazon S3 with public bucket
AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store
questions.explanation: The Parameter Store store hierarchical configuration parameters, with String and SecureString types (crypted via KMS), and the default level is free — ideal for application settings.
questions.hint: For common settings (and some secrets), there is the free 'parameter cabinet' of Systems Manager.
optionRationales: The Parameter Store store hierarchical configuration parameters, with String and SecureString types (crypted via KMS), and the default level is free — ideal for application settings.
The Secrets Manager is paid by secret and specialized in credentials with automatic rotation; for non-sensitive settings it would be unnecessary cost.
Exposing settings in public bucket is unsafe and does not offer the integration of typed and hierarchical parameters of configuration tools.
The KMS manages encryption keys, but is not a repository of application configuration parameters.

questions.text: The security team wants a service that continuously monitors the account AWS in search of suspicious activities — as calls from API unusual, instances communicating with known malicious addresses and attempts to compromise credentials — automatically analyzing sources such as CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs and Logs DNS. Which service performs this intelligent threat detection?
options: AWS CloudTrail
Amazon GuardDuty
Amazon CloudWatch
AWS WAF
questions.explanation: The GuardDuty is the threat detection service of the AWS: continuously analyzes CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs and Logs DNS with machine learning and threat intelligence, generating findings about malicious activities without installing agents.
questions.hint: Think of the guard who watches the log of the account day and night looking for malicious behavior.
optionRationales: The GuardDuty is the threat detection service of the AWS: continuously analyzes CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs and Logs DNS with machine learning and threat intelligence, generating findings about malicious activities without installing agents.
The CloudTrail records calls from API (the raw material), but does not analyze the records in search of threats — this intelligence is the GuardDuty.
The WAF filters malicious web requests in specific applications, without monitoring the general behavior of the account and credentials.
The CloudWatch metric collection and operational logs, but has no threat intelligence to identify malicious activities automatically.

questions.text: When reviewing a policy IAM in JSON, a beginner found the elements 'Effect', 'Action' and 'Resource'. What each of these elements defines in a policy statement?
options: The three elements are only descriptive comments without practical effect
Effect defines encryption; Action defines allowed time; Resource defines instance type
Effect defines the cost of the operation; Action defines the user; Resource defines the Region
Effect defines whether the statement allows or denies (Allow/Deny); Action defines which transactions are affected; Resource defines which resources the statement applies to
questions.explanation: These are the central elements of a declaration IAM: the effect (allow or deny), the actions of API covered (ex: s3:GetObject) and target resources identified by ARN.
questions.hint: Read the statement as a phrase: '[allow/deny] [what operations] [about what]'.
optionRationales: These are the central elements of a declaration IAM: the effect (allow or deny), the actions of API covered (ex: s3:GetObject) and target resources identified by ARN.

Policies IAM they do not deal with costs; the user is defined outside of the policy (or in the main element in resource policies) and the Region is part of the ARN of the resource, not of an own element called Resource with that role.
None of these meanings correspond to the elements: encryption and timetables would be treated via Condition, and type of instance is not the role of the Resource element.
The three elements are the functional core of the policy — without them the declaration does not define any permission.

questions.text: When designing the permissions of a new application, the architect defined that each component will receive only the minimum permissions strictly necessary for its function — for example, the upload function can only record in the specific prefix of the bucket, nothing more.?
options: High availability
Horizontal scalability
Principle of minor privilege
Shared responsibility
questions.explanation: The lowest privilege is to grant only the minimum permissions required for each task, reducing the potential impact of compromised credentials or errors — a pillar of good practice in the IAM.
questions.hint: 'Only what is needed, and nothing more' — what is the classic name of this principle?
optionRationales: The lowest privilege is to grant only the minimum permissions required for each task, reducing the potential impact of compromised credentials or errors — a pillar of good practice in the IAM.
The shared responsibility model divides duties between AWS and customer; does not deal with granularity of permissions granted to components.
High availability is an attribute of resilience of architecture, not related to the dimensioning of permissions.
Horizontal scalability tries to add instances to meet demand — a concept of capacity, not access security.

questions.text: Right after you create an account AWS for a new project, the architect applied two immediate measures: activated the multifactor authentication in the root user and kept its credentials for use only in emergencies, creating separate identities for daily work. Why these measures are considered essential?
options: Because MFA in the root accelerates the technical support of AWS
Because the root has unlimited and unrestricted power over the account, and its commitment would give complete control to an attacker
Because root is the only identity that can create instances EC2
Because without MFA in root the account cannot access paid services
questions.explanation: Root user cannot be limited by policies IAM and executes exclusive critical actions; protect it with MFA and avoiding it day by day is the first safety recommendation of any account AWS.
questions.hint: Think about what would happen if someone stole the most powerful (and limitless) identity from the account.
optionRationales: Root user cannot be limited by policies IAM and executes exclusive critical actions; protect it with MFA and avoiding it day by day is the first safety recommendation of any account AWS.
Any user or role IAM with appropriate permissions can create instances; resource operations do not require root.
The MFA is a authentication protection and has no relation to priority or speed of support service.
The account normally works without MFA in root — the measure is a good practice of protection, not a functional requirement of billing.

questions.text: A company wants to ensure that no bucket S3 the account can be publicly exposed, even if a developer mistakenly configures a permissive pocket policy or public ACLs. S3 provides this security lock at the account level?
options: Life cycle policies in the pocket
Version enabled on all the bucks
S3 Transfer Acceleration
S3 Block Public Access enabled at account level
questions.explanation: Block Public Access overlaps with public policies and ACLs: enabled in the account, blocks any public access to all bucks, functioning as a safety net against accidental exposures.
questions.hint: There is a master switch of the S3 who vetoes public access even when someone tries to grant it.
optionRationales: Block Public Access overlaps with public policies and ACLs: enabled in the account, blocks any public access to all bucks, functioning as a safety net against accidental exposures.
Versioning protects against accidental exclusions and overwrites of objects, but does not prevent public access configured by mistake.
Transfer Acceleration accelerates long-distance uploads — has no public access control function.
Life cycle policies automate class transitions of storage and object expiration, unrelated to public exposure.

questions.text: During a secure architecture review, an architect recommended encrypting the data 'in transit' and 'in rest'. What each of these terms means?
options: In transit: temporary cached data; in rest: data with completed backup
In transit: mobile application data; in rest: web application data
In transit: data moving through the network between systems (protected by TLS); at rest: data stored on disks, banks or buckets (protected by storage encryption))
In transit: data in different regions; in rest: data in the same region
questions.explanation: That's the fundamental distinction: TLS/SSL protects communication while the data travels, and mechanisms like KMS, EBS Encryption and SSE protect the data wherever they are recorded.
questions.hint: Think of the dice as a traveler: a protection for the road, another for the house where he sleeps.
optionRationales: That's the fundamental distinction: TLS/SSL protects communication while the data travels, and mechanisms like KMS, EBS Encryption and SSE protect the data wherever they are recorded.
The terms do not refer to the geographical location of the data, but to their state: moving through the network or stored.
The type of application is irrelevant to the definition; any data may be in transit or at rest at different times.
Cache and backup are specific storage cases; the real distinction is between network communication and persistence in storage media.

questions.text: An architect explained to the team the difference between implementing an application in multiple Availability Zones (Multi-AZ) and in multiple Regions (Multi-Region). What statement correctly describes the type of failure that each approach protects?
options: Multi-AZ and Multi-Region offer exactly the same protection, changing only the cost
Multi-Region is mandatory for any application in production in AWS
Multi-AZ protects against the failure of a data center or zone within the Region; Multi-Region protects against the unavailability of an entire Region
Multi-AZ protects against programming errors in the application
questions.explanation: AZs isolate local infrastructure failures (energy, network, disaster in a data center), while deployment in multiple regions protects against events affecting a whole geographical area, in addition to meeting latency and compliance requirements.
questions.hint: Ask yourself: what falls into each scenario — a building, or an entire geographical area?
optionRationales: AZs isolate local infrastructure failures (energy, network, disaster in a data center), while deployment in multiple regions protects against events affecting a whole geographical area, in addition to meeting latency and compliance requirements.
The protections are distinct: Multi-AZ does not cover the failure of an entire Region, and Multi-Region adds geographic resilience with greater complexity and cost.
Infrastructure redundancy does not fix bugs: a code error also replicates in all areas where the application runs.
Multi-Region is an architecture decision based on requirements of RTO/RPO, compliance and criticality — most applications achieve high availability suitable with Multi-AZ.

questions.text: A company stores critical documents in a pocket S3 in the region of São Paulo and, by strategy of disaster recovery, wants to automatically keep a copy of each new object in a pocket in the region of North Virginia. S3 meets this requirement?
options: S3 Transfer Acceleration
S3 Intelligent-Tiering
Replication between regions (Cross-Region Replication) - CRR)
Life cycle policy (Lifecycle Policy))
questions.explanation: A CRR automatically replicates the objects of a original bucket to a bucket in another region, keeping a geographically distant copy for disaster recovery and compliance.
questions.hint: The name of the resource says exactly what it does: replicate 'crossing' Regions.
optionRationales: A CRR automatically replicates the objects of a original bucket to a bucket in another region, keeping a geographically distant copy for disaster recovery and compliance.
Transfer Acceleration speeds up remote client uploads using Edge Locations, but does not copy objects automatically between different region pocketes.
Life cycle policies move objects between storage classes or expire over time — do not replicate them to another region.
Intelligent-Tiering optimizes costs by moving objects between access layers within the same pocket, without creating copies in other regions.

questions.text: An analyst mistakenly erased an important report from a pocket S3, and the team took days to rebuild it. So that exclusions and accidental overwrites can be undone in the future, recovering the previous state of any object, which feature of the bucket should be enabled?
options: Storage class S3 Glacier
Replication between regions (CRR)
Version S3 (Versioning)
S3 Block Public Access
questions.explanation: With the versioning, the S3 preserves all versions of each object: overwritten create new versions and exclusions just insert a removable marker, allowing to restore any previous state.
questions.hint: Think of the resource that transforms each change into another saved 'version' instead of definitive replacement.
optionRationales: With the versioning, the S3 preserves all versions of each object: overwritten create new versions and exclusions just insert a removable marker, allowing to restore any previous state.
The replication copies objects to another Region, but by default can propagate changes; it was not designed as a mechanism to undo accidental exclusions in the original bucket.
Block Public Access prevents public exposure of objects — access protection, not version recovery.
Glacier is a low-cost archiving class; moving objects there does not create version history or protect against exclusion.

questions.text: In one Auto Scaling Group, one of the bodies EC2 has stopped responding to integrity checks. Auto Scaling automatically does in this situation?
options: Restarts the operating system of the instance indefinitely until it responds
Reduces the group's desired ability to ignore the instance with problem
Send an email to the administrator and wait for manual correction
Closes the unhealthy instance and launches a new substitute to maintain the desired capacity
questions.explanation: One of the central functions of the Auto Scaling is the self-recovery: failed instances in health check are closed and replaced automatically, maintaining the desired number of healthy instances without human intervention.
questions.hint: The group has a target number of healthy instances — what it does with those who get sick?
optionRationales: One of the central functions of the Auto Scaling is the self-recovery: failed instances in health check are closed and replaced automatically, maintaining the desired number of healthy instances without human intervention.
The Auto Scaling acts alone in replacement; notifications can be configured, but recovery does not depend on manual action.
The desired capacity remains the same — the goal is to restore the lost instance, not operate with fewer servers.
The standard behavior is to replace the defective instance with a new one, and not insist on rebooting the same machine.

questions.text: A web application runs in four instances EC2 behind a Application Load Balancer with health checks configured. If one of the instances starts to fail in integrity checks, how the balancer reacts?
options: Migrate the instance disk to a new instance automatically
Turn off the entire balancer until all instances are healthy
Stop sending new requests to the instance with failure and distribute traffic only between healthy instances
Continues to send traffic equally to all instances, whether healthy or not
questions.explanation: The ELB monitors the integrity of the targets and routes traffic only to those who pass the health check, automatically isolating faulty instances from the users' route.
questions.hint: Balancer works as an informed porter: to which list of servers it directs visitors?
optionRationales: The ELB monitors the integrity of the targets and routes traffic only to those who pass the health check, automatically isolating faulty instances from the users' route.
Balancer continues to operate normally with healthy targets — interrupting all service because of an instance would nullify the purpose of redundancy.
Ignoring the state of integrity would send users to a broken server — exactly what health checks exist to avoid.
The ELB does not manage disks or replace instances; it just decides where to route traffic (replacement is role of Auto Scaling).

questions.text: A company keeps its main site on servers in AWS and a static contingency page hosted in the S3. She wants you to DNS direct users automatically to the contingency page only when the main site is unavailable. What router policy does the Route 53 implements this behavior?
options: Simple routing with multiple IP addresses
Weight-weighted rotation 50/50
Failover routing with health checks at the primary endpoint
Geolocation rotation
questions.explanation: The policy of failure of the Route 53 monitors the primary endpoint via health checks and, when it fails, responds with the secondary record (the contingency page), reversing when the primary recovers.
questions.hint: Primary while healthy, secondary when failing: what's the name of this 'Plan B' policy'?
optionRationales: The policy of failure of the Route 53 monitors the primary endpoint via health checks and, when it fails, responds with the secondary record (the contingency page), reversing when the primary recovers.
Equal weights would send half of the users to contingency all the time, even with the main healthy site — not the desired behavior.
Geolocation chooses the destination by the user's geographical origin, and not by the availability of the main site.
Simple routing does not use health checks — users could continue to receive the server IP out of the air.

questions.text: During the disaster recovery planning, the board defined that the sales system should operate again at most 2 which disaster recovery metric this requirement corresponds to?
options: RTO (Recovery Time Objective: the maximum acceptable time to restore service after interruption
TTL (Time to Live) of records DNS
SLA (Service Level Agreement) AWS
RPO (Recovery Point Objective: the maximum acceptable loss of data measured in time
questions.explanation: The RTO defines how long the business tolerates running out of the system — 'returning to operation in 2 hours' is exactly a recovery time goal.
questions.hint: The metric question is: 'how much TEMPO Can we stay out of the air?' — what acronym answers that?
optionRationales: The RTO defines how long the business tolerates running out of the system — 'returning to operation in 2 hours' is exactly a recovery time goal.
The RPO deals with how many data (in time) can be lost — for example, 'lose at most 15 minutes of transactions' — and not the deadline for the service to return.
The SLA is the contractual commitment of availability of a provider, and not the internal metric of recovery time defined by the business.
The TTL defines how long solvers cache a record DNS — a technical parameter, not a disaster recovery metric.

questions.text: In the disaster recovery plan, the same board defined that, in case of catastrophic failure, the company agrees to lose as much as possible the last 15 minutes of recorded data. Which metric this limit corresponds to, and what it directly influences the architecture?
options: RPO (Recovery Point Objective), which determines the minimum frequency of backups or replication of data
Maximum throughput of the database in production
Time of spread of the DNS after failover
RTO (Recovery Time Objective), which determines the size of contingency instances
questions.explanation: The RPO defines the maximum acceptable data loss window; a RPO of 15 minutes requires backups or replication at least at each 15 minutes (or continuous replication) to be completed.
questions.hint: The metric question is, 'how many DADOS (measured in time) can we lose?' — and the answer dictates the pace of backups.
optionRationales: The RPO defines the maximum acceptable data loss window; a RPO of 15 minutes requires backups or replication at least at each 15 minutes (or continuous replication) to be completed.
The RTO it deals with the time to restore the service, not the data loss window; moreover, it influences the standby strategy, not directly the size of the instances.
Throughput is an operational performance metric, unrelated to the data loss limit in disasters.
The spread of DNS affects the time of redirection of users (linked to the RTO), and not the amount of data lost.

questions.text: A company with a limited budget needs a disaster recovery strategy for an internal system that tolerates being out of the air for several hours. The choice was to store regular backups in another region and, only in case of disaster, provide the infrastructure and restore the data. As this strategy is called?
options: Warm standby
Active-active multi-site
Pilot light
Backup & Restore
questions.explanation: Backup & Restore is the most economical DR strategy: nothing is running in the Recovery Region — only stored backups — in exchange for the largest RTO among the strategies, because everything needs to be provided and restored after the disaster.
questions.hint: It's the copy safe strategy: nothing connected in the other region, only backups waiting for the worst day.
optionRationales: Backup & Restore is the most economical DR strategy: nothing is running in the Recovery Region — only stored backups — in exchange for the largest RTO among the strategies, because everything needs to be provided and restored after the disaster.
The asset-active keeps the system running in full capacity in multiple regions simultaneously — the most expensive strategy, with RTO near zero, the opposite of the scenario.
Warm standby keeps a reduced version of the environment running in the Recovery Region, with a continuous cost higher than just saving backups.
The pilot light keeps the essential components (like the replicated bank) always active in the other region; the scenario describes only stored backups, with nothing running.

questions.text: In a disaster recovery strategy, a company keeps in the secondary region only the minimum core always active — the continuously replicated database — while application servers are turned off (only configured as images and templates), ready to be connected and scaled quickly in case of disaster.?
options: Active-active multi-site
Backup & Restore
Warm standby
Pilot light
questions.explanation: In the pilot light, the 'pilot call' (critical components such as replicated data) remains always lit in the recovery region, and the rest of the infrastructure is provided only when necessary — balancing cost and speed of recovery.
questions.hint: Think of the pilot flame of a heater: small, always lit, ready to light the full fire quickly.
optionRationales: In the pilot light, the 'pilot call' (critical components such as replicated data) remains always lit in the recovery region, and the rest of the infrastructure is provided only when necessary — balancing cost and speed of recovery.
In Backup & Restore nothing is running in the Secondary Region — nor the replicated bank; all part of the backups, with RTO Well, it's much bigger..
In warm standby, a reduced functional version of the application INTEIRA (including servers) is always running — more than just the driver light data core.
In the asset-active, both regions attend production in total capacity simultaneously — the most expensive and complete level, far from the scenario described.

questions.text: A digital bank requires RTO and RPO close to zero for your transaction system: no noticeable interruption and no data loss, even in the failure of an entire region. The high cost has been approved. What disaster recovery strategy meets this extreme requirement?
options: Multi-site active, with the application running in total capacity in multiple regions simultaneously
Pilot light with provision on demand
Backup & Restore with backups every hour
Warm standby with reduced capacity
questions.explanation: In the active-activity, all regions respond to production traffic at the same time with data replicated continuously; the failure of one region only redistributed users to the others, virtually without interruption or loss.
questions.hint: To RTO ~zero can't be 'click after': everything needs to be already attending production everywhere.
optionRationales: In the active-activity, all regions respond to production traffic at the same time with data replicated continuously; the failure of one region only redistributed users to the others, virtually without interruption or loss.
This strategy involves hours of RTO (provide and restore everything) and up to an hour of data loss — incompatible with near zero requirements.
The pilot light still requires to connect and scale the application infrastructure after the disaster, resulting in RTO of tens of minutes or more.
Warm standby needs to scale the reduced capacity to the production port during the disaster, generating a degradation window — small but not zero.

questions.text: In an order architecture, the payment service sends tasks directly to the tax billing service for synchronous calls. When the issue is out of the air, payments also fail. What architectural change makes the flow resilient to emission service failures?
options: Make the payment service try the synchronous call infinitely until it succeeds
Unify the two services into a single monolithic application
Increase the size of the issue service instance
Place a row of the Amazon SQS between the services, so that the requests are stored in a durable way until the issue process them
questions.explanation: The decoupling via SQS absorbs unavailability of the consumer: the payment service publishes in the queue and continues to work, and the issue processes the accumulated messages when it recovers — without loss of orders.
questions.hint: The classic solution for 'one falls and takes the other together' is to put a durable shock absorber between them.
optionRationales: The decoupling via SQS absorbs unavailability of the consumer: the payment service publishes in the queue and continues to work, and the issue processes the accumulated messages when it recovers — without loss of orders.
More capacity does not solve the fragility of synchronous coupling: any emission drop would continue to bring down payments.
Infinite synchronous retentivities secure resources, degrade payment and can overload the service in recovery even more.
Founding the services would increase the coupling: a failure anywhere would knock down the whole set.

questions.text: A row of the Amazon SQS process orders, but some malformed messages repeatedly fail in processing and return to the row in infinite loop, wasting resources. SQS handles these problematic messages correctly?
options: Long polling, filtering faulty messages
Dead-letter tail (DLQ): after a set number of attempts, the message is moved to a separate row for analysis
Visibility Timeout greater, which automatically discards the message
Row FIFO, who rejects malformed messages at the entrance
questions.explanation: A DLQ receives messages that have exceeded the maximum number of receipts without successful processing, removing them from the main cycle and preserving them for research and correction.
questions.hint: Think of the 'dead mail box': the destination of messages that no one can deliver.
optionRationales: A DLQ receives messages that have exceeded the maximum number of receipts without successful processing, removing them from the main cycle and preserving them for research and correction.
Visibility Timeout only controls how long the message becomes invisible during processing — it does not rule out or isolate messages with repeated faults.
Rows FIFO ensure order and deduplication, but do not validate content or isolate messages that fail in processing.
Long polling optimizes the way to search for messages (reducing empty answers), without any analysis or filtering of defective content.

questions.text: A company needs to centralize and automate the backups of its resources AWS — volumes EBS, banks RDS, tables DynamoDB and file systems EFS — with unique scheduling and retention policies, applied by tags, and centralized monitoring.?
options: Manual snapshots of each service separately
S3 Cross-Region Replication
AWS Backup
AWS Storage Gateway
questions.explanation: The AWS Backup centralizes data protection of multiple services (EBS, RDS, DynamoDB, EFS, among others) with policy-based backup plans, tag allocation, retention rules and unified monitoring.
questions.hint: The name of the service is literal: the central backup service of AWS.
optionRationales: The AWS Backup centralizes data protection of multiple services (EBS, RDS, DynamoDB, EFS, among others) with policy-based backup plans, tag allocation, retention rules and unified monitoring.
Managing snapshots manually in each service is exactly the operational fragmentation that the scenario wants to eliminate with centralization and automation.
A CRR replica objects between buckets S3 — does not cover EBS, RDS, DynamoDB or EFS, nor offers centralized backup retention policies.
The Storage Gateway integrates on-premises storage with cloud; is not the central resource backup orchestration tool AWS.

questions.text: A global application uses Amazon DynamoDB and it needs that the data are available for reading and writing in various regions at the same time, with automatic replication between them, ensuring continuity even if an entire region is unavailable. DynamoDB meets this requirement?
options: DynamoDB Global Tables
Overall secondary indexes (GSI)
DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX)
Backups on demand from DynamoDB
questions.explanation: Global Tables create multi-Region replicas and multi-active table: applications read and write locally in any participating region, with automatic replication — regional resilience and low global latency.
questions.hint: Watch out for similar names: the right feature turns the table into multi-Active Region.
optionRationales: Global Tables create multi-Region replicas and multi-active table: applications read and write locally in any participating region, with automatic replication — regional resilience and low global latency.
The DAX is a cache in memory that accelerates readings in the same Region; does not replicate data between Regions.
Backups protect against data loss, but do not provide active reading/writing in multiple regions during a regional failure.
Despite the 'global' name, GSIs only allow queries for alternative attributes within the same table and Region — do not replicate data between Regions.

questions.text: A critical application uses Amazon RDS in the region of São Paulo. For the strategy of disaster recovery, the architect created a replica of the bank reading in the region of Ohio. In case of complete disaster in São Paulo, what action allows us to use this replica to restore the operations?
options: Promote the replica of reading to the independent main instance, accepting writings in the Ohio Region
Restore an old snapshot in Ohio Region and discard replica
Convert replica to ElastiCache cluster to take over the writings
Wait for RDS automatically transfer the writing endpoint to the replica
questions.explanation: Reading replicas between regions can be promoted to autonomous reading and writing instances — a classic DR mechanism that combines continuous replication (good RPO) with fast promotion (good RTO).
questions.hint: The replica is a 'successor in training': what is the act that makes it the new bank holder?
optionRationales: Reading replicas between regions can be promoted to autonomous reading and writing instances — a classic DR mechanism that combines continuous replication (good RPO) with fast promotion (good RTO).
The automatic endpoint failureover is characteristic of Multi-AZ within the same Region; the promotion of a replica between Regions is a deliberate action of the administrator (or automation own).
Restoring snapshots would lose replicated transactions continuously until disaster — wasting the main benefit of keeping the replica up to date.
ElastiCache is a cache service in memory — there is no replica conversion RDS in cache, neither cache replaces a relational production bank.

questions.text: A web application saves user sessions in the memory of each instance EC2. When the Auto Scaling removes an instance, users connected to it lose their shopping carts. What change makes the application more resilient to these instances substitutions?
options: Disable the Auto Scaling so that no instance is removed
Schedule instance removals to hours without any connected user
Increase the memory of each instance to support more sessions
Make the statess instances, moving the state of the sessions to an external storage like ElastiCache or DynamoDB
questions.explanation: Statess applications do not keep local status: with sessions in a shared repository, any instance attends any user, and the loss of an instance stops causing loss of session data.
questions.hint: The problem is the state living inside the server — where it should live to survive the instances?
optionRationales: Statess applications do not keep local status: with sessions in a shared repository, any instance attends any user, and the loss of an instance stops causing loss of session data.
Opening the hand of elasticity and self-recovery to preserve local sessions exchanges a problem for another bigger one — and instances can still fail alone.
More memory does not change the problem: the sessions would remain stuck to the instance and lose themselves with it.
Failures don't happen on schedule, and applications with constant traffic rarely have empty windows — the right design is to outsource the state.

questions.text: An architect has configured a Auto Scaling Group with minimum capacity 2, desired 4 and maximum 10, distributed in two Availability Zones. What is the role of the MINIMUM value in this resilience configuration?

questions.text: A company uses a mixture of EC2, AWS Fargate and AWS Lambda, and you want a discount based on a fixed spending commitment per hour (in dollars) during 1 or 3 years, maintaining the freedom to exchange family of instance, Region and even computer service. questions.text: An unexpected marketing campaign will require extra servers for only two weeks, without any long-term commitment, and the load will not tolerate interruptions. EC2 is the appropriate for this punctual need?

questions.text: Tax reports are generated monthly and stored in S3. They are frequently consulted in the first month, rarely after 90 days and, by legal requirement, must be retained by 5 which mechanism of S3 automates the movement of these objects to cheaper classes as they age?

questions.text: A data lake in S3 contains millions of objects whose access patterns change unpredictablely over time. File everything would make the recovery of objects still active slow (hours) and expensive — unfeasible for data with unpredictable access.
One Zone-IA reduces resilience (one AZ) and charges recovery rate — bad for objects that are accessed again frequently.

questions.text: By regulatory requirement, digitised medical records must be retained by 10 years, but they will almost never be consulted — and, when they do, a wait until 12 hours for recovery is acceptable. What class of S3 offers the MENOR storage cost for this scenario?
options: S3 Standard-IA

Standard is optimized for frequent access and costs often more per GB than deep archiving classes.
The Instant Retrieval offers recovery in milliseconds at a higher cost — unnecessary when 12 waiting hours are acceptable.
Standard-IA meets infrequent accesses that require immediate recovery — more expensive than the Glacier classes for decade-long retention.

questions.text: An analysis of use revealed that most instances EC2 of a company uses less than 10% of CPU and memory, because they were provided with 'free for warranty'. The recommended practice of adjusting the type and size of the instances to the real need of the load is called what?
options: Lift-and-shift
Vertical scaling)

Load balancing

Climbing vertically is AUMENTAR the size of a resource to gain capacity — the scenario requires fine adjustment (usually reduction) to the appropriate size.

questions.text: FinOps team wants automatic and machine-based recommendations about which instances EC2, volumes EBS and functions Lambda are oversized or undersized, with specific suggestions of more suitable types from the actual metrics of use. AWS generates these recommendations?

AWS Artifact

AWS Optimizer Computers
questions.explanation: Computer Optimizer analyzes historical metrics of machine learning use and recommends ideal types and sizes for EC2, Auto Scaling Groups, EBS and Lambda — the dedicated right-sizing tool of AWS.
questions.hint: The name of the service delivers the mission: 'optimize computing' with automatic recommendations.
optionRationales: Computer Optimizer analyzes historical metrics of machine learning use and recommends ideal types and sizes for EC2, Auto Scaling Groups, EBS and Lambda — the dedicated right-sizing tool of AWS.
The calculator estimates planned architecture costs ANTES implementation — it does not analyse the actual use of existing resources.

The Artifact deliver conformity reports from the AWS — no relationship with optimization of computational resources.

questions.text: An electronic commerce site has intense traffic during the day and almost zero at dawn, but keeps the same fixed amount of instances EC2 from the point of view of costs, what architectural change eliminates this waste?

Buy Reserved Instances for maximum peak capacity
