optionRationales: The Auto Scaling aligns capacity (and cost) with real demand: less early morning instances, more peaks — paying only for the necessary at every moment.
Larger instances in fixed quantity would increase the cost — the problem is idle capacity outside peaks, not individual size.
Booking the entire peak guarantees discount, but keeps the waste of the morning paid; reservations make sense for capacity BASE constant.
The monitoring economy would be irritating and blind the operation — without metrics, nor the Auto Scaling Officer.

questions.text: Financial manager wants to visually analyze account expenses AWS in the last six months, grouped by service and project tag, identifying growth trends. AWS provides this graphical and interactive analysis of the cost history?

The QuickSight is a generic BI tool for dashboards of any given — the native tool and ready for account costs is the Cost Explorer.
The CloudTrail records calls from API for safety audit — does not show billing analyses.

questions.text: The board defined a US monthly spending ceiling$ 3.000 for the development environment in the AWS and wants to be notified by e-mail when the actual expenditure reaches 80% of this value and again when the forecast indicates that the ceiling will be exceeded.?

Computer Optimizer recommends resource sizing — does not accompany budgets or trigger spending notifications.
The Inspector varre security vulnerabilities in workloads — no budget relationship.

questions.text: One API internal is used only a few times a day, but rotates in an instance EC2 On 24/7, generating constant cost for very little use. From the point of view of cost optimization, why migrate this API for AWS Lambda with API Gateway would be advantageous?
options: Because Lambda is always cheaper than EC2 in any scenario
Because Lambda does not charge by data transfer

Because API Gateway eliminates the need for security and authentication
questions.explanation: The Lambda charge by request and duration: no calls, zero cost of computing — for sporadic charges, the economy over an instance 24/7 It's huge..
questions.hint: Server connected all day to answer 'from time to time' versus pay only when someone calls — where is the waste?
optionRationales: The Lambda charge by request and duration: no calls, zero cost of computing — for sporadic charges, the economy over an instance 24/7 It's huge..
At loads of very high constant volume, the EC2 (with reservations) can cost less — the advantage of serverless is proportional to the idleness of the load.
Output data transfer continues to be collected normally in serverless architectures.
The API Gateway FACILITA authentication and control, but does not eliminate it — and that is not cost argument.

questions.text: A rendering farm processes thousands of animation boards per night. Jobs are fault-tolerant: if one machine is lost, the board simply returns to the queue and is processed by another. What combination of purchase model and justification optimizes the cost of this load to the maximum.?

questions.explanation: Discontinuation-tolerant loads are the perfect use case for Spot: the maximum discount of EC2 with operational risk neutralized by reprocessing line design.
questions.hint: If you lose a machine 'does not hurt', the idle capacity market pays the biggest discount of EC2.
optionRationales: Discontinuation-tolerant loads are the perfect use case for Spot: the maximum discount of EC2 with operational risk neutralized by reprocessing line design.
Failure tolerance described eliminates the need for guaranteed stability — paying full tariff would waste the main economic opportunity.
Dedicated hosts are the most expensive option and meet licensing/insulation requirements — nothing in the scenario justifies them.
The night demand and yield variable does not justify fixed capacity commitment for three years — reserves meet constant loads.

questions.text: The development and approval environments of a company run in instances EC2 and RDS which are only used in commercial hours (8h at 18h, working days), but remain connected all the time. What simple measure can reduce the cost of these environments in up to 70%?

questions.explanation: Stopped instances do not generate computer cost: turn off dev/approval in ~128 idle weekly hours (nights and weekends) cut most of the cost without affecting the team.

optionRationales: Stopped instances do not generate computer cost: turn off dev/approval in ~128 idle weekly hours (nights and weekends) cut most of the cost without affecting the team.
Larger instances would increase the cost — waste is in idle hours, not in the type of instance.
Reservations paid for continuous use 24/7 — for necessary resources only 25% of time, off exceeds the reserve discount.
Duplicate environments DOBRARIA the cost — the opposite of the economy objective.

questions.text: The financial team needs to know how much each project and each department spends on AWS, but all resources are mixed into the same account. What practice allows categorizing the costs per project in billing reports?

questions.hint: Label each resource with its 'gift' and notify the billing system to consider these labels.
optionRationales: Cost allocation tags, after being applied to the resources and activated on the billing console, become filter dimensions in the Cost Explorer and no CUR — enabling the view of expenditure by project and area.
The friendly name is not a structured billing dimension; without enabled allocation tags, reports do not group for this information.
The manual division is laborious, error-prone and unnecessary — the platform offers automatic categorization via tags.
Users IAM control ACESSO, non-attribution of costs — the person who creates the resource does not define the category of collection in the reports.

questions.text: When reviewing the invoice, a company was surprised with the item 'Data Transfer'. About data transfer costs in AWS, what general rule the architect should consider when designing cost-optimized solutions?

questions.hint: Entering is free; leaving (and crossing internal borders) is what costs.
optionRationales: The basic rule of transfer: data entering the AWS are not charged; the charge affects the exit to the internet and the traffic between AZs and between regions – therefore optimized architectures minimize these flows.
The exit to the internet and traffic between AZs/Regions are charged — ignoring this generates surprises just like that of the scenario.
It's the opposite: entry is free just to facilitate cloud adoption.
Transfer costs are permanent and proportional to volume — there is no age exemption from the account.

questions.text: A cost analysis identified dozens of volumes EBS 'orphans' (not attached to any instance), forgotten old snapshots and unused Elastic IPs. Why these resources deserve immediate attention in cost optimization?

optionRationales: Unattached volumes, accumulated snapshots and idle IPs continue on the bill month after month with no benefit — identifying and removing them is the fastest win of any optimization program.
A AWS does not exclude the customer's resources by idleness — they remain (and continue to be charged) until the customer acts.
Except for very specific quota limits, idle resources do not block new provisions — their problem is purely financial.
While resource hygiene also benefits safety, the central point of idle volumes/IPs in cost discipline is valueless continuous collection.

questions.text: A company wants to quickly check if it is leaving money on the table: idle instances, unused volumes, loose IPs and opportunities for Reserved Instances. Which tool of the AWS already includes automatic cost optimization checks ready for use, with actionable recommendations?

optionRationales: The Trusted Advisor includes ready-to-cost checks — instances EC2 underutilized, volumes EBS orphans, idle IPs, use of reservations — with direct recommendations, without prior configuration.
The CloudFormation provides infrastructure as code — does not audit waste or recommends savings.
The GuardDuty detects security threats — does not analyze cost efficiency.
X-Ray tracks distributed requests for application performance debugging — is not cost optimization tool.

questions.text: When a new order is created in an e-commerce system, three different systems need to be notified immediately: billing, stocking and sending confirmation emails. The architect wants to publish a single message that is automatically delivered to all these registered destinations, without the order system needing to know each of them. AWS meets this requirement?
options: Amazon SNS, which allows you to post a message in a topic and automatically deliver it to all subscribers (subscribers) registered
Amazon Kinesis Data Streams, creating a stream that each system continuously consumes
AWS Step Functions, creating a workflow that calls each system in sequence
Amazon SQS, setting up a separate row for each of the three systems and sending the same message manually for each row
questions.explanation: Correct. Amazon SNS implements the publishing/subscribe standard (fan-out): a single message published in a topic is automatically delivered to all registered subscribers, such as rows SQS, functions Lambda or e-mail.
questions.hint: Think of the publication/signature service that automatically delivers a message to all destinations listed in a topic.
optionRationales: Correct. Amazon SNS implements the publishing/subscribe standard (fan-out): a single message published in a topic is automatically delivered to all registered subscribers, such as rows SQS, functions Lambda or e-mail.

The Amazon SQS is a point-to-point row: each message is usually consumed by a single recipient. Sending it manually to multiple rows would require extra logic in the ordering system, which the SNS resolve natively.
The Step Functions orchestrate workflows with sequential or parallel steps explicitly defined, but was not designed as a publication/signature mechanism to notify multiple uncoupled systems.

The Kinesis Data Streams is focused on ingesting and processing large volumes of real-time data (streaming) and requires management of shards and consumers — a more complex solution than is necessary for this reporting scenario.

questions.text: An instance EC2 performing a critical workload (without being part of a Auto Scaling Group) occasionally becomes unavailable due to hardware failures of the underlying physical host. The architect wants the AWS automatically detect this hardware failure and retrieve the instance — preserving the same ID, private IP address, metadata and data in the volumes EBS — without manual intervention. What it should set up?
options: Associate the instance to a Network Load Balancer with health checks configured
Place the instance in a Auto Scaling Group with minimum and desired capacity equal to 1
Migrate the instance to a type (type instance) with more vCPUs and memory
An alarm from the Amazon CloudWatch based on the StatusCheckFailed_System metric, with the action of automatically recovering the instance ("recover")
questions.explanation: Correct. CloudWatch in the system status check metric (which detects problems in the underlying hardware/host), configured with the 'recover' action, automatically migrates the instance to a new hardware, preserving ID, private IP, metadata and data in EBS.
questions.hint: Think about the resource of CloudWatch which can automatically trigger a recovery action from the instance itself when detecting failure in the underlying hardware.
optionRationales: Correct. CloudWatch in the system status check metric (which detects problems in the underlying hardware/host), configured with the 'recover' action, automatically migrates the instance to a new hardware, preserving ID, private IP, metadata and data in EBS.

One Auto Scaling Group would replace the default instance by a new instance — with a new ID and, in general, a new private IP — which does not meet the requirement to preserve the same instance and its identifiers.
A Network Load Balancer just stop sending traffic to an unhealthy target; it does not recover or replace the instance with hardware failure.
Increasing the size of the instance does not prevent or resolve hardware failures in the underlying physical host — the problem is not related to the instance processing capacity.

questions.text: A team set up automatic backups on Amazon RDS with a retention period of 7 days. A failure in an implementation corrupted important data to 14Yesterday's h32. The team needs to restore the database exactly to the state in which it was a few minutes before the corruption, without losing the transactions that occurred before that time. Amazon RDS allows this restoration?
options: Point-in-time restoration (PITR), creating a new database instance with data in the state of a specific moment within the backup retention period
Perform the failover of a Multi-AZ deployment for standby
Promote an existing Read Replica to the main instance
Restore the manual snapshot created at the time the database was originally created
questions.explanation: Right. The point-in-time restoration of the RDS combines the automatic daily snapshot with transaction logs, allowing to recreate the bank in a new instance in the exact state of any second within the configured retention period.
questions.hint: Think of the feature that combines daily backups with transaction logs to restore the database to any second within the set retention period.
optionRationales: Right. The point-in-time restoration of the RDS combines the automatic daily snapshot with transaction logs, allowing to recreate the bank in a new instance in the exact state of any second within the configured retention period.
A Read Replica is continuously updated with the same changes from the main instance — including data corruption — and does not offer a mechanism to 'return in time' until an earlier moment.
In a Multi-AZ deployment, the standby is maintained synchronized by synchronous replication; data corruption would also be replicated to the standby, so the failover does not solve the problem.

A snapshot of the moment of creation reflects only the initial state of the bank, without any of the legitimate transactions occurring later — restoring it would cause much greater loss of data than punctual corruption..

questions.text: An application uses one Application Load Balancer with instances EC2 unequally recorded between two Availability Zones: 6 fora AZ-A and 2 fora AZ-B. The team realizes that, without any additional configuration, traffic is distributed so that each instance — regardless of AZ — receives approximately the same amount of requests. Application Load Balancer, enabled by default, explains this behavior?
options: Cross-area balancing, which distributes traffic uniformly among all registered targets, regardless of the Availability Zone in which they are located
Persistent sessions (sticky sessions), which keep each user always in the same instance
Health checks, which remove unhealthy instances from rotation
Connection draining (deregistration delay), which allows connections in progress to end before removing an instance
questions.explanation: Correct. Application Load Balancer, the balancing between zones is enabled by default and cannot be disabled: the total traffic is equally distributed among all registered instances, not only equally divided between the AZs and the AZs..
questions.hint: Think about the configuration of Application Load Balancer, active by default and which cannot be disconnected, which distributes requests equally among all target instances, not only between Availability Zones.
optionRationales: Correct. Application Load Balancer, the balancing between zones is enabled by default and cannot be disabled: the total traffic is equally distributed among all registered instances, not only equally divided between the AZs and the AZs..
Persistent sessions control which instance the requests of the same user are directed to, but do not explain why the total load is balanced by instance between AZs with different number of instances.
Health checks only determine whether an instance may or may not receive traffic; they do not balance the amount of requests per instance between different Availability Zones.
Connection drainage deals with the graceful removal of balancing instances, but is not the resource responsible for distributing traffic evenly between instances in different AZs.

questions.text: A company wants to gradually launch a new version of its application, hosted on a separate set of servers. Initially, only 10% of production traffic should be directed to the new version, with the others 90% continue in the current version. The proportion can be adjusted over the next days. Amazon Route 53 allows traffic to be distributed in this way?
options: Geographical route (geolocation routing), which directs traffic based on user location
Failover routing, which directs all traffic to a secondary resource if the primary is unavailable
Latency-based routing (latency-based routing), which directs the user to the region with lower latency
Weighted routing, which distributes requests across multiple resources according to the weights defined by the administrator
questions.explanation: Correct. The weighted routing of Route 53 allows to assign a relative weight to each record, controlling the proportion of traffic directed to each resource — ideal for gradual releases (canary releases)).
questions.hint: Think about the policy of routing the Route 53 allowing traffic to be divided between two resources according to a ratio manually defined by the administrator.
optionRationales: Correct. The weighted routing of Route 53 allows to assign a relative weight to each record, controlling the proportion of traffic directed to each resource — ideal for gradual releases (canary releases)).

Failover routing is all-or-nothing: it directs 100% from traffic to the main resource while it is healthy, and only changes to secondary in case of failure — does not allow sharing traffic in fixed percentages.
Latency-based routing automatically chooses the lowest perceived latency feature for each user, but does not offer direct control over a percentage ratio defined by the administrator.
Geographical router directs users to specific resources based on their geographical location, not based on a configurable percentage proportion independent of location.

questions.text: A table of the Amazon DynamoDB store critical data from a financial application. By compliance requirement, the company needs to be able to restore the table to any point in time within the last 35 days, in case of exclusion or accidental recording of items. DynamoDB must be enabled to meet this requirement?
options: DynamoDB Streams
Point-in-Time Recovery (PITR)
Global Tables
Auto Scaling of the DynamoDB
questions.explanation: The Point-in-Time Recovery of DynamoDB, when enabled, it allows to restore the table for any second within a window held from up to 35 days, protecting against accidental exclusions or recordings.
questions.hint: Think about the resource of DynamoDB which allows to restore the table for any second inside a window held from up 35 days.
optionRationales: The Point-in-Time Recovery of DynamoDB, when enabled, it allows to restore the table for any second within a window held from up to 35 days, protecting against accidental exclusions or recordings.

The DynamoDB Streams captures an orderly record of changes to items for external applications (as functions Lambda) process these changes — it is not in itself a mechanism for restoring the table to a point in time.
Global Tables replicate the table among multiple Regions for high availability and low global latency, but do not offer a restoration mechanism for a point in the previous time.
The Auto Scaling of the DynamoDB automatically adjusts the read/write capability based on demand — has no relation to backup or data restoration.

questions.text: A request processing system receives sudden and unpredictable traffic peaks. During these peaks, the service responsible for processing the requests — which runs in a fixed number of instances — becomes overloaded and begins to reject new requests. The architect wants to unplug the receipt of requests for their processing, so that no request is lost during the peaks, even if processing takes longer to clear the accumulated demand.?
options: Manually increase the size of processing instances whenever a traffic peak is perceived
Insert a row of the Amazon SQS between the receipt and processing of requests, allowing the processing service to consume messages at its own pace
Reduce timeout of requests HTTP received by the system of applications
Configure the Auto Scaling processing service to reduce the number of instances during peak traffic
questions.explanation: Right. Amazon SQS uncouple consumer producers: it absorbs peak incoming messages and allows the processing service to consume at its own pace without losing orders during peak traffic.
questions.hint: Think of the queue service that can receive high-speed messages during peaks and allow consumers to process them at their own pace.
optionRationales: Right. Amazon SQS uncouple consumer producers: it absorbs peak incoming messages and allows the processing service to consume at its own pace without losing orders during peak traffic.

Sudden and unpredictable peaks do not give sufficient time for manual intervention; moreover, resizing instances manually does not decouple the receipt of processing or avoid loss of requests during peak.
Reducing timeout makes requests fail faster during overload, but does not prevent requests from being rejected — actually, it would make the experience worse by discarding orders even faster.
Reducing capacity during a peak demand is the opposite of what the scenario needs — this would increase the burden and the rate of rejected applications.

questions.text: A company needs to ensure that snapshots of volumes EBS of its bodies EC2 are automatically created every day, at a specified time, and that snapshots with more than 30 days are automatically excluded — without anyone having to perform this process manually. AWS meets this need?
options: Manually Create One AMI of the instance once a month
Use AWS Trusted Advisor to create snapshots daily
Enable 'version' directly in the volumes EBS by the console of the EC2
Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager (DLM), automating the creation, retention and deletion of volume snapshots EBS based on scheduled policies
questions.explanation: Correct. Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager lets you define policies that create volume snapshots EBS automatically on a defined schedule and exclude older snapshots than a set retention period, without manual intervention.
questions.hint: Think of the resource of AWS dedicated specifically to automating policies for creating and retaining volume snapshots EBS.
optionRationales: Correct. Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager lets you define policies that create volume snapshots EBS automatically on a defined schedule and exclude older snapshots than a set retention period, without manual intervention.
Volumes EBS they do not have a 'version' feature; this concept exists for objects of the Amazon S3, not for block volumes of EBS.
Create a AMI monthly does not meet the requirement for automated daily snapshots with automatic deletion after 30 days, in addition to continuing to depend on manual execution.
The AWS Trusted Advisor provides recommendations on cost, security, performance and other aspects of the account — it does not create or schedule volume snapshots EBS.

questions.text: A critical static site is served via Amazon CloudFront, using a pocket S3 as origin. The team wants that, if the main origin (primary bucket in a region) becomes unavailable, the CloudFront automatically serve the content from a secondary source (bucket replica in another region), without manual intervention. CloudFront allows this configuration?
options: Create two distributions CloudFront separate, one for each bucket
Configure different behavior caches based on the path pattern of the URL
Configure geographical restrictions (geo restrictions) in distribution
Origin group with failure of origin, defining a primary and secondary origin
questions.explanation: Correct. An origin group allows you to configure a primary origin and one of failover; the CloudFront automatically directs requests to secondary origin when the primary returns configured errors (source failure).
questions.hint: Think about the resource of CloudFront which allows to define a primary and a secondary origin, automatically alternating to the secondary when the primary fails.
optionRationales: Correct. An origin group allows you to configure a primary origin and one of failover; the CloudFront automatically directs requests to secondary origin when the primary returns configured errors (source failure).
Two independent distributions have different domains and do not automatically alternate between them — there is no native mechanism of fading between separate distributions.
Cache behaviors route requests for different origins based on the path of URL requested, but do not provide automatic failover for the same URL when the main origin fails.
Geographical restrictions block or allow access to content on the basis of the country of origin of the request — have no relation to failure between origins.

questions.text: When designing VPC of a new application that needs to be fault-resilient, a newly contracted architect created all sub-networks (public and private) within a single Availability Zone, by simplicity. What is the main problem of this approach in terms of resilience?
options: The cost of VPC increases proportionally to the number of Availability Zones used
If this single Availability Zone is unavailable, all application resources — in all sub-networks — are inaccessible, creating a single point of failure
Sub-networks created in a single Availability Zone cannot receive internet traffic
The Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling cannot be used when there are sub-networks in only one Availability Zone
questions.explanation: Right. Concentrating all subnets into a single AZ means that any interruption in that AZ (energy, network, etc.) affects TODOS the application's resources at the same time — exactly the unique point of failure that a resilient architecture seeks to avoid.
questions.hint: Think about what happens to TODOS the application resources if the only Availability Zone used presents a failure.
optionRationales: Right. Concentrating all subnets into a single AZ means that any interruption in that AZ (energy, network, etc.) affects TODOS the application's resources at the same time — exactly the unique point of failure that a resilient architecture seeks to avoid.
Internet access via Internet Gateway operates independently of how many AZs a VPC use — is not the cause of the problem described.
The Auto Scaling can operate with subnets in a single AZ (although this is not recommended for resilience) — technically this does not prevent the use of the service.

There is no additional cost for VPC or by subnets themselves for using more Availability Zones — the cost is associated with resources provided (such as instances and gateways), not with the amount of AZs used for subnets.

questions.text: An application uses the Amazon ElastiCache for Redis as main cache. The team wants that, if the primary node of Redis fails, a replica in another Availability Zone is automatically promoted the primary, without the need for manual reconfiguration of the application. Which ElastiCache for Redis feature meets this requirement?
options: Increase the type (node type) of the Redis cluster node to one with more memory
Migrate to ElastiCache to Memcached with multiple knots
Configure daily manual snapshots of the Redis cluster
A replica group with Multi-AZ enabled, which monitors the primary node and automatically promotes a replica in case of failure
questions.explanation: Correct. An ElastiCache to Redis group with Multi-AZ enabled continuously monitors the primary node and, in case of failure, automatically promotes a replica in another AZ the primary, updating the endpoint without manual reconfiguration.
questions.hint: Think of the ElastiCache to Redis feature that monitors the primary node and automatically promotes a replica in another AZ if it fails.
optionRationales: Correct. An ElastiCache to Redis group with Multi-AZ enabled continuously monitors the primary node and, in case of failure, automatically promotes a replica in another AZ the primary, updating the endpoint without manual reconfiguration.
Memcached partitions the data between us (without replication) and has no automatic failover mechanism — loss of a node means loss of the data stored in it.
Increasing node size improves processing/memory capacity, but does not create replicas or provide automatic failure in case of primary node failure.
Snapshots are useful for backup and later recovery, but do not automatically promote a real-time primary replica when the current node fails.

questions.text: After an incident in which backups stored in a pocket S3 were encrypted and overwritten by an invader who obtained valid credentials, the company wants to ensure that the backups stored in this pocket did not POSSAM be excluded or overwritten by NONE — not even by a user with administrative privileges — during a defined retention period. S3 meets this requirement?
options: A Bucket Policy Denying the DeleteObject Action for All Users
S3 Object Lock in compliance mode, which prevents the exclusion or overwriting of the versions of objects until the end of the retention period, even by users with high privileges
AWS Backup using standard vault without Vault Lock
Only the versioning of the S3, which maintains previous versions of objects
questions.explanation: Correct. S3 Object Lock in the compliance mode applies a model WORM (write-once-read-many: no user — including the root account — can delete or overwrite the protected versions until the end of the retention period.
questions.hint: Think about the resource of S3 which applies a write-once-read-many model (WORM), preventing exclusion or overwriting until the end of a retention period — even by administrators.
optionRationales: Correct. S3 Object Lock in the compliance mode applies a model WORM (write-once-read-many: no user — including the root account — can delete or overwrite the protected versions until the end of the retention period.

The versioning itself preserves previous versions, but a user with permission to delete versions (including an invader with privileged credentials) can still erase them permanently — does not offer guaranteed immutability.
A bucket policy can be changed or removed by any identity with sufficient permissions (such as an invader with administrative credentials), so it does not guarantee real immutability.
Without the Vault Lock, the policies of the vault AWS Backup can still be altered or removed by users with administrative permissions, not guaranteeing the required immutability.

questions.text: One VPC with private subnets in three Availability Zones uses a single NAT Gateway, created in only one of these AZs, to allow the instances of these sub-networks to access the internet. The architect realizes that if this specific AZ becomes unavailable, private instances in the OUTRAS two AZs also lose access to the internet, even if their own AZs are healthy. What change solves this problem?
options: Migrate all private subnets to the same Availability Zone NAT Gateway
Create multiples NAT Gateways in the same Availability Zone NAT Gateway original
Create a NAT Gateway in each Availability Zone and configure the route table of each private sub-network to use the NAT Gateway of MESMA AZ
Replace NAT Gateway by one Internet Gateway shared between the three AZs
questions.explanation: Right. NAT Gateway by AZ, with the route tables of the private sub-networks pointing to the NAT Gateway local, eliminates dependence between AZs: failure of an AZ affects only the subnets of that AZ.
questions.hint: Think about how to eliminate dependence between private sub-networks of an AZ and a resource of NAT located in another AZ.
optionRationales: Right. NAT Gateway by AZ, with the route tables of the private sub-networks pointing to the NAT Gateway local, eliminates dependence between AZs: failure of an AZ affects only the subnets of that AZ.

One Internet Gateway allows resources with public IP address to communicate with the internet; it does not replace the function of NAT Gateway to provide Internet access to resources in private sub-networks without public IP.
Add More NAT Gateways in the same AZ does not solve the problem: if this entire AZ becomes unavailable, all the NAT Gateways will also stay in it, maintaining dependence between AZs.
Concentrate all private subnets into a single AZ re-introduces a single point of failure for the whole application — the opposite of a resilient architecture.

questions.text: A company maintains its main site on servers in the primary region and a simplified version (read only) hosted in another region, intended to be used only in the event of the primary region's unavailability. Route 53 must send TODO traffic to the primary region while it is healthy and automatically redirect TODO the traffic to the secondary region if the primary stop responding to health checks. Route 53 meets this requirement?
options: Latency-based routing between the two regions
Failover routing (failover routing policy), with a primary and secondary record associated with health checks
Weighted routing, attributing weight 100 primary registration and weight 0 Secondary school
Rotating multiple responses (multivalue answer routing) with health checks
questions.explanation: Correct. Failover's routing policy was designed for passive-active scenarios: all traffic goes to primary registration while your health check is healthy, and the Route 53 automatically switch to secondary registration if the primary fails.
questions.hint: Think about the policy of routing the Route 53 designed specifically for active-passive scenarios, where all traffic goes to a primary resource until it fails in health checks.
optionRationales: Correct. Failover's routing policy was designed for passive-active scenarios: all traffic goes to primary registration while your health check is healthy, and the Route 53 automatically switch to secondary registration if the primary fails.
A weight 0 makes the secondary record never receive traffic, even if the primary is unavailable — does not provide the automatic failure required by the scenario.

Latency-based routing directs each user to the Region with less perceived latency, and can send traffic to the Secondary Region even with the healthy primary — does not meet the requirement of 'all traffic to the primary until it fails'.
Multivalue routing returns multiple healthy records pseudo-randomically, distributing requests among them — does not guarantee that 100% traffic goes to the primary region while it's healthy.

questions.text: A worker consumes messages from a row of Amazon SQS in some cases, the worker who received a message locks or delays more than expected to process it, without confirming (excluding) the message in the queue. The team wants that, if a message is not confirmed within a configurable period after being delivered to a worker, it will be available again in the queue so that another worker can try to process it. What configuration of the SQS controls this behavior?
options: Visibility timeout, the period during which a message delivered to a consumer becomes invisible to others before returning to the queue if not confirmed
Delay queue, which postpones the initial delivery of new messages posted in the queue
Dead-letter tail (DLQ), receiving messages after exceeding the maximum number of processing attempts
Long polling, which reduces the number of empty calls by consuming queue messages
questions.explanation: Correct. The visibility timeout defines how long a message received by one consumer remains invisible to others; if the consumer does not exclude it within that period, it automatically becomes visible in the queue for another attempt.
questions.hint: Think about the configuration of SQS determining how long a message delivered to a consumer is 'hidden' from the others before returning automatically to the queue.
optionRationales: Correct. The visibility timeout defines how long a message received by one consumer remains invisible to others; if the consumer does not exclude it within that period, it automatically becomes visible in the queue for another attempt.
Delay queue delays the first delivery of newly published messages; it does not control what happens with a message already delivered to a consumer who failed to confirm it.
Long polling is an optimization to reduce empty consumption requirements (cost/efficiency); it is not related to the return of unconfirmed messages to the queue.

A DLQ is the final destination of messages after many failed attempts — but the mechanism that makes the message available again for new attempt soon after a failure is the visibility timeout, not the DLQ.

questions.text: A company wants that, whenever an object is created in a pocket S3, every time a pipeline of AWS CodePipeline change status, and whenever a custom event is issued by an internal application, different functions Lambda are activated — each routed according to filtering rules based on the content and origin of the event. AWS it was designed as a central event bus, capable of routing events from multiple sources (including several services of the AWS and own applications) for multiple destinations based on rules?
options: AWS Step Functions
Amazon SQS
Amazon EventBridge
Amazon SNS
questions.explanation: Correct. Amazon EventBridge works as a central event bus, receiving events of dozens of services from AWS and own applications, and route them to multiple destinations based on filtering rules by content and origin.
questions.hint: Think of the service designed as a central event bus, with filtering rules that route events from various sources — including services from AWS — for multiple destinations.
optionRationales: Correct. Amazon EventBridge works as a central event bus, receiving events of dozens of services from AWS and own applications, and route them to multiple destinations based on filtering rules by content and origin.

The SQS is a point-to-point message row, aimed at simple disconnection between producer and consumer — it has not been designed as an event bar with content-based routing rules and multiple native sources of the AWS.
The Step Functions orchestrate workflows with explicitly defined stages and state transitions — does not act as a central bus that receives and routes events from multiple external sources.

The SNS offers publication/signature (fan-out) for multiple destinations, but does not have content-based filtering rules or native integration with dozens of service event sources from AWS that the EventBridge offers.

questions.text: A database Amazon RDS is configured in Multi-AZ mode. One developer suggests that the application send reading queries directly to the standby instance in the other Availability Zone to reduce the load in the main instance. Why this suggestion does NOT work as the developer expects?
options: The standby instance accepts only writing operations, never readings
The standby instance only becomes existing after the main instance is excluded
Multi-AZ does not create a standby instance; it only performs automatic backups more frequently
The standby instance of a Multi-AZ deployment exists only for high availability failure and does not accept read connections; to download readings, it is necessary to create Read Replicas
questions.explanation: Correct. The standby instance of Multi-AZ is kept synchronized to take over quickly in case of failure, but is not available to receive application reading connections. To scale readings, the correct feature is the Read Replicas.
questions.hint: Think of the purpose of the standby instance of a multi-AZ deployment — high availability failure — and what other resource of the RDS is used to download reading queries.
optionRationales: Correct. The standby instance of Multi-AZ is kept synchronized to take over quickly in case of failure, but is not available to receive application reading connections. To scale readings, the correct feature is the Read Replicas.
The standby instance is provided and kept continuously in parallel with the main instance since the creation of the Multi-AZ implantation — it is not created only after an exclusion.
Multi-AZ effectively supplies and maintains a standby instance synchronized into another AZ — it's not just a change in backup frequency.
In normal operation, the standby instance does not accept either readings or written directly from the application — it remains synchronized only to take over in case of failure.

questions.text: In one Application Load Balancer, an instance EC2 began to present intermittent flaws in its application. The team realized that the ALB It took several minutes to stop sending traffic to this instance, even after it started failing in health checks. The team wants unhealthy instances to be removed from rotation MAIS RAPIDAMENTE. What can be adjusted in the target group health check configuration for this?
options: Reduce the interval between checks (health check interval) and/or reduce the number of consecutive checks with required failure (unhealthy threshold))
Reduce the number of Availability Zones used by Load Balancer
Increase the timeout of each health check
Deactivate the cross-zone load balancing)
questions.explanation: Correct. The time to a target being considered unhealthy is, approximately, the interval between verifications multiplied by unhealthy threshold; reducing these values causes the ALB detect and remove unhealthy instances more quickly.
questions.hint: Think of the two parameters of health check that control how often the ALB check the health of the targets and how many consecutive failures are needed before considering an unhealthy target.
optionRationales: Correct. The time to a target being considered unhealthy is, approximately, the interval between verifications multiplied by unhealthy threshold; reducing these values causes the ALB detect and remove unhealthy instances more quickly.
Increasing the timeout gives the instance more time to respond before a verification is considered a failure, which tends to delay — not accelerate — the detection of an unhealthy instance.
The number of Availability Zones used by Load Balancer does not influence the speed at which individual health checks detect flaws in a target.
Cross-zone load balancing affects how traffic is distributed among healthy targets, but has no relation to the speed of detection of an unhealthy target by health checks.

questions.text: A team is evaluating migrating from a RDS for MySQL standard for the Amazon Aurora, attracted by the high durability and resilience of storage. Amazon Aurora ensures data durability at storage level, even without the explicit configuration of traditional Multi-AZ RDS?
options: The Aurora store data only locally in volume EBS of the main instance, requiring frequent manual backups
The storage of Aurora automatically replicates the data in 6 copies distributed by 3 Availability zones, transparently, independently of configured computer replicas
The Aurora replicates the data to the Amazon S3 in real time as your only way of durability
The durability of Aurora depends exclusively on manual creation of Read Replicas in other Availability Zones
questions.explanation: Correct. The storage layer of Aurora is distributed and automatically replicates each volume of data in 6 copies distributed by 3 Availability Zones, offering high durability and resilience even without additional reading replicas.
questions.hint: Think of how the storage layer of Aurora (storage layer) is designed in a distributed way between Availability Zones, regardless of read replicas.
optionRationales: Correct. The storage layer of Aurora is distributed and automatically replicates each volume of data in 6 copies distributed by 3 Availability Zones, offering high durability and resilience even without additional reading replicas.
This description corresponds to the traditional storage model of the RDS based on EBS — o Aurora uses a self-distributed storage layer, not a single volume EBS local.

Although the Aurora send backups and logs to S3, the real-time durability of the data comes from the storage layer distributed in 6 copies between AZs, not a direct replication to the S3 to each writing.

Read Replicas are optional computer instances to scale readings; the replication of storage in 6 copies between AZs occur automatically in the storage layer of the Aurora, regardless of the existence of Read Replicas.

questions.text: An application has endpoints (Application Load Balancers) in two different regions of the AWS. The team wants users to be automatically directed to the nearest and healthiest endpoint, using static IP addresses (anycast) that don't change even if an endpoint is unavailable — unlike a solution based on DNS, which may take time to propagate changes due to TTL of the records. AWS meets this requirement?
options: Amazon CloudFront
AWS Global Accelerator
AWS Direct Connect
Amazon Route 53 with latency-based routing
questions.explanation: Correct. AWS Global Accelerator provides static anycast IP addresses and redirects traffic almost instantly to the nearest healthy endpoint, without depending on the spread of TTL of DNS.
questions.hint: Think of the service that provides static anycast IP addresses and redirects traffic almost instantly to the nearest healthy endpoint, without depending on TTL of DNS.
optionRationales: Correct. AWS Global Accelerator provides static anycast IP addresses and redirects traffic almost instantly to the nearest healthy endpoint, without depending on the spread of TTL of DNS.
Latency routing Route 53 is based on DNS and is subject to TTL of records — customers with cached answers can continue to access an unavailable endpoint until expiry of the TTL.

The CloudFront It's a CDN focused on cache content in edge locations; although it has failover of origin, it was not designed primarily to provide static IPs anycast directing traffic between regional ALBs.

The AWS Direct Connect establishes dedicated network connectivity between an on-premises environment and AWS — has no relation to the route of traffic of users to the nearest and most healthy regional endpoint.

questions.text: A team is migrating a containerized application to the AWS and wants that, if a container suddenly stops or stops, it is detected and replaced automatically, without the team needing to manage servers EC2 or own monitoring scripts. What approach offers this resilience in a managed way?
options: Run the application in Amazon ECS with the type of launch AWS Fargate, which monitors tasks and automatically replaces them in case of failure, without server management
Pack the application as a AMI and launch a new instance manually whenever there is a failure
Run the application in a single instance EC2 dedicated with Docker manually installed
Run the application in instances EC2 with a cron script that periodically checks if the container is running
questions.explanation: Correct. AWS Fargate, o ECS manages the underlying infrastructure and continuously monitors the running tasks, automatically replacing those that fail or stop unexpectedly, without the team needing to manage servers EC2.
questions.hint: Think about the type of launch of Amazon ECS which eliminates server management and automatically replaces failed tasks.
optionRationales: Correct. AWS Fargate, o ECS manages the underlying infrastructure and continuously monitors the running tasks, automatically replacing those that fail or stop unexpectedly, without the team needing to manage servers EC2.
This approach is manual, prone to failures and still requires the team to manage servers EC2 — exactly what the team wants to avoid.
A single instance EC2 represents a single point of failure and offers no automatic replacement of the container in case of failure.
This process is manual and slow, not meeting the requirement for automatic detection and replacement of the container in case of failure.

questions.text: An application keeps a large number of connections open directly with a database Amazon RDS in Multi-AZ mode. During a failover event (change to the standby instance), the application takes a considerable time to recover, as each connection needs to be re-established and re-authenticated individually. AWS, positioned between the application and the database, reduces the impact perceived during failure when managing a pool of connections?
options: One Application Load Balancer pointing to the endpoint of the RDS
Amazon ElestiCache
AWS Database Migration Service (DMS)
Amazon RDS Proxy
questions.explanation: Correct. Amazon RDS Proxy manages a pool of connections between the application and the database, drastically reducing the time perceived by the application during a failover, as the proxy maintains connections and redirects traffic to the new main instance.
questions.hint: Think of the service that lies between the application and the database, maintaining a pool of connections and drastically reducing the time perceived by the application during a failure of the RDS.
optionRationales: Correct. Amazon RDS Proxy manages a pool of connections between the application and the database, drastically reducing the time perceived by the application during a failover, as the proxy maintains connections and redirects traffic to the new main instance.
ElastiCache is a cache layer for query results — it does not manage the pool of connections to the database nor reduces the time to fail the RDS.
The AWS DMS is used for database migration and replication tasks — does not act as a real-time connection proxy between the application and the database.
One Application Load Balancer operates in the application layers (HTTP/HTTPS) and was not designed to manage connection pools with relational databases during failure events.

questions.text: An application uses a standard queue (Standard Queue) of Amazon SQS during the tests, the team noticed that occasionally, MESMA payment message is delivered more than once to the consumer, making the payment processed twice for the same request. What is the most likely explanation and recommended approach to deal with it?
options: The solution is to reduce the row's visibility timeout to the lowest possible value
This indicates a serious failure in the SQS which should be reported to the support of the AWS, because rows should never deliver duplicate messages
Standard threads of SQS offer delivery 'at least once' (at-last-once), so occasional duplicates are expected; the application should be designed to process messages in an identical way
Duplicate messages only occur in rows FIFO, never in standard rows
questions.explanation: Correct. SQS ensure delivery 'at least once', which can result in occasional duplicate messages. The recommended practice is to design the processing in an identical way, for example by checking if the order has already been processed before applying the payment again.
questions.hint: Think of the delivery guarantee that the standard rows of SQS offer (at least once) and how the application should be designed to deal with it.
optionRationales: Correct. SQS ensure delivery 'at least once', which can result in occasional duplicate messages. The recommended practice is to design the processing in an identical way, for example by checking if the order has already been processed before applying the payment again.
Occasional duplicate deliveries in standard rows are a documented and expected behavior of SQS, not a service failure.
Too narrowing the visibility timeout may actually, AUMENTAR the occurrence of duplicates, because the message can become visible again before the original consumer finishes processing it..
It's the opposite: rows FIFO offer 'exactly-once' processing (within certain conditions), while standard rows do not guarantee single delivery — are the standard rows that can deliver duplicates.

questions.text: A critical application uses Amazon Aurora and needs a disaster recovery strategy between regions with the MENOR RPO (Recovery Point Objective) possible — the secondary region should be delayed in relation to primary by a few seconds at most and it should be possible to promote it to the primary region quickly in the event of a disaster. Aurora better meets this requirement?
options: Aurora Global Database, which replicates data between regions with typically lower latency than 1 second and allows to promote the secondary region in case of disaster
Multi-AZ deployment within a single region
Read Standard Replica RDS for MySQL between regions
Automatic backups of Aurora manually copied to another region once a day
questions.explanation: Correct. Aurora Global Database was designed specifically for disaster recovery between regions with latency replication typically below 1 second (RPO very low) and allows to promote the secondary region quickly in case of disaster.
questions.hint: Think about the resource of Aurora specifically designed for replication between regions with extremely low replication delay (typically less than 1 second).
optionRationales: Correct. Aurora Global Database was designed specifically for disaster recovery between regions with latency replication typically below 1 second (RPO very low) and allows to promote the secondary region quickly in case of disaster.

Read Standard replicas between regions use asynchronous replication with generally larger latency (seconds to minutes) and a process of promotion different from the optimized mechanism of Aurora Global Database for this scenario.
Daily backups manually copied would result in a RPO up to 24 hours — far above the scenario's few seconds requirement.
Multi-AZ protects against failures of a Zone of Availability within a single Region, but does not offer protection against a disaster affecting the entire Region.

questions.text: An architect is configuring replication between regions (Cross-Region Replication), CRR) of the Amazon S3 between an original ticket in São Paulo and a destination ticket in Oregon, but the configuration fails with an error. He realizes that the versioning is enabled only in the original ticket. What needs to be done to make the CRR function correctly?
options: Enable the versioning also in the destination pocket — the CRR requires that the versioning is enabled in AMBOS the newsletters, origin and destination
Disable the versioning in the original pocket, since the CRR is not compatible with versioning
Create a Lifecycle policy in the destination pocket before setting up the CRR
Move the destination bucket to the same region of the original bucket
questions.explanation: Correct. The replication between regions of S3 requires that the versioning is enabled both in the original and the destination pocket; without this, the configuration of the CRR failure.
questions.hint: Think of which configuration, related to maintaining the version history of each object, the replication between regions of the S3 requires in AMBOS the pockets involved.
optionRationales: Correct. The replication between regions of S3 requires that the versioning is enabled both in the original and the destination pocket; without this, the configuration of the CRR failure.
It's the opposite: the CRR requires that the versioning be enabled in the original (and also the destination) pocket — disable it would make replication impossible.
Moving the destination pocket to the same region would eliminate the purpose of replication between regions (CRR), which is just to keep a copy in a different region.
Lifecycle policies control the transition/expiration of objects and are not a prerequisite for enabling replication between regions.

questions.text: A small development team wants to implement a web application and obtain, with minimal configuration, an environment that already includes load balancing between multiple instances EC2 in different zones of availability and automatic replacement of unhealthy instances — without having to manually configure each of these components individually (Load Balancer, Auto Scaling Group, health checks). AWS offers this experience?
options: AWS Elastic Beanstalk, which provides and manages automatically Load Balancer, Auto Scaling Group and health checks from the application code sent
Amazon EC2, manually launching an instance and configuring each component individually
AWS CloudFormation, requiring the team to write a detailed template describing each resource
AWS Lambda, hosting the entire web application in a single function
questions.explanation: Correct. AWS Elastic Beanstalk provide and manage the underlying infrastructure automatically — including Load Balancer, Auto Scaling Group and health checks — from the application code, with minimum configuration by the team.
questions.hint: Think of the PaaS service of the AWS providing automatically Load Balancer, Auto Scaling and health checks from the application code, with minimum configuration.
optionRationales: Correct. AWS Elastic Beanstalk provide and manage the underlying infrastructure automatically — including Load Balancer, Auto Scaling Group and health checks — from the application code, with minimum configuration by the team.
Although the Lambda have its own resilience model, it does not reproduce the experience of a managed set of instances EC2 with Load Balancer and Auto Scaling for traditional web applications.
This is exactly the manual and laborious approach that the team wants to avoid — set up individually Load Balancer, Auto Scaling and health checks.

The CloudFormation can provide these resources, but requires the team to write and maintain a detailed infrastructure template — the Elastic Beanstalk offers this result with much less configuration, from the application code only.

questions.text: During a disaster event that has made the Region a primary application unavailable, the team needs to quickly put in production, in the Region secondary, a Read Replica of Amazon RDS which had been kept synchronized with the main database. What action is needed for this Read Replica to accept writing operations and function as the new main database?
options: Restart the Read Replica to automatically accept written messages
Just update the application endpoint to point to the Read Replica, without any other action
Promote (promote) the Read Replica, transforming it into an independent instance that accepts readings and writings, closing the replication with the old main instance
Create a new Multi-AZ from the Read Replica before any other action
questions.explanation: Correct. The promotion (promote) of a Read Replica RDS the transforms it into an independent database instance, capable of accepting writing operations, closing the replication relationship with the original main instance..
questions.hint: Think about the specific action of RDS which transforms a Read Replica into an independent database instance, capable of accepting written.
optionRationales: Correct. The promotion (promote) of a Read Replica RDS the transforms it into an independent database instance, capable of accepting writing operations, closing the replication relationship with the original main instance..
As long as it is not promoted, a Read Replica remains read-only and rejects writing operations — pointing out the application to it without promoting it would cause flaws in all writing operations.
A simple reboot does not alter the role of Read Replica; it will only continue reading until the promotion action is executed explicitly.
Multi-AZ configuration is an optional step that can be done later; the necessary and specific action for the Read Replica to accept written is the promotion.

questions.text: An operations team wants to be notified by e-mail and SMS automatically whenever the average use of CPU of a Auto Scaling Group stay above 85% for more than 5 minutes, to proactively investigate before users are affected. AWS meets this requirement?
options: A rule of AWS config that checks the use of CPU daily
One Application Load Balancer with health checks configured to send emails
A policy of Auto Scaling sending an email before adding a new instance
An alarm from the Amazon CloudWatch monitoring the metric of CPU of the Auto Scaling Group, configured to publish a notification in a topic of the Amazon SNS when the limit is reached
questions.explanation: Correct. CloudWatch can continuously monitor the metric of CPU and, when exceeding the limit defined by the configured period, publish a notification in a topic SNS, delivering the message by email and SMS to subscribers.
questions.hint: Think of the combination between the monitoring service that continuously evaluates metrics and triggers alarms, and the notification service that delivers messages by email/SMS.
optionRationales: Correct. CloudWatch can continuously monitor the metric of CPU and, when exceeding the limit defined by the configured period, publish a notification in a topic SNS, delivering the message by email and SMS to subscribers.
Health checks of a Load Balancer determine whether a target receives traffic or not — they do not send email notifications or SMS for operations teams.

The AWS Config evaluates the compliance of the resource configuration (non-real-time performance metrics) and has not been designed for metric limits-based alerts with the required minute granularity.
Scalability policies adjust the group's capacity based on metrics, but do not send email notifications/SMS by themselves — this requires integration with CloudWatch Alarms and SNS.

questions.text: An internal application is used sporadically: virtually without traffic during the night and on weekends, but with significant peaks in specific business hours. The team wants a relational database compatible with MySQL/PostgreSQL that automatically adjusts its computing capacity up and down in seconds, as required, without the team having to manually predict or schedule the size of the instance. Amazon Aurora meets this requirement?
options: An instance Aurora stocked of the largest size available, kept continuously connected
Aurora with Read Additional replicas created manually before each expected peak
Aurora Serverless v2, which automatically adjusts the computing capacity (in units ACU) based on load, in seconds
Migratory to Amazon DynamoDB, which is not a relational database
questions.explanation: Correct. Aurora Serverless v2 automatically adjusts the computing capacity in units ACU, in seconds, according to current demand — ideal for sporadic and unpredictable loads, without manual provisioning.
questions.hint: Think about the option of Aurora which automatically adjusts its computing capacity in seconds, as the demand changes, without manual provisioning of instances.
optionRationales: Correct. Aurora Serverless v2 automatically adjusts the computing capacity in units ACU, in seconds, according to current demand — ideal for sporadic and unpredictable loads, without manual provisioning.
Keeping a large instance connected continuously wastes resources during long periods of low usage — exactly the opposite of the automatic and efficient adjustment that the team seeks.
Creating replicas manually requires early forecasting of peaks and does not adjust the main instance computing capacity automatically in seconds.
The scenario requires a relational database compatible with MySQL/PostgreSQL — the DynamoDB It's a bank NoSQL and does not meet this compatibility requirement.

questions.text: A table of the Amazon DynamoDB uses as partition key the field 'status_order', which has only three possible values ('new', 'processing', 'completed'). With application growth, the team perceives transfer rate limitation (throttling) even with seemingly sufficient capacity provided in total. What is the most likely cause and recommendation for this problem?
options: The problem is caused by the absence of an overall secondary index (GSI)
The table needs an ordination key (sort key), regardless of the selected partition key
The low cardinality of the partition key concentrates the items in few physical partitions ('hot partitions'); the partition key must have high cardinality, distributing the items evenly
The problem is caused by the use of DynamoDB Streams, which must be disabled
questions.explanation: Correct. With only three possible values, all items are concentrated in few physical partitions, creating 'hot partitions' that suffer throttling even if the total capacity of the table seems sufficient. The partition key must have high cardinality values to distribute the items evenly.
questions.hint: Think of how many different values the chosen partition key can assume and how it affects the distribution of items between the physical partitions of the DynamoDB.
optionRationales: Correct. With only three possible values, all items are concentrated in few physical partitions, creating 'hot partitions' that suffer throttling even if the total capacity of the table seems sufficient. The partition key must have high cardinality values to distribute the items evenly.
The DynamoDB Streams only captures a record of changes for external consumption; it does not cause throttling in table reading/writing operations.
Adding an ordination key does not correct the fundamental problem of a partition key with low cardinality — items would remain concentrated on the same few physical partitions.
One GSI help in alternative query patterns, but does not solve the problem of item distribution (and writing ability) in the base table caused by a low cardinality partition key.

questions.text: A financial trading application needs to process millions of connections TCP per second with extremely low latency, and customers need to connect using static IP addresses. The team is choosing between a Application Load Balancer (ALB) and a Network Load Balancer (NLB). What's the best choice and why?
options: Neither Load Balancers supports this volume of connections; multiple instances would be required EC2 with DNS Round-robin
Network Load Balancer, operating in the transport layer (Cover 4), supports millions of requests per second with ultra low latency and offers a static IP address by Availability Zone
Both offer exactly the same performance and static IP addresses, the choice is just aesthetic
Application Load Balancer, because content-based router HTTP reduces latency of connections TCP
questions.explanation: Correct. The Network Load Balancer operates in the Layer 4 (transport), was designed for extreme volumes of connections TCP/UDP with ultra low latency and provides a static IP address (or Elastic IP) by Availability Zone — exactly meeting the requirements of the scenario.
questions.hint: Think about the type of Load Balancer operating in the transport layer (Cover 4 model OSI), designed for extreme connections volumes with minimum latency and static IP support.
optionRationales: Correct. The Network Load Balancer operates in the Layer 4 (transport), was designed for extreme volumes of connections TCP/UDP with ultra low latency and provides a static IP address (or Elastic IP) by Availability Zone — exactly meeting the requirements of the scenario.

The ALB operates in the Layer 7 (application) and content-based routing HTTP adds additional processing — this does not reduce the latency of connections TCP in relation to a Layer balancer 4 as the NLB.
ALB and NLB differ significantly: operate in different layers of the model OSI, have distinct performance characteristics, and only the NLB offers static IP addresses natively by AZ.
The NLB was specifically designed to support extreme volumes of connections (millions per second) with ultra low latency — no need to resort to DNS round-robin manual between instances EC2.

questions.text: An application consults the Amazon ElastiCache before consulting the database. When a data is not found in the cache (cache miss), the application consults the database, returns the result to the user and then records this result in the cache so that future queries are answered directly by the cache. As this cache strategy is known?
options: Write-behind: the writings are done first in the cache and then replicated asynchronously to the database
Lazy loading (also called cache-aside): the data is loaded into the cache only when requested and not found (cache miss)
TTL Infinite: data remains in cache forever, without expiration
Write-through: all written in the database is simultaneously written in the cache
questions.explanation: Correct. In the lazy loading strategy (cache-aside), the application searches the cache first; in case of miss cache, search the database and then save the result to the cache, so that the next queries are answered by the cache.
questions.hint: Think about the name of the strategy in which the data is loaded into the cache only after an attempt to read which resulted in a cache failure (cache miss).
optionRationales: Correct. In the lazy loading strategy (cache-aside), the application searches the cache first; in case of miss cache, search the database and then save the result to the cache, so that the next queries are answered by the cache.

Write-through describes a strategy in which the cache is updated at the time of each writing on the bank — different from the scenario described, which loads the cache only after a reading failure (miss cache).
Write-behind is a strategy of buferization of writings, different from the behavior described, which deals with how the cache is populated after a reading that failed (cache miss).
TTL is a separate configuration about how long an item remains in the cache — does not describe the behavior of loading the cache only after a failed read attempt.

questions.text: A team is choosing the type of instance EC2 for three different workloads: (1) an in-memory database server that processes large data sets in RAM, (2) a video processing cluster that performs intensive calculations of CPU, and (3) a simple web server with moderate traffic and balanced use of CPU/memory. What a combination of families of instances EC2 is more suitable for these three loads, respectively?
options: Optimized computer (C) for the in-memory bank, general purpose (T/M) for video processing, and optimized memory (R) for the web server
General purpose (T/M families) for all three loads, as they offer the best balance for any scenario
Optimized memory (family R) for the in-memory bank, optimized computing (family C) for video processing, and general purpose (family T/M) for the web server
Optimized storage (Families I/D) for all three loads, as they offer the best overall performance
questions.explanation: Correct. R family instances offer high memory/vCPU ratio, ideal for in-memory banks; the C family offers high processing capacity, ideal for intensive loads of CPU as video processing; and T/M families offer the appropriate balance for moderate traffic web servers.
questions.hint: Think of the ratio between vCPU and memory that each family of instance EC2 offers, and in what resource (memory or CPU) is the limiting factor of each workload.
optionRationales: Correct. R family instances offer high memory/vCPU ratio, ideal for in-memory banks; the C family offers high processing capacity, ideal for intensive loads of CPU as video processing; and T/M families offer the appropriate balance for moderate traffic web servers.

This combination reverses the critical features of each load: the in-memory bank needs high memory ratio/vCPU (family R), and video processing needs high capacity of CPU (family C) — not the other way around.

Optimized storage instances are focused on loads with high local I/O throughput (such as banks) NoSQL which depend on local NVMe disks) — do not represent the best general choice for in-memory banks, processing of CPU or simple web servers.
Although suitable for the web server, general purpose instances are not the ideal choice for loads with specific and intense memory needs (bank in-memory) or CPU (video processing).

questions.text: An application stores files CSV of several gigabytes in Amazon S3, but each query of the application needs only a few columns and a subset of lines that meet a specific condition. Currently, the application lowers the entire file to process and filter locally, which is slow and consumes unnecessary bandwidth. S3 allows the application to recover only the necessary data, using an expression SQL simple, without downloading the whole object?
options: S3 Select, which allows you to run queries SQL simple directly on objects CSV, JSON or Parquet stored in S3, returning only the requested data
S3 Transfer Acceleration, which speeds up the download of the entire file using the edge locations of the CloudFront
S3 Multipart Upload, which divides the file into parts for parallel upload
S3 Batch Operations, which performs a mass operation on a list of objects
questions.explanation: Correct. S3 Select lets you run an expression SQL simple directly on the content of an object CSV, JSON or Parquet, returning only the requested columns/lines, without the entire object having to be transferred.
questions.hint: Think about the resource of S3 which allows to use an expression SQL simple to return only the necessary columns/lines of an object, without lowering it completely.
optionRationales: Correct. S3 Select lets you run an expression SQL simple directly on the content of an object CSV, JSON or Parquet, returning only the requested columns/lines, without the entire object having to be transferred.
Transfer Acceleration accelerates the transfer of the entire object through the edge locations — it does not filter or return only a subset of the contents of the object.
Multipart Upload is a resource for uploading large objects into parallel parts — it has nothing to do with consulting or filtering the content of an object during reading.
The S3 Batch Operations performs an action (such as copying or tagging) on a large list of objects — not designed to filter the internal content of a single object during reading.

questions.text: One API REST built with Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda receives a large volume of identical requests (even endpoints, same parameters) for a resource whose result changes only every few minutes. At each request, a new invocation of the function Lambda and a new search of the database is carried out, generating unnecessary cost and latency. API Gateway can reduce the number of invocations from Lambda and latency for these repeated requests?
options: Enable cache of API Gateway to the stage of the API, defining a life time (TTL) for the cache responses of each endpoint combination and parameters
Configure the API Gateway to use authentication IAM instead of keys for API
Increase the timeout set for the function Lambda
Migration to API of REST API for HTTP API, which is always faster
questions.explanation: Correct. API Gateway temporarily stores endpoint responses by a TTL configurable; identical requests within this period are met by the cache, without invoking the Lambda nor consult the bank again.
questions.hint: Think about the resource of API Gateway that temporarily stores endpoint responses, avoiding repeated calls to the backend for identical requests within a defined period.
optionRationales: Correct. API Gateway temporarily stores endpoint responses by a TTL configurable; identical requests within this period are met by the cache, without invoking the Lambda nor consult the bank again.
Increasing the timeout only allows the execution to take longer before it fails — does not reduce the number of calls or avoid repeated queries to the database.
The authentication method used by API is not related to cache storage of responses and does not reduce the number of invocations of Lambda.
HTTP APIs can be faster and cheaper in general, but this does not replace the answer cache — without cache, each identical request would continue to invoke the Lambda and consulting the database.

questions.text: An account of AWS performs various functions Lambda. One of them, responsible for processing critical payments, needs to ensure that it always has the capacity to execute available, even if other functions in the same account consume much of the limit of competition of the account during peaks of traffic. Lambda ensures that this critical function always has a minimum number of simultaneous performances available, isolating it from the competitive consumption of other functions?
options: Set up reserved competition for the payment function, with a part of the account's limit of competition reserved exclusively for it
Increase the memory allocated to the payment function
Configure a Dead Letter Queue (DLQ) for the payment function
Publish a new version of the payment function
questions.explanation: The reserved competition reserves part of the account's limit of competition exclusively for the specified function, ensuring that it always has available capacity, isolated from the consumption of other functions.
questions.hint: Think about the configuration of Lambda which reserves a part of the account's limit of competition exclusively for a specific function, excluding it from other functions.
optionRationales: The reserved competition reserves part of the account's limit of competition exclusively for the specified function, ensuring that it always has available capacity, isolated from the consumption of other functions.

Increasing memory improves the resources of CPU/memory available for CADA individual execution, but does not reserve or isolate a set of simultaneous executions in relation to other account functions.
One DLQ capture events that failed after exhausting repetition attempts — it does not reserve simultaneous execution capacity for function.
Publishing versions manages the code life cycle and implementation aliases — this does not isolate or reserve competition over other account functions.

questions.text: An instance EC2 executes an application with intense use of I/O in volumes EBS with Provisioned IOPS (The team realizes that, at times of high network traffic for other purposes (such as replication of data outside the instance), the performance of the EBS falls significantly, suggesting that the general network traffic of the instance is competing with traffic for volumes EBS for the same network capacity. What can be configured to ensure network capacity DEDICADA for traffic EBS, separate from the general network traffic of the instance?
options: Increase volume size EBS, without changing the type of instance
Migrate volumes EBS from i2 to gp3
Use an instance enabled as 'EBS-optimized', which provides dedicated network capacity for traffic between instance and volumes EBS
Deactivate volume encryption EBS to reduce overhead
questions.explanation: Correct. 'EBS-optimized' provide dedicated and separate network capacity specifically for traffic with volumes EBS, avoiding that it competes with the general network traffic of the instance.
