questions.hint: Think about the feature of some instances EC2 providing dedicated and separate network capacity specifically for traffic with volumes EBS.
optionRationales: Correct. 'EBS-optimized' provide dedicated and separate network capacity specifically for traffic with volumes EBS, avoiding that it competes with the general network traffic of the instance.

Increasing volume size does not resolve a network bandwidth dispute between traffic EBS and the general network traffic of the instance — the limit is in the network capacity of the instance, not in the size of the volume.
Changing the volume type does not solve a network bandwidth containment problem at the instance level — the described gargal is in shared network capacity, not in volume type.
The cryptographic overhead of EBS is minimal and not related to network bandwidth containment between traffic EBS and general instance network traffic.

questions.text: Courts EC2 in private subnets of a VPC frequently access the Amazon S3 to read and record large volumes of data. Currently, this traffic passes through a NAT Gateway up to the public internet to reach the S3, generating data processing costs from the NAT Gateway and additional latency. VPC allows such traffic to the S3 remain within the network of the AWS, without passing through NAT Gateway or on the public internet, reducing cost and latency?
options: An Elastic IP assigned to each instance EC2
Increase the size of NAT Gateway to support more bandwidth
One VPC Peering with another VPC containing the bucket S3
One VPC Gateway-type endpoint for the Amazon S3, added to the private subnet route table
questions.explanation: Right. VPC Gateway-type endpoint for the S3 (or DynamoDB) is added directly to the sub-network route table, allowing traffic for these services to remain in the network of the AWS, without passing through NAT Gateway or on the Internet, without additional cost per hour or per processed data.
questions.hint: Think about the type of VPC Endpoint that allows private subnet traffic to Amazon S3 (and DynamoDB) remain in the network of AWS, being added directly to the route table, without cost per hour or per processed data.
optionRationales: Right. VPC Gateway-type endpoint for the S3 (or DynamoDB) is added directly to the sub-network route table, allowing traffic for these services to remain in the network of the AWS, without passing through NAT Gateway or on the Internet, without additional cost per hour or per processed data.
Buckets S3 do not reside 'within' a VPC; o VPC Peering connects VPCs to each other and is not the way to access the S3 directly from the network of the AWS without going through the Internet.

Assigning Elastic IPs gives public IP addresses to instances, but does not avoid the way through NAT Gateway does not resolve the additional cost and latency to access the S3 from private sub-networks.
NAT Gateways do not have a configurable 'size' in this way, and even increasing capacity, traffic would continue to generate data processing cost and additional latency when passing through it.

questions.text: A site has two categories of content: images of products, which rarely change, and a file JSON with the stock count, which is updated every few seconds. Both are served through the same distribution of the Amazon CloudFront, but currently configured with the same TTL of a kind used in the manufacture of 24 hours, making users see outdated stock information. What the architect should set up to solve this while taking advantage of the cache for the images?
options: Reduce or TTL of the whole distribution for a few seconds, applying it also to the images
Disable cache from CloudFront completely and serve everything directly from the origin
Create different behavior caches for each path pattern, defining a TTL long for the images and a TTL short (or cache disabled) for the stock file
Create a second distribution CloudFront identical only to the stock file
questions.explanation: Correct. Cache behaviors allow you to set different cache rules — including TTL — for different path patterns within the same distribution, allowing to keep long cache for images and short cache (or disabled) only for the stock file.
questions.hint: Think about the resource of CloudFront which allows you to set cache rules (including TTL) different for different path patterns within the same distribution.
optionRationales: Correct. Cache behaviors allow you to set different cache rules — including TTL — for different path patterns within the same distribution, allowing to keep long cache for images and short cache (or disabled) only for the stock file.

This would resolve the stock outdated, but would drastically reduce the cache's benefit to the images, increasing the load on the origin and latency without need — something that caches separate behaviors avoid.
Disable the cache completely eliminates the benefit of CloudFront for images, which rarely change and benefit greatly from a long-term cache.
Creating a separate whole distribution is an unnecessary complexity — cache behaviors within a single distribution already solve this requirement directly.

questions.text: A company needs to migrate 80 data terabytes from your data center on-premises for the Amazon S3. The Internet connection available has limited capacity, and the network transfer would take more than a month. AWS is more suitable to accelerate this initial migration of large volume of data?
options: Compress files before upload using the AWS CLI
AWS Snowball Edge, a physical storage device sent to the company to load the data locally and returned to AWS for import S3
Increase the number of parallel connections used by S3 Transfer Acceleration
AWS Direct Connect, hiring a link of greater capacity only for this transfer
questions.explanation: Correct. AWS Snowball Edge is a robust physical storage device, sent to the customer, used to transfer large volumes of data (such as 80 TB) without depending on the limited capacity of the internet connection — the data are loaded locally and imported into S3 after the device returns to AWS.
questions.hint: Think of the service of AWS involving the sending of a physical storage device to the customer, for the physical transport of large volumes of data without depending on the network.
optionRationales: Correct. AWS Snowball Edge is a robust physical storage device, sent to the customer, used to transfer large volumes of data (such as 80 TB) without depending on the limited capacity of the internet connection — the data are loaded locally and imported into S3 after the device returns to AWS.

Provide a new connection Direct Connect usually takes weeks to months to establish and is focused on continuous connectivity — is not a practical solution to accelerate a single and urgent data transfer.
The S3 Transfer Acceleration still depends on the total capacity of the same limited internet connection — multiple parallel connections do not exceed the aggregate band limit available.
Compression may reduce the volume of data, but it is unlikely that it will reduce 80 TB enough to make a transfer of more than a month, in a limited, practical link.

questions.text: A real-time network package processing application run in instances EC2, needs very high rate of packages per second (PPS), low network latency between instances and minimum jitter. The team wants to take advantage of an optimized network feature, available in modern instances, to meet this requirement. Which feature should be enabled/used?
options: Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration in instances
Enhanced Networking (using the Elastic Network Adapter driver) - ENA), available in supported instance types, which offers higher rate of packages per second, lower latency and lower jitter
Migrate instances to a public sub-network
Increase volume size EBS attached to the bodies
questions.explanation: Correct. Enhanced Networking, enabled via driver ENA in supported instance types, offers significantly higher per second package rates, lower latency between instances and lower jitter, compared to the standard network driver..
questions.hint: Think of the optimized network feature, based on a specific network adapter driver, available in modern instance types for high network performance.
optionRationales: Correct. Enhanced Networking, enabled via driver ENA in supported instance types, offers significantly higher per second package rates, lower latency between instances and lower jitter, compared to the standard network driver..
Volume size EBS is related to storage capacity — is not related to the rate of packages per second or network latency between instances.
The S3 Transfer Acceleration accelerates transfers to/from S3 using the internet edge locations — has no relation to network performance between instances EC2.
Public or private sub-networks determine Internet accessibility, not the rate of packages per second or network latency between instances.

questions.text: A company has hundreds of instances EC2 and wants to identify, based on the actual history of use of CPU, memory and network (collected by CloudWatch), which instances are over or undersized, receiving recommendations of types of instance more suitable for the observed use profile. AWS generates this type of automated recommendation based on machine learning?
options: Amazon CloudWatch Logs Insights
AWS Optimizer Computers
AWS Configure
AWS Cost Explorer
questions.explanation: Correct. AWS Computer Optimizer analyzes historical metrics of use of CPU, memory, network and other resources collected by CloudWatch and uses machine learning to recommend instance types (EC2, among other resources) better suited to the observed use profile.
questions.hint: Think of the service of AWS analyzing historical metrics of use (CPU, memory, network) and use machine learning to recommend more appropriate instance types.
optionRationales: Correct. AWS Computer Optimizer analyzes historical metrics of use of CPU, memory, network and other resources collected by CloudWatch and uses machine learning to recommend instance types (EC2, among other resources) better suited to the observed use profile.
The CloudWatch Logs Insights is a consultation tool on logs — it does not generate recommendations for sizing instance types based on usage metrics.

The AWS Cost Explorer focus on visualization and cost and usage forecasting — it does not generate recommendations for dimensioning machine learning-based instances about patterns of use of CPU/memory/network.
The AWS Config evaluates the configuration of resources in relation to compliance rules — it does not analyze usage patterns to generate sizing recommendations.

questions.text: A site serves JavaScript files, CSS and HTML relatively large through the Amazon CloudFront. The team wants to reduce the size of the files transferred to the users' browsers, improving the loading time, without having to pre-compress and manage multiple versions of each file at source. CloudFront meets this requirement?
options: Enable automatic compression of objects from CloudFront, compressing eligible files (such as JS, CSS and HTML) in formats like Gzip or Brotli before delivering them, when the customer supports
Configure a TTL minimum of 0 seconds for all objects
Restrict access to distribution only via HTTPS
Enable Field-Level Encryption in Distribution
questions.explanation: Correct. Automatic compression of objects from CloudFront compresses eligible text files (JS), CSS, HTML, etc.) using Gzip or Brotli before delivering them to browsers that support compression, reducing the size transferred without requiring multiple pre-compressed versions at source.
questions.hint: Think about the configuration of CloudFront which automatically compresses text files (like JS, CSS, HTML) using Gzip or Brotli before delivering them to browsers that support compression.
optionRationales: Correct. Automatic compression of objects from CloudFront compresses eligible text files (JS), CSS, HTML, etc.) using Gzip or Brotli before delivering them to browsers that support compression, reducing the size transferred without requiring multiple pre-compressed versions at source.
The TTL controls how long an object remains in cache — it does not affect whether the content is compressed before delivery.
Field-Level Encryption encrypts specific fields of sensitive data in forms — has no relation to the size of the transferred static files or to content compression.
Restrict access to HTTPS deals with transport safety — does not reduce the size of transferred files or active content compression.

questions.text: An e-commerce application has a very predictable daily traffic pattern: consistent peaks every day at 9h e at 20h, observed over several weeks. The current scalability policy (target tracking, reactive) adds instances only DEPOIS that the CPU is already high, causing a few minutes of performance degradation at the beginning of each peak, until the new instances are ready. ANTES of each peak, with the system adapting automatically if the traffic pattern changes in the future, without the team having to manually redefine schedules. Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling meets this requirement?
options: Increase target value of target tracking policy
Scheduled scaling, manually setting up an increase in capacity to 8h45 e at 19h45 every day
Predictive scaling, which uses machine learning about the history of use to predict traffic peaks and provide capacity in advance, automatically adjusting to changes in the pattern
Simple scaling, which adds a fixed instance whenever an alarm of the CloudWatch is activated
questions.explanation: Correct. Predictive scaling uses machine learning about historical data to predict recurring traffic patterns and provide capacity before peaks start, continuously updating your predictions if the pattern changes — without requiring manual timing definition.
questions.hint: Think about the type of scalability policy that uses machine learning about historical traffic patterns to provide capacity ANTES of an expected peak, automatically adapting to future changes in the pattern.
optionRationales: Correct. Predictive scaling uses machine learning about historical data to predict recurring traffic patterns and provide capacity before peaks start, continuously updating your predictions if the pattern changes — without requiring manual timing definition.
Simple scaling remains purely reactive: action only occurs after a metric-based alarm is triggered, i.e. after the peak has already begun — does not anticipate increased traffic.

Scheduled scaling requires the team to manually identify and maintain schedules, and does not automatically adjust if the traffic pattern changes — predictive scaling automates this adaptation using machine learning.
Changing the target value of the metric does not resolve the delay between detection of CPU high and the availability of new bodies — policy remains reactive, only with a different threshold.

questions.text: A mobile game has players in North America, Europe and Asia. The board (leaderboard), stored in Amazon DynamoDB, needs to be read with very low latency by players in all these regions, and players can also record new scores that should be visible to players from other regions in a few seconds. DynamoDB allows the data to be available locally, with low read and write latency, in multiple regions of the AWS simultaneously?
options: Global Tables, which replicate the table among multiple selected regions, allowing low latency local readings and writings in each region, with active-active replication among them
DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX), implemented in a single region
Increase the provided reading/writing capacity of the table in a single region
Read Replicas DynamoDB created in each region
questions.explanation: Right. DynamoDB replicate the table between the selected regions in an active-configuration: each region accepts low latency local readings and writings, and the changes are automatically spread to the other regions in seconds.
questions.hint: Think about the resource of DynamoDB which replicates a table among multiple regions of the AWS, allowing readings and local writings of low latency in each of them.
optionRationales: Right. DynamoDB replicate the table between the selected regions in an active-configuration: each region accepts low latency local readings and writings, and the changes are automatically spread to the other regions in seconds.
The DAX is a cache in memory that reduces reading latency within a single implantation/region — it does not replicate the data between multiple regions of the AWS.
The DynamoDB does not have the concept of 'Read Replicas' as the RDS; the mechanism of replication between regions of the DynamoDB are the Global Tables.

Increasing capacity in a single region does not solve the inherent latency of a request crossing long geographical distances to that region — it is necessary to have the data replicated locally in each region.

questions.text: An application needs to orchestrate a high volume event processing stream (millions of executions per day), where each execution is short (seconds) and does not need to maintain a detailed execution history for more than a few hours. The team evaluates using the AWS Step Functions, but is concerned about the cost and the execution rate limits of the standard workflow type (Standard). What kind of workflow do you have? Step Functions is suitable for this scenario of high volume and short duration?
options: Standard Workflows, which are always the recommended option regardless of execution volume
Express Workflows, designed for high volume and short-term executions, with a collection model based on duration and number of executions
Amazon SQS configured with FIFO, without using the Step Functions
AWS Batch, which completely replaces the Step Functions for any workflow
questions.explanation: Right. The Express Workflows of Step Functions were designed specifically for very high volume and short duration executions, with much higher rate limits and a collection model based on the number of executions and duration, more suitable for this profile..
questions.hint: Think about the type of workflow of Step Functions optimized specifically for very high volume and short duration executions, with a different collection model from the standard.
optionRationales: Right. The Express Workflows of Step Functions were designed specifically for very high volume and short duration executions, with much higher rate limits and a collection model based on the number of executions and duration, more suitable for this profile..
Standard Workflows have lower execution rate limits and a state transition collection model, less suitable for very high volume loads and very short executions — they are not always the best option.
The AWS Batch is a service for the execution of batch jobs, with a different purpose from Step Functions — it is not a 'type of workflow' of Step Functions nor replaces it for state orchestration.
Rows FIFO of the SQS ensure order and unique message processing, but do not offer workflow orchestration capabilities (state machine) that the Step Functions provides.

questions.text: A data processing application needs to download a single very large object (several gigabytes) from Amazon S3 As soon as possible. Instead of making the sequential download from start to finish, the team wants to split the download into several parts and download them EM PARALELO using multiple connections, joining the parts later. S3 allows each connection to request only one specific band of bytes of the same object?
options: Enable bucket versioning to allow parallel downloads
S3 Select, returning the entire object automatically divided
S3 Multipart Upload, applied to the download process
GET Range (byte-range fetches), which allows you to request only a specific range of bytes of an object in each request GET, allowing parallel downloads of parts of the same object
questions.explanation: Correct. Range parameter in a request GET of the S3 allows specifying a specific bytes interval of the object to be returned, allowing multiple connections to lower different parts of the same object in parallel.
questions.hint: Think about the parameter of a request GET of the S3 which allows specifying an object bytes interval, allowing multiple connections to lower different parts of the same object in parallel.
optionRationales: Correct. Range parameter in a request GET of the S3 allows specifying a specific bytes interval of the object to be returned, allowing multiple connections to lower different parts of the same object in parallel.
Multipart Upload is a specific resource for ENVIO large objects in parallel parts — it does not apply to the download of an existing object.
The S3 Select Run Queries SQL to filter the content of an object — it does not automatically divide an object into bytes intervals for parallel download.
Bucket versioning manages the version history of objects and has no relation to the ability to download parts of an object in parallel.

questions.text: An application uses Amazon Aurora with multiple Replicas of Reading (Aurora Replications) to scale reading queries. The volume of reading queries varies significantly throughout the day: high during business hours and low during the morning. The team wants the Number of Reading Replications to increase and decrease automatically based on the reading load, without the need to add or remove replicas manually. Aurora meets this requirement?
options: Configure the DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) in front of the Aurora
Aurora Auto Scaling for reading replicas, which adds or removes Aurora Replications automatically based on a scalability policy defined on metrics as using CPU or connections
Manually increase the number of replicas at the beginning of each working day and remove them at night
Aurora Serverless v2 applied only to the main instance (writer))
questions.explanation: Correct. Aurora Auto Scaling allows you to define a policy that automatically adds or removes Aurora Replicas based on monitored metrics, such as use of CPU or number of connections, adjusting the number of reading replicas to demand.
questions.hint: Think about the resource of Aurora adding or removing read replicas automatically (Aurora Replicas) based on scalability policies defined on use metrics.
optionRationales: Correct. Aurora Auto Scaling allows you to define a policy that automatically adds or removes Aurora Replicas based on monitored metrics, such as use of CPU or number of connections, adjusting the number of reading replicas to demand.

The Aurora Serverless v2 adjusts the computing capacity of an instance (in ACUs), but the scenario specifically asks that the Number of read replicas automatically change — that's the Aurora Auto Scaling for replicas.
This process is manual and does not meet the automatic adjustment requirement without team intervention.
The DAX is a specific cache service for the DynamoDB and is not compatible with the Aurora, which is a relational database.

questions.text: A corporate application requires external clients to configure firewall rules based on fixed IP addresses to access a set of servers behind a load balancer. The team is using one Application Load Balancer (ALB), whose IP address changes over time, making it difficult for customers to set up firewalls. load balancer of AWS allows you to associate a static IP address (Elastic IP) by area of availability?
options: Add Record DNS Type A pointing to the current IP of ALB
Network Load Balancer (NLB), which offers a static IP address per availability zone, and can be associated with an Elastic IP
Application Load Balancer (ALB), configuring an Elastic IP directly into your network interface
Classic Load Balancer, which always provides a static IP address
questions.explanation: Correct. The Network Load Balancer operates on the transport layer (chamber 4) and provides a static IP address per availability zone, to which it is possible to associate an Elastic IP — serving customers who need fixed IPs for firewall rules.
questions.hint: Think about the type of load balancer of AWS operating in the transport layer (chamber) 4) and offers a static IP address by availability zone.
optionRationales: Correct. The Network Load Balancer operates on the transport layer (chamber 4) and provides a static IP address per availability zone, to which it is possible to associate an Elastic IP — serving customers who need fixed IPs for firewall rules.
The ALB does not allow to associate Elastic IPs directly — your IP address can change over time, which is precisely the problem described in the scenario.
The Classic Load Balancer it also has dynamic IP addresses, presenting the same problem of ALB for this requirement.
A record DNS does not solve the dynamic IP problem: it would need to be updated every time the IP of ALB change, and IP-based firewall rules would continue to break.

questions.text: An application uses the Amazon ElastiCache for Redis to store cached data. The cached data volume has grown beyond the memory capacity of a single node, and the team needs to partition (do sharding) the cached data between multiple nodes, keeping the writing capacity distributed among them. Which ElastiCache for Redis configuration allows partitioning data between multiple shards (groups of noxious)?
options: Add read replicas to the primary node, without enabling cluster mode
Migratory to Amazon DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX)
Increase the size (type instance) of the existing single node
Enable cluster mode in ElastiCache for Redis, which partitions data between multiple shards, each with its own primary node
questions.explanation: Right. ElastiCache for Redis's Mode Cluster partitions data into multiple shards, each with its own primary node, allowing both storage and writing capacity to be scaled horizontally.
questions.hint: Think of the ElastiCache for Redis configuration that partitions (sharding) the cache data between multiple groups of nodes (shards), each with its own primary node.
optionRationales: Right. ElastiCache for Redis's Mode Cluster partitions data into multiple shards, each with its own primary node, allowing both storage and writing capacity to be scaled horizontally.
Reading replicas without cluster mode increase reading ability, but all data still resides in memory of a single primary shard — there is no partitioning of data.
The DAX is a specific cache layer for the DynamoDB — is not a partitioning configuration for ElastiCache for Redis.
Climbing vertically a single node has limits and does not offer the horizontal partitioning between multiple shards that the team needs.

questions.text: An engineering team wants to migrate its instances EC2 of a generic processing workload (code compilation, containerized microservices) for instance types that offer better cost-performance ratio, and the application is already compatible with the architecture ARM64. What family of processors, developed by itself AWS is used in certain types of instance EC2, is known for offering better cost-benefit for workloads compatible with ARM?
options: Intel Xeon processors from previous generations, which are usually cheaper because they have fewer resources
Courts Spot exclusively, regardless of processor family
Fora with GPU dedicated (G or P families), which accelerate any kind of workload
Processors AWS Graviton, based on architecture ARM, available in instance types (such as M6g, C6g, R6g) that usually offer better cost-performance ratio for compatible loads
questions.explanation: Right. Processors AWS Graviton, based on architecture ARM and developed by itself AWS, are available in instance families (such as the 6g) and usually offer better cost-performance ratio for workloads compatible with ARM64.
questions.hint: Think of the family of processors developed by the self AWS, based on architecture ARM, known for offering better cost-performance ratio for compatible workloads.
optionRationales: Right. Processors AWS Graviton, based on architecture ARM and developed by itself AWS, are available in instance families (such as the 6g) and usually offer better cost-performance ratio for workloads compatible with ARM64.
Institutions based on ancient generations of Xeon are not promoted as the best cost-performance option — Graviton is the recommended path by AWS for loads compatible with ARM who seek this benefit.
Spot is a precision model, not a processor family, and does not deal with the compatibility detail with ARM64 mentioned in the scenario.
Fora with GPU they are oriented to graphic/ML loads and tend to be more expensive — they do not represent better cost-performance ratio for generic processing.

questions.text: A distribution of Amazon CloudFront serves global traffic and uses a unique source server, located in a single region of AWS. At peak times, even with the cache of CloudFront, the origin receives a considerable volume of simultaneous requests from different edge locations around the world they had miss cache at the same time, overloading it. CloudFront adds an extra layer of central cache between the edge locations and origin, reducing the amount of requests that reach it?
options: Configure Lambda@Edge to respond directly without consulting the source
Origin Shield, an additional cache layer of the CloudFront consolidating the miss cache requests of several edge locations before they get to the origin
Enable Field-Level Encryption in Distribution
Increase the number of edge locations enabled in distribution
questions.explanation: Right. Shield adds an extra central cache layer between the edge locations and origin, consolidating requests for miss caches from different locations and significantly reducing the load that comes to origin.
questions.hint: Think about the resource of CloudFront adding an extra central cache layer between the edge locations and origin, consolidating Miss cache requests.
optionRationales: Right. Shield adds an extra central cache layer between the edge locations and origin, consolidating requests for miss caches from different locations and significantly reducing the load that comes to origin.
Increase the number of edge locations tends to increase, not decrease, the number of independent points that may have miss cache and generate requests at source.
The Lambda@Edge executes custom code on edge locations, but does not, by itself, provide a consolidated cache layer that reduces Miss cache requests to the source.
Field-Level Encryption protects sensitive data from forms and is not related to the reduction of load at source caused by cache misses.

questions.text: The database team has noticed that an instance Amazon RDS is showing slowness at certain times, but is not able to identify which consultations SQL specific are consuming more bank resources (load, or 'load') during these periods. Amazon RDS provides a visual panel that helps identify queries (SQL states) which contribute most to the database load in a time interval?
options: Amazon RDS Performance Insights, which provides a visual database load panel (DB Load) and allows you to identify key queries SQL, hosts and users who contribute to this load
Enable Multi-AZ in instance RDS
AWS Trusted Advisor
Amazon CloudWatch Alarms configured on the CPUtilization metric
questions.explanation: Correct. RDS Performance Insights provides a database load visual panel (DB Load), allowing you to identify and detail which queries SQL, hosts and users more contribute to this load in a certain time interval.
questions.hint: Think about the resource of Amazon RDS which provides a database load visual panel (DB Load) and helps identify which queries SQL more specific contribute to this load.
optionRationales: Correct. RDS Performance Insights provides a database load visual panel (DB Load), allowing you to identify and detail which queries SQL, hosts and users more contribute to this load in a certain time interval.
An alarm from CPU warns when use is high, but does not detail the load by consultation SQL individual.
The Trusted Advisor offers general good practice checks (cost, safety, performance), not a detailed bank load analysis at the consultation level.
Multi-AZ provides high availability by means of a standby replica — does not provide a performance diagnosis at the consultation level SQL.

questions.text: An application executed in an instance EC2 keeps a large data set loaded into memory RAM (the 'hot' state of the application), and the initialization process to rebuild this state of zero takes many minutes. The team wants power PARAR (stop) the instance during periods of low demand to save costs, but, when starting it again, the content of the memory RAM it must be restored exactly as it was, without needing to reprocess everything. EC2 meets this requirement?
options: Create a AMI before you stop her
EC2 Hibernate, which saves the contents of memory RAM in a volume file EBS root when stopping the instance, restoring it automatically when the instance is started again
Use instances Spot, that always preserve the state of memory
EC2 Auto Recovery, which automatically recreates the instance in case of hardware failure
questions.explanation: Correct. EC2 Hibernate Saves Memory Content RAM in a volume file EBS root at the time of the instance stop and restore it automatically at the next startup, preserving the 'hot' state of the application without needing to reprocess it.
questions.hint: Think about the resource of EC2 which saves the contents of memory RAM on disk when you stop the instance and restore it automatically when it is started again.
optionRationales: Correct. EC2 Hibernate Saves Memory Content RAM in a volume file EBS root at the time of the instance stop and restore it automatically at the next startup, preserving the 'hot' state of the application without needing to reprocess it.
Auto Recovery treats underlying hardware failures by relaunching the instance — does not preserve the memory state RAM in a stop and start deliberated by the team.
Create a AMI captures a disk-based snapshot to launch new instances — does not preserve or restore memory status RAM in execution of the original instance when stopping/starting.
Spot is a model of precision and instances Spot can be interrupted with little warning — this does not preserve the state of memory itself RAM between stops and beginnings.

questions.text: A web application behind a Application Load Balancer is suffering a brute force attack on the login form: the same set of IP addresses is sending thousands of login attempts per minute. The team wants to automatically block, for a period, IPs that exceed a certain number of requests in a short time interval, without blocking legitimate users.?
options: AWS WAF with a rate-based rule (rate-based rule), which automatically blocks IP addresses that exceed a requirement limit defined in a time window
Increase the size of the instances EC2 behind the ALB to support more requests
Configure a Security Group which blocks all entry traffic at the door 443
Configure the Amazon GuardDuty to automatically block suspicious traffic
questions.explanation: The rules based on the rate of AWS WAF monitor the amount of IP requests from origin in a time window and automatically block (for a configurable period) IPs that exceed the defined limit, mitigating brute force attacks without affecting legitimate users.
questions.hint: Think about the resource of AWS WAF allowing you to automatically lock IP addresses that exceed a number of requests in a time window.
optionRationales: The rules based on the rate of AWS WAF monitor the amount of IP requests from origin in a time window and automatically block (for a configurable period) IPs that exceed the defined limit, mitigating brute force attacks without affecting legitimate users.
Lock the whole door 443 would prevent access of TODOS users, including legitimate ones — is not a selective solution against abusive IPs.
Increasing computing capacity does not stop the brute force attack — it would just make it more expensive to absorb it without solving the problem.
The GuardDuty detects and generates threats alerts, but does not block traffic directly in the network layer/load balancer — this blocking action is the role of the WAF.

questions.text: A company operates a critical financial application and wants advanced protection against volumetric DDoS attacks on layers 3/4 and 7, including access to a specialized DDoS response team (DRT) and cost protection against escalating peaks caused by an attack. AWS Shield Standard, enabled by default and free, already offers some protection, but does not cover these additional features. AWS meets this requirement?
options: AWS Shield Standard, which already provides access to DRT and cost protection
AWS Shield Advanced, which offers advanced protection against DDoS, access to DDoS Response Team (DRT) and cost protection against escalating peaks during attacks
AWS WAF, configured in isolation without the Shield Advanced
Amazon GuardDuty with all detectors enabled
questions.explanation: Correct. AWS Shield Advanced, a paid service, adds advanced protection against large-scale DDoS attacks, access to specialized team DRT and cost protection against escalating peaks caused by attacks.
questions.hint: Think about the level of protection against DDoS AWS, payment, which adds access to a specialized response and cost protection team against escalating peaks during attacks.
optionRationales: Correct. AWS Shield Advanced, a paid service, adds advanced protection against large-scale DDoS attacks, access to specialized team DRT and cost protection against escalating peaks caused by attacks.
The AWS WAF protects against holdings in the application layer, such as SQL injection e XSS, but does not provide access to the DDoS Response Team or cost protection against escalating peaks.
The GuardDuty is a threat detection service — it does not provide DDoS mitigation capability or access to DRT.
The Shield Standard is the basic, free and automatically enabled protection for all customers — it does NOT include access to DRT no cost protection, benefits exclusively from Advanced level.

questions.text: A company uses AWS KMS to encrypt sensitive data with a customer-managed key (customer managed key) - CMK). By security policy, the underlying cryptographic material of the key must be rotated annually, but the team does not want to manually re-encrypt all existing data at each rotation, nor to update key references in their applications. KMS meets this requirement?
options: Use only keys managed by AWS (AWS managed keys), which cannot have the rotation configured by the customer
Create a new one CMK every year and manually re-encrypt all data with the new key
Enable automatic key rotation at CMK, which generates new cryptographic material annually maintaining the same ID/ARN of the key, without requiring re-encryption of existing data
Disable encryption and apply encryption at the application level
questions.explanation: Correct. Automatic key rotation of the KMS generates new backend cryptographic material periodically (annually), but maintains the same ID/ARN of CMK — o KMS continues to know how to decipher old data with the previous material, without the need to re-encrypt existing data or change references in the application.
questions.hint: Think about the resource of KMS which automatically generates new cryptographic material for a customer-managed key periodically, without changing the ID/ARN of the key nor require re-cryption of data.
optionRationales: Correct. Automatic key rotation of the KMS generates new backend cryptographic material periodically (annually), but maintains the same ID/ARN of CMK — o KMS continues to know how to decipher old data with the previous material, without the need to re-encrypt existing data or change references in the application.
This is exactly the manual work of re-crypting and updating references that the team wants to avoid — automatic rotation resolves this in a transparent way.

The AWS managed keys already rotate automatically every year, but the scenario explicitly requires the use of a customer-managed key (CMK) — and the question is about the rotational resource applicable to that CMK.
Remove encryption managed by KMS eliminates your benefits completely and does not meet the requirement of periodic key rotation.

questions.text: An application stores database credentials Amazon RDS The security team requires that these credentials be removed from the code, stored securely and rotated automatically in a regular interval, without the need to manually change the password in the database and in the application to each rotation. AWS fully meets this requirement?
options: Store credentials as environment variables encrypted in a function Lambda
AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store, in the Standard layer, without any additional configuration
Create a Bucket S3 private to store a configuration file with credentials
AWS Secrets Manager, which stores credentials securely and encryptedly, and can rotate them automatically within a defined interval, updating both the stored secret and the password in the database
questions.explanation: Correct. AWS Secrets Manager encrypted credentials storage and offers automatic rotation integrated with databases RDS, updating the bank password and the secret stored simultaneously, without manual intervention.
questions.hint: Think of the service of AWS dedicated to secure storage of credentials that can rotate them automatically, updating both the secret and password in the database.
optionRationales: Correct. AWS Secrets Manager encrypted credentials storage and offers automatic rotation integrated with databases RDS, updating the bank password and the secret stored simultaneously, without manual intervention.

The Parameter Store in the Standard layer can store encrypted secrets via KMS, but does not offer integrated automatic rotation that updates the password in the database — this feature is Secrets Manager.
This would also require updating manually both the environment variable and the database password at each rotation — does not meet the full automatic rotation requirement.
Store credentials in a file at S3 does not offer automatic rotation and is a less secure standard than a dedicated secret management service.

questions.text: A company wants to continuously monitor its accounts AWS in search of malicious or unauthorized activities — as calls for API anomalous, communication with IP addresses known to host malware, or instances EC2 committed mining cryptocurrency — automatically analyzing sources like CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs and DNS logs, without needing to deploy agents or own infrastructure. AWS meets this requirement?
options: AWS CloudTrail, configured to generate alerts automatically
AWS Config, which assesses the conformity of resource configuration with defined rules

Amazon GuardDuty, a threat detection service that continuously analyzes CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs and DNS logs using threat intelligence and machine learning, without requiring agents or additional infrastructure
Amazon Inspector, evaluating software vulnerabilities in instances EC2 and images of containers
questions.explanation: Correct. Amazon GuardDuty continuously analyzes data sources as CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs and DNS logs, applying threat intelligence and machine learning to identify malicious activities, such as cryptocurrency mining or communication with malicious IPs, without the need for agents.
questions.hint: Think of the threat detection service of the AWS that continuously analyzes logs as CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs and DNS, using threat intelligence and machine learning, without requiring agents.
optionRationales: Correct. Amazon GuardDuty continuously analyzes data sources as CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs and DNS logs, applying threat intelligence and machine learning to identify malicious activities, such as cryptocurrency mining or communication with malicious IPs, without the need for agents.

The AWS Config checks whether the resource configuration is in accordance with defined rules — it does not analyze logs for malicious activity patterns such as cryptocurrency mining or calls from API anomalous.
The Inspector focus on vulnerability assessment in workloads — not on continuous analysis of account activity logs for threat detection.

The CloudTrail records the activity of API, but does not analyze these logs in search of threats using threat intelligence and machine learning — this is the role of GuardDuty, which uses the CloudTrail as one of your data sources.

questions.text: A company stores large volumes of files in the Amazon S3 and suspect that some of these files may contain sensitive data, such as credit card numbers or identifiable personal information (PII), stored without proper control. The team wants a service that uses machine learning and pattern matching to automatically discover and classify these sensitive data within the newsletters S3. What is the service of AWS meets this requirement?
options: Amazon Macie, using machine learning and pattern matching to discover, classify and protect sensitive data (such as PII and financial data) stored in Amazon S3
Amazon Athena, carrying out consultations SQL manuals on the files of the S3
Amazon Rekognition, which analyzes images and videos
AWS Glue Data Catalog, which only catalogues metadata of data schemes
questions.explanation: Correct. Amazon Macie uses machine learning and pattern matching techniques to scan buckets S3, identifying and automatically classifying sensitive data as identifiable personal information (PII) and credit card numbers.
questions.hint: Think of the service of AWS using machine learning to automatically discover and classify sensitive data (such as PII) stored in Amazon S3.
optionRationales: Correct. Amazon Macie uses machine learning and pattern matching techniques to scan buckets S3, identifying and automatically classifying sensitive data as identifiable personal information (PII) and credit card numbers.
The Athena allows you to consult data via SQL, but does not automatically discover and classify sensitive data patterns using machine learning on all the bucks.
The Glue Data Catalog manages metadata about data structure/scheme — it does not classify the sensitivity of data content.
Rekognition is focused on image and video analysis — not discovery of sensitive text data, such as PII, in objects of the S3.

questions.text: A platform team wants developers to create their own roles and policies IAM for your projects, but you need to ensure that, regardless of the permissions a developer grants to a roll, this roll is NUNCA may exceed a centrally defined maximum set of permissions (for example, you may never access resources from other teams or change account security settings). IAM allows to define this maximum effective permissions for entities created by other users?
options: Resource tags combined with tag-based policies
Groups of IAM, which only group users for allocation of common policies
Permission Boundaries, a managed policy that defines the MAXIMUM set of permissions that an entity IAM may have, regardless of the identity-based policies attached to it
Service Control Policies (SCPs) applied only to the root account (management account))
questions.explanation: Right. Permission Boundaries define the maximum ceiling of effective permissions of an entity IAM (user or role): even if identity-based policies grant wider permissions, effective access never exceeds what the limit allows.
questions.hint: Think about the resource of IAM which defines the maximum limit of permissions that an entity may have, complementing (but not replacing) identity-based policies.
optionRationales: Right. Permission Boundaries define the maximum ceiling of effective permissions of an entity IAM (user or role): even if identity-based policies grant wider permissions, effective access never exceeds what the limit allows.

SCPs act at the level of AWS Organizations, restricting what whole accounts can do — the scenario describes limiting individual roles/users created within the UMA other users, which is the purpose of permission bonds.
Groups of IAM are an organizational resource to assign shared policies to users — they do not impose a maximum ceiling of permissions for roles created independently by others.
Tag-based policies may restrict access to resources with specific tags, but do not set a general ceiling of maximum permissions, regardless of what identity policies grant.

questions.text: A company needs to continuously ensure that all volumes EBS The team also wants to maintain a history of changes in the configuration of resources for audit purposes. AWS meets these requirements for continuous conformity assessment and configuration history?
options: AWS Config, which continuously evaluates the configuration of resources against defined rules (such as 'volumes' EBS must be encrypted'), maintains a history of configuration changes and can trigger automatic remediations via SSM Automation
Amazon CloudWatch Events (EventBridge) configured in isolation
AWS Trusted Advisor, at the Basic support level
Amazon Inspector, configured to scan volumes EBS
questions.explanation: Correct. AWS Config continuously evaluates remedies against compliance rules (such as requiring volume encryption) EBS), maintains a detailed history of configuration changes for audit, and can trigger automatic remediation actions using the SSM Automation.
questions.hint: Think of the service of AWS which continuously evaluates whether resources are in accordance with defined rules (such as volume encryption), maintains configuration history and can trigger automatic remedial actions.
optionRationales: Correct. AWS Config continuously evaluates remedies against compliance rules (such as requiring volume encryption) EBS), maintains a detailed history of configuration changes for audit, and can trigger automatic remediation actions using the SSM Automation.

The EventBridge route events between services and can trigger actions, but does not continuously evaluate the configuration of resources against compliance rules nor maintains a configuration history.
The basic level of Trusted Advisor offers only a limited set of checks and does not provide continuous evaluation of custom rules, auto repair or configuration history.

The Inspector evaluate workloads (instances) EC2, container images, Lambda) as for software vulnerabilities and network exposure — general non-conformity of resource configuration, such as encryption, with history of changes.

questions.text: The security team suspects that an instance EC2 within a VPC is communicating with a suspicious external IP address, but needs to confirm this by analyzing network traffic metadata (origin, destination, ports, protocol, and whether the traffic has been accepted or rejected) that enters and exits the network interfaces of the VPC — without needing to capture the content (payload) of the packages. AWS captures this type of information on network traffic in a VPC?
options: Amazon CloudWatch Logs, configured in isolation without any additional source
AWS X-Ray, tracking requests through microservices
AWS CloudTrail, which records calls from API made on account

VPC Flow Logs, which capture metadata about IP traffic entering and leaving the network interfaces of a VPC (origin, destination, ports, protocol, accepted/rejected action), without capturing the contents of the packages
questions.explanation: Right. VPC Flow Logs record metadata on IP traffic in network interfaces from VPC — including IPs and ports of origin/destiny, protocol, number of packages/bytes and whether traffic was ACCEPT or REJECT — without capturing the payload of packages.
questions.hint: Think of the resource of AWS that records metadata on IP traffic (origin, destination, port, protocol, accepted/rejected) that enters and exits the network interfaces of a VPC.
optionRationales: Right. VPC Flow Logs record metadata on IP traffic in network interfaces from VPC — including IPs and ports of origin/destiny, protocol, number of packages/bytes and whether traffic was ACCEPT or REJECT — without capturing the payload of packages.
The CloudTrail records management activity/API (who called which API), non-traffic metadata of network packages between instances.
The CloudWatch Logs is a log storage destination/service; network traffic metadata itself need to be generated by VPC Flow Logs, which can then be sent to CloudWatch Logs.
X-Ray tracks application level requests between distributed services — it does not capture raw IP traffic metadata at the level of network interfaces of the VPC.

questions.text: A company needs to enable HTTPS in one Application Load Balancer and in a distribution of CloudFront, using certificates SSL/TLS The team wants to avoid the manual process of purchasing, uploading and renewing certificates before they expire, preferring a service that provides and renews publicly reliable certificates automatically, integrating natively with these services. AWS meets this requirement?
options: AWS KMS, creating a symmetrical key to represent the certificate

AWS Certificate Manager (ACM), which automatically supplies, manages and renews certificates SSL/TLS public, integrating directly with ALB, CloudFront and other services, without additional cost for public certificates
AWS Secrets Manager, storing the certificate as a rotating secret
Make manual upload of certificates from an external certifying authority to the IAM, renewing them manually each year
questions.explanation: Correct. AWS Certificate Manager provide certificates SSL/TLS public for free, renews them automatically before maturity, and integrates natively with services such as ALB and CloudFront, eliminating manual certificate management.
questions.hint: Think of the service of AWS providing and renewing certificates automatically SSL/TLS public, with native integration to services such as the ALB and the CloudFront.
optionRationales: Correct. AWS Certificate Manager provide certificates SSL/TLS public for free, renews them automatically before maturity, and integrates natively with services such as ALB and CloudFront, eliminating manual certificate management.
The KMS manage encryption keys to encrypt data — it does not issue or manage certificates SSL/TLS for endpoints HTTPS.
This is exactly the manual process that the team wants to avoid — the ACM automates the issue and renewal of certificates.

The Secrets Manager rotates secrets as database credentials via functions Lambda — it has not been designed to issue/renew certificates TLS publicly reliable nor for native termination integration HTTPS with ALB/CloudFront.

questions.text: A company wants to ensure, at the account level and in the pocket, that no object or pocket of the Amazon S3 can be accidentally made public by a developer — even if someone incorrectly configures a ACL or bucket policy allowing public access. The team wants a centralized control that blocks this type of configuration, regardless of other policies. S3 meets this requirement?
options: Encrypt all objects with SSE-KMS
A Bucket policy that explicitly denies the main "*"
S3 Block Public Access, configured at the account and/or bucket level, which superimposes ACLs and Bucket policies to prevent resources S3 become public, even if future settings try to allow this
Enable bucket versioning
questions.explanation: Correct. S3 Block Public Access can be enabled at the account or pocket level and superimposes (replaces) ACLs and Bucket policies that attempt to grant public access, functioning as a centralized lock against accidental, current or future public settings.
questions.hint: Think about the resource of S3, configurable at account level or pocket, which superimposes (substitute) configurations of ACL and Bucket policies to prevent resources from becoming public.
optionRationales: Correct. S3 Block Public Access can be enabled at the account or pocket level and superimposes (replaces) ACLs and Bucket policies that attempt to grant public access, functioning as a centralized lock against accidental, current or future public settings.

A bucket policy denying "*" in a specific bucket may be misconfigured or simply not exist in another bucket — it does not offer overlay at account level that prevents future public settings in all bucks.
Versioning preserves the history of versions of objects — has no relation to the control of public accessibility of objects.
Encryption protects the confidentiality of data at rest, but does not prevent a bucket/object from being made publicly accessible via ACLs or Bucket Policies.

questions.text: A company uses several security services from AWS — GuardDuty, Inspector, Macie, AWS Config — each generating its own discoveries (findings) in separate consoles. The security team wants a single centralized panel that automatically adds, organizes and prioritizes the discoveries of all these services, in addition to evaluating the account's overall security posture in relation to standards such as the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. AWS meets this requirement?
options: AWS Trusted Advisor, which shows general cost and performance recommendations
Amazon CloudWatch Dashboards, manually created for each security service
AWS Organizations, setting up an audit account

AWS Security Hub, which adds, organizes and automatically prioritizes multiple service security discoveries (GuardDuty, Inspector, Macie, Config, etc.) in a centralized panel, in addition to evaluating the account against safety standards such as the CIS Benchmark
questions.explanation: Correct. AWS Security Hub automatically centralizes and correlates security discoveries of various services of AWS (GuardDuty, Inspector, Macie, Config, among others) in a single panel, in addition to continuously evaluating the account in relation to safety standards such as the CIS AWS Benchmark Foundations.
questions.hint: Think of the service of AWS which functions as a central panel that aggregates and prioritizes discoveries (findings) of other security services, such as GuardDuty, Inspector and Macie, and evaluates the count against patterns such as the CIS Benchmark.
optionRationales: Correct. AWS Security Hub automatically centralizes and correlates security discoveries of various services of AWS (GuardDuty, Inspector, Macie, Config, among others) in a single panel, in addition to continuously evaluating the account in relation to safety standards such as the CIS AWS Benchmark Foundations.
Building dashboards manually for each service requires significant manual effort and does not offer automatic aggregation, prioritization and evaluation against standards that Security Hub provides.
The Trusted Advisor provides general checks of good practice in various categories, but does not specifically aggregate the findings of GuardDuty/Inspector/Macie/Configure a unified security vision.
The AWS Organizations manages the multi-account structure and policies (such as SCPs) — it does not aggregate and prioritize, by itself, security discoveries of other services.

questions.text: A company has two accounts AWS: a "Auditory" account and a "Production" account. Auditors who have users IAM in the Audit account they need to occasionally access resources only reading in the Production account, without it being necessary to create users. IAM (with its own long-term credentials) in the Production account. IAM allows users of one account to assume temporary permissions in another account, without duplicated long-term credentials?
options: Configure a VPC Peering between the two accounts
Share the root user password of the Production account with the auditors
Create a IAM Role in the production account with a trust policy that allows the audit account to assume its AWS STS (sts:AssumeRole), granting temporary permissions only reading
Create a user IAM identical, with the same access credentials, in both accounts
questions.explanation: Correct. By creating a role in the Production account with a trust policy that trusts in the Audit account, authorized users can use sts:AssumeRole to obtain temporary credentials with the permissions defined in the role, without the need for duplicate users or long-term credentials.
questions.hint: Think of the mechanism of IAM/STS which allows a principal of an account to temporarily assume a role with permissions defined in another account, using a trust policy, without duplicated long-term credentials.
optionRationales: Correct. By creating a role in the Production account with a trust policy that trusts in the Audit account, authorized users can use sts:AssumeRole to obtain temporary credentials with the permissions defined in the role, without the need for duplicate users or long-term credentials.
This is exactly the approach of duplicate long-term credentials that the scenario wants to avoid, in addition to being a bad security practice.
Sharing root credentials is a severely inadequate security practice and violates principles of lesser privilege.
The VPC Peering connects networks at the infrastructure level — has no connection to granting permissions IAM for users to access APIs of services from AWS between accounts.

questions.text: A company wants to implement a network firewall with state-of-the-art (stateful) package inspection at the state level. VPC, capable of filtering traffic based on domain rules, intrusion signatures (IDS/IPS) and custom rules, centrally applied to multiple VPCs input/output traffic, without having to install and manage third-party firewall applications in instances EC2. What is the service of AWS meets this requirement?
options: Security Groups, applied to each instance individually
AWS Network Firewall, a state-of-the-art, managed network firewall service that allows domain filtering, domain rules, IDS/IPS and customised rules, centrally applicable to VPC traffic
Network ACLs (NACLs), configured in each sub-network
AWS WAF, directly associated with the sub-networks of the VPC
questions.explanation: Correct. AWS Network Firewall is a managed state-of-the-art package inspection service that supports domain filtering, signature rules IDS/IPS and custom rules, which can be applied centrally to the traffic of multiple VPCs, without the need to manage own applications.
questions.hint: Think about the network-managed firewall service of AWS, with inspection of packages with state, which offers filtering by domain and rules of IDS/IPS, Centrally applicable to VPCs traffic.
optionRationales: Correct. AWS Network Firewall is a managed state-of-the-art package inspection service that supports domain filtering, signature rules IDS/IPS and custom rules, which can be applied centrally to the traffic of multiple VPCs, without the need to manage own applications.
Security Groups are stateful, but operate by instance/ENI based on IP/port/protocol — they do not offer filtering by domain, signature of IDS/IPS, nor centralized inspection in multiple VPCs.
NACLs are permission/denial state rules at the sub-network level, based on IP/port/protocol — do not support domain filtering or domain signatures of IDS/IPS.

The AWS WAF operates in the application layer (HTTP/HTTPS) and is associated with resources such as ALB, API Gateway or CloudFront — it cannot be directly associated with sub-networks of VPC for general inspection of network traffic.

questions.text: A company wants to automatically evaluate its instances EC2 and images of containers stored in Amazon ECR in search of known software vulnerabilities (CVEs) and unintentional network exposure, receiving a prioritized risk report, without having to install and maintain third-party scanning tools. AWS meets this requirement?
options: Amazon Inspector, which automatically scans instances EC2 and images of containers in ECR in search of known software vulnerabilities (CVEs) and network exposure, generating priority risk reports
Amazon GuardDuty, focused on real-time threat detection log analysis
AWS Trusted Advisor, at the Basic support level
AWS Config, evaluating configuration compliance rules
questions.explanation: Correct. Amazon Inspector performs automated and continuous scanning in instances EC2 and images of containers in ECR, identifying known software vulnerabilities (CVEs) and network exposure problems, with prioritized risk reports.
questions.hint: Think of the service of AWS which automatically scans instances EC2 and container images in ECR in search of known software vulnerabilities (CVEs) and network exposure.
optionRationales: Correct. Amazon Inspector performs automated and continuous scanning in instances EC2 and images of containers in ECR, identifying known software vulnerabilities (CVEs) and network exposure problems, with prioritized risk reports.
The GuardDuty analyze activity logs (CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs, DNS) for real-time threat detection — it does not scan software vulnerabilities (CVEs) in instances EC2 or container images.
The AWS Config checks the configuration of resources against compliance rules — it does not scan vulnerabilities of software packages (CVEs)).
The Trusted Advisor at the Basic level offers a limited set of general checks of good practices, no deep scanning of vulnerabilities CVE in instances EC2 and container images.

questions.text: A company with multiple accounts AWS organized by AWS Organizations wants to prevent QUALQUER user or role in certain accounts (including administrators of these accounts) can disable the AWS CloudTrail or leaving the organisation — regardless of permissions IAM This is the first time that the Commission has been able to take a decision on the application of Article 93(2) of the Treaty. AWS Organizations allows this restriction to be applied centrally to all accounts of an organizational unit (OR)?
options: IAM Policies attached to each user administrator individually in each account

Service Control Policies (SCPs), applied to an organizational unit, which define the maximum limit of actions allowed in all accounts of this OU, even for local administrators with permissions IAM large
AWS config Rules applied to each account
Account Tags (account tags) combined with tag based policies
questions.explanation: Correct. SCPs, applied to an OR in AWS Organizations, define a ceiling of permissions that applies to TODAS the accounts of that unit, including its administrators — a SCP which he denies `cloudtrail:StopLogging` and the exit of the organization prevents these actions regardless of policies IAM local.
questions.hint: Think about the resource of AWS Organizations which defines the maximum limit of actions allowed in all accounts of an organizational unit, overlapping even with permissions IAM local administrators.
optionRationales: Correct. SCPs, applied to an OR in AWS Organizations, define a ceiling of permissions that applies to TODAS the accounts of that unit, including its administrators — a SCP which he denies `cloudtrail:StopLogging` and the exit of the organization prevents these actions regardless of policies IAM local.

This requires manual configuration per user/account, and administrators with permissions IAM The Commission has also proposed that the Member States should take measures to ensure that the Community's policies are consistent with those of the Member States. SCPs impose a roof that even local administrators can't bypass.

The rules of the AWS Config detects and reports non-compliant configurations (which may trigger remedial action), but does not NEGAM a proactive action such as disabling the CloudTrail Before it happens.
Account tags are metadata for organization and cost allocation — they do not impose an organizational permission ceiling that overlaps permissions IAM local.

questions.text: An application executed in instances EC2, within private sub-networks (no route to the internet) of a VPC, you need to call APIs from AWS Systems Manager and AWS KMS. The team doesn't want to add one NAT Gateway or expose instances to the internet only to allow such calls from API, preferring to keep all traffic within the network of AWS. What's the use of AWS allows the instances to access these APIs privately, without going through the internet?
options: Internet Gateway attached to VPC

VPC Interface Endpoints (with technology AWS PrivateLink), which create private network interfaces within the VPC to access services of the AWS (as SSM and KMS) without the traffic leaving the network of AWS
NAT Gateway, set up in a public sub-network
VPC Peering with the management account of AWS
questions.explanation: Right. VPC Interface Endpoints, based on AWS PrivateLink, create private elastic network interfaces within the VPC which allow you to directly call APIs of services from AWS, as SSM and KMS, without the traffic passing through the internet or requiring a NAT Gateway.
questions.hint: Think of the resource of AWS, based on PrivateLink, which creates private network interfaces within the VPC to access APIs of services of the AWS without going through the Internet.
optionRationales: Right. VPC Interface Endpoints, based on AWS PrivateLink, create private elastic network interfaces within the VPC which allow you to directly call APIs of services from AWS, as SSM and KMS, without the traffic passing through the internet or requiring a NAT Gateway.
One NAT Gateway directs outbound traffic to the internet — exactly what the team wants to avoid; it does not keep the traffic privately within the network of AWS.
Attach one Internet Gateway and routing traffic through it exposed the instances to/via the internet, contrary to the scenario requirement.
APIs of services of the AWS (SSM, KMS) are not reachable endpoints via VPC Peering with a 'management account' — this is not the mechanism used for private access to the APIs of the services of AWS.

questions.text: An operations team needs access to the instance shell EC2 in private sub-networks for maintenance tasks, but the company's security policy prohibits opening the door 22 (SSH) no Security Groups and forbids the use of exposed bastion hosts. The team wants a way to gain interactive access to the forum shell, with all the session registered for audit, without opening doors to the Security Groups. What's the use of AWS meets this requirement?
options: Enable EC2 Connect with the door 22 open for office IP interval
Use AWS Direct Connect to access the instances via SSH

AWS Systems Manager Session Manager, which provides access to the instance shell via the agent SSM, no need to open entry doors (such as 22) no Security Groups, with full record of the session for audit
Configure a bastion host with the door 22 open only for corporate IPs
questions.explanation: The Session Manager of the AWS Systems Manager establishes a shell session through the SSM Agent installed in the instance, without requiring open entrance doors at Security Groups, and log the entire session for audit purposes.
questions.hint: Think about the resource of AWS Systems Manager providing interactive access to the instance shell EC2 through an agent, without needing to open entry doors at Security Groups, with session log for audit.
optionRationales: The Session Manager of the AWS Systems Manager establishes a shell session through the SSM Agent installed in the instance, without requiring open entrance doors at Security Groups, and log the entire session for audit purposes.
This is exactly the open-door bastion host approach that company security policy prohibits.
That would still require opening the door. 22 no Security Group, what politics forbids.
The Direct Connect provides a dedicated network link to AWS, but access instances via SSH through it would still require the door 22 open no Security Group.

questions.text: A financial institution needs to store and use cryptographic keys in a hardware security module (HSM) dedicated, validated according to standards as FIPS 140-2, with exclusive customer control over the hardware (a AWS has no access to the key material), to meet the rigid regulatory requirements that the AWS KMS standard multi-tenant does not satisfy. What service AWS meets this requirement?
options: AWS KMS with keys managed by AWS (AWS managed keys)
AWS Secrets Manager, configured with additional encryption
AWS CloudHSM, providing hardware security modules (HSM) dedicated to the customer, validated according to FIPS 140-2, giving the customer exclusive control over the key material
Amazon S3 with SSE-C (keys provided by the customer)
questions.explanation: Correct. AWS CloudHSM provides clusters of HSM dedicated single instance, validated as FIPS 140-2, in which the customer has exclusive control over the cryptographic material — meeting regulatory requirements that the KMS multi-tenant standard does not cover.
questions.hint: Think of the service of AWS providing a hardware security module (HSM) dedicated to the customer, validated according to FIPS 140-2, for cases where the KMS standard multi-tenant is not enough.
optionRationales: Correct. AWS CloudHSM provides clusters of HSM dedicated single instance, validated as FIPS 140-2, in which the customer has exclusive control over the cryptographic material — meeting regulatory requirements that the KMS multi-tenant standard does not cover.
The AWS managed keys run in infrastructure HSM multi-tenant standard of KMS — exactly what does not meet the dedicated hardware requirement and exclusive customer control.
The Secrets Manager stores and rotates secrets, but is not a dedicated hardware security module nor provides hardware control validated as FIPS 140-2.
The SSE-C allows the customer to provide their own keys to encrypt objects in S3, but does not provide an application HSM dedicated to cryptographic storage/operations in general.

questions.text: A company wants to demand that users IAM can only perform destructive actions (such as finishing instances EC2 or delete the notes S3) if they have been authenticated using multifactor authentication (MFA) in the current session — even if the user has permissions IAM for these actions. IAM allows to condition the use of certain permissions to the presence of MFA in the sitting?
options: Store code MFA of the user in AWS Secrets Manager and validate it manually before each action
Add a condition "Condition" with the key aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent defined as true in politics IAM which grant such destructive permissions, denying the action if that condition is not met
Create a Security Group which only allows traffic of authenticated users with MFA
Require MFA only at the time of initial login on the console, without any additional configuration in the policies
questions.explanation: Right. The condition key aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent allows a policy IAM verify that the temporary credentials of the current session have been authenticated with MFA, denying destructive actions when this condition is not met, even if the user has permission for the action.
questions.hint: Think of the condition key of IAM verifying whether the current user session was authenticated with multifactor authentication, allowing to deny destructive actions if this condition is not met.
optionRationales: Right. The condition key aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent allows a policy IAM verify that the temporary credentials of the current session have been authenticated with MFA, denying destructive actions when this condition is not met, even if the user has permission for the action.
Require MFA only in the login does not restrict specific actions of API based on the use of MFA in the current session of credentials — a policy condition is needed to impose this by action.
Security Groups operate on network traffic (IP/port/protocol) and have no knowledge of the authentication context IAM, as MFA.
It's not like that. IAM evaluation MFA; policy conditions IAM can directly verify the status of MFA of the temporary credentials of the session, without the need for manual storage of codes.

questions.text: A startup is developing a mobile application and wants to offer end users registration, login (including social login via Google/Facebook) and profile management features, without needing to build and maintain their own user directory service and zero authentication. After login, the application needs to get tokens (JWT) which can be used to authorize calls to a API protected. What service AWS meets this requirement?
options: AWS IAM, creating a user IAM for each end user of the application
AWS IAM Identity Center (old AWS SSO), designed for corporate workforce authentication in accounts and applications of AWS
AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory
Amazon Cognito User Pools, a fully managed user directory that offers registration, login (including social identity providers) and issues tokens JWT for authorization of calls from API
questions.explanation: Correct. Amazon Cognito User Pools is a fully managed user directory that offers registration, login (including social identity providers like Google and Facebook) and issues tokens JWT (ID, access and refresh tokens) that can be used to authorize API calls.
questions.hint: Think of the service of AWS which provides a fully managed user directory, with registration, login (including social providers) and token issue JWT for use in APIs.
optionRationales: Correct. Amazon Cognito User Pools is a fully managed user directory that offers registration, login (including social identity providers like Google and Facebook) and issues tokens JWT (ID, access and refresh tokens) that can be used to authorize API calls.

The IAM Identity Center is designed to provide SSO employees (labour force) accessing accounts AWS and corporate applications — not for registration/login of end users of a mobile application with social providers.

The AWS Managed Microsoft AD is focused on corporate directory services (such as entering instances EC2 in a domain) — not designed for registration/login of end-users of applications with social identity providers.
Create a user IAM for each end user is an inappropriate practice, not scale, and the IAM was not designed for authentication of end users of social login applications.

questions.text: A company uses AWS Organizations to manage dozens of accounts AWS. The security team wants to make sure that TODAS calls from API made in QUALQUER account of the organisation (existing or future) are automatically registered in a single pocket S3 centralized, without needing to configure the CloudTrail individually in each account. CloudTrail meets this requirement?
options: Create a trail of CloudTrail separately in each account, pointing to the same pocket S3
Use VPC Flow Logs configured in the management account
An Organization Trail, created in the management account, which automatically applies event registration to all member accounts (existing and future), centralizing logs in a single bucket S3
Enable AWS Configure each account to record calls from API
questions.explanation: An Organization Trail, created in the management account of AWS Organizations, is automatically applied to all member accounts — including accounts created in the future — by centralizing all of their logs in a single pocket S3, without individual configuration.
questions.hint: Think about the type of trail (trail) CloudTrail, created in the management account of the AWS Organizations, which applies automatically to all existing and future member accounts.
