optionRationales: An Organization Trail, created in the management account of AWS Organizations, is automatically applied to all member accounts — including accounts created in the future — by centralizing all of their logs in a single pocket S3, without individual configuration.
This approach requires manual configuration in each account, and future accounts would not have the path automatically — does not meet the requirement for automatic application to future accounts.
The AWS config tracks changes in resource configuration over time — it does not record the full flow of calls from API (management events/data) such as CloudTrail.
The VPC Flow Logs capture network traffic metadata at the level of VPC — non-activity of calls from API between accounts.

questions.text: An application needs to encrypt large files (several gigabytes) before storing them. AWS KMS directly to encrypt the entire file is not feasible, because the KMS has a size limit for data that can be passed directly into an encryption operation (Encrypt). What encryption standard, supported by KMS, allows you to encrypt data of any size using a combination of a local data key and a master key in KMS?
options: Increase data size limit KMS through a support request

Envelope encryption (encryption envelope): or KMS generates a data key, used to encrypt the large file locally (without the size limit of KMS), and the data key itself is encrypted by KMS using the CMK is stored together with encrypted data
Disable encryption for files larger than 4 KB
Call Operation Encrypt KMS repeatedly, dividing the file into small blocks of up to 4 KB
questions.explanation: Right. In envelope encryption, or KMS generates a data key that is used locally to encrypt the file (of any size), and only that data key — small — is encrypted by CMK no KMS and stored together with the data, avoiding the size limit of the direct Encrypt operation of the KMS.
questions.hint: Think of the encryption pattern in which a data key generated by KMS is used to encrypt data locally (without size limit), while the data key itself is encrypted by the master key of the KMS.
optionRationales: Right. In envelope encryption, or KMS generates a data key that is used locally to encrypt the file (of any size), and only that data key — small — is encrypted by CMK no KMS and stored together with the data, avoiding the size limit of the direct Encrypt operation of the KMS.

Calling Encrypt repeatedly for each block of a gigabyte file would be extremely inefficient and would generate high call costs from API — the recommended standard for large data is envelope encryption..
The payload size limit of the direct Encrypt operation KMS (4 KB) is fixed and cannot be increased via support request — envelope encryption is the documented standard for larger data.
Disable encryption for large files contrary to the objective of protecting data and does not meet the requirement to encrypt them.

questions.text: A company operates several internal microservices that communicate with each other via HTTPS/mTLS within a VPC, and wants to issue certificates TLS for these internal services without exposing their internal domain names to a public certification authority, maintaining a private CA hierarchy own to issue and manage these internal certificates. AWS meets this requirement?
options: AWS Secrets Manager, generating self-signed certificates automatically
Amazon Cognito, configuring a pool of certificates
AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) standard, issuing public certificates for internal domain names

AWS Certificate Manager Private Certificate Authority (ACM Private CA), which allows to create and operate a hierarchy of private certifying authority to issue X certificates.509 for domestic remedies, without exposing them to a public CA
questions.explanation: Correct. ACM Private CA allows you to create and operate your own private certification authority hierarchy, issuing X certificates.509 for internal resources and services (including mTLS scenarios), without having to expose domain names within a public CA.
questions.hint: Think of the service of AWS which allows the operation of the own hierarchy of private certification authority (CA), issuing certificates for domestic remedies without relying on a public CA.
optionRationales: Correct. ACM Private CA allows you to create and operate your own private certification authority hierarchy, issuing X certificates.509 for internal resources and services (including mTLS scenarios), without having to expose domain names within a public CA.

The public certificates of the ACM standard require domain validation via DNS public and intended for publicly reliable endpoints — not to issue certificates for internal names without public exposure.
The Secrets Manager manages secrets such as credentials and keys to API — it does not operate a CA hierarchy or issue X certificates.509.
The Cognito is an identity/authentication service for end-users — does not have certification authority functionality for TLS between internal services.

questions.text: A company has a set of instances EC2 Rolling 24/7, with a stable and predictable use profile for the next few years 1 a 3 The team wants to significantly reduce the cost of these instances compared to the On-Demand price, in exchange for a commitment to use for a fixed period. EC2 is more suitable for this scenario?
options: On-Demand Mechanisms, paying the standard price per hour without any discount
Spot Instances, which offer the biggest discounts but can be interrupted by AWS with little warning

Reserved Instances (RIs), which offer significant discounts (up to ~75%) in relation to the price On-Demand in exchange for a commitment to use by 1 or 3 years, ideal for stable and predictable workloads
Dedicated Hosts, which offer physical servers dedicated to the client
questions.explanation: Correct. Reserved Instances offer significant discounts in exchange for a commitment to use 1 or 3 years, being the ideal choice for stable, predictable and long-term workloads, as database servers that run continuously.
questions.hint: Think of the model of precision of the EC2 which offers significant discounts in exchange for a commitment to use by 1 or 3 years, ideal for stable and predictable long-term workloads.
optionRationales: Correct. Reserved Instances offer significant discounts in exchange for a commitment to use 1 or 3 years, being the ideal choice for stable, predictable and long-term workloads, as database servers that run continuously.
The Spot Instances offer the biggest discounts, but can be claimed by AWS with little warning — inadequate for database servers that need to run continuously.
The On-Demand model offers no discount for the long-term and predictable use described, leaving significant cost savings on the table.

Dedicated Hosts meet licensing/conformity requirements that require dedicated physical hardware and are usually more expensive—not primarily a cost optimization mechanism for stable workloads in general.

questions.text: A company needs to process a large batch of video rendering every night. Processing is divided into thousands of independent tasks, and the system is already prepared to resume a task in another instance if the current instance is interrupted. The team wants to minimize the cost of computing these tasks, even if this means that some instances may be interrupted by AWS occasionally. What model of precision of the EC2 offers the largest discount for this type of work load tolerant to failures and interruptions?
options: Spot Instances, which offer discounts from up to 90% in relation to the price On-Demand, using unused computing capacity of AWS, may be interrupted with prior warning of 2 minutes
On-Demand Mechanisms Auto Scaling
Dedicated Forums, which guarantee physical hardware dedicated to the customer
Reserved Instances of 3 years, which require long-term commitment
questions.explanation: Correct. Spot Instances use idle capacity of AWS and offer the largest possible discounts (up to ~90% in relation to On-Demand), being ideal for workloads tolerant to interruptions, such as batch processing distributed in thousands of independent tasks.
questions.hint: Think of the model of precision of the EC2 which uses idle capacity of AWS with the largest possible discounts, but which can be interrupted by AWS with little warning — ideal for interrupt-tolerant loads.
optionRationales: Correct. Spot Instances use idle capacity of AWS and offer the largest possible discounts (up to ~90% in relation to On-Demand), being ideal for workloads tolerant to interruptions, such as batch processing distributed in thousands of independent tasks.
A commitment of 3 years doesn't fit well in a batch workload that could be executed intermittently, and RIs don't offer the biggest discounts available for interruption-tolerant loads.
Dedicated Forums meet compliance/insulation needs and are more expensive — they do not represent a cost minimisation choice for batch jobs that are fault-tolerant.
The On-Demand price offers no special discount — it does not minimize the cost for workloads that can tolerate interruptions, such as Spot Instances allow.

questions.text: A company stores audit logs in Amazon S3 which need to be retained by 7 years by regulatory requirement, but rarely (or never) are accessed after the first 90 days. Currently, all logs remain in the storage class S3 Standard, generating high storage costs over the years. S3 allows you to automatically move these objects to a cheaper storage class after a certain period without manual intervention?
options: Manually move objects to another bucket every month
Reduce the number of replicas of the bucket
Lifecycle policy (lifecycle policy) S3, that automatically transitions objects to cheaper storage classes (such as S3 Glacier) after a defined number of days, according to the expected access pattern
Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration in Bucket
questions.explanation: Correct. A life cycle policy of the S3 allows you to set rules that automatically transition objects to cheaper storage classes, such as S3 Glacier, after a defined number of days — suitable for long retention and rare access data, without manual intervention.
questions.hint: Think about the configuration of S3 automatically moving objects to cheaper storage classes (such as Glacier) after a defined number of days without manual intervention.
optionRationales: Correct. A life cycle policy of the S3 allows you to set rules that automatically transition objects to cheaper storage classes, such as S3 Glacier, after a defined number of days — suitable for long retention and rare access data, without manual intervention.
This is a manual process, subject to errors and operationally costly, compared to an automated life cycle policy.
Transfer Acceleration accelerates uploads/downloads in long distances — has no relation to storage class costs.
The S3 does not expose a 'number of replicas' configuration for the customer to reduce; the storage cost is determined by the storage class, not by a replica configuration.

questions.text: A company stores millions of objects in S3 whose access patterns are unpredictable and vary over time: some objects are accessed frequently for weeks and then run out of access for months, without a defined standard. The team wants to optimize storage costs automatically, moving objects between frequent and infrequent access levels based on the actual pattern of use, without defining life-cycle rules based on fixed time and without recovery rates to access data at frequent/infrequent levels. S3 meets this requirement?
options: S3 Standard-IA (Infrequent Access), configured for all objects
S3 Glacier Deep Archive, configured for all objects

S3 Intelligent-Tiering, which monitors access patterns and automatically moves objects between frequent and infrequent access levels (and optionally archiving), optimizing costs without impact of performance or recovery rates at these levels
S3 One Zone-IA, configured for all objects
questions.explanation: Correct. S3 Intelligent-Tiering monitors the access patterns of each object and automatically moves it between frequent and infrequent access levels (and optionally archival levels) based on actual use, without charging recovery rates at these levels and without requiring fixed-time life-cycle rules.
questions.hint: Think about the storage class of S3 which monitors the patterns of access to objects and moves automatically between cost levels, without the need to define life-cycle rules based on fixed time.
optionRationales: Correct. S3 Intelligent-Tiering monitors the access patterns of each object and automatically moves it between frequent and infrequent access levels (and optionally archival levels) based on actual use, without charging recovery rates at these levels and without requiring fixed-time life-cycle rules.

The S3 Standard-IA charges a recovery rate and assumes uncommon access; if some objects are accessed frequently, this would generate high recovery costs — Intelligent-Tiering automatically adapts without these rates at frequent/unreserved levels.
One Zone-IA stores data in a single area of availability (less durability against loss of AZ), still collects recovery fees and does not automatically adapt to unpredictable access patterns.
Glacier Deep Archive has recovery times measured in hours, being inadequate for objects that may need frequent access for weeks.

questions.text: The financial team of a company wants to visualize and analyse the expenditure of AWS over time, identify which services or accounts are consuming more financial resources, compare costs between periods and generate future spending forecasts based on usage history. AWS provides this visualization and analysis of historical costs and forecasts?
options: AWS Budgets, only sends alerts when a defined expenditure limit is reached or foreseen
AWS Trusted Advisor, focusing on recommendations for good practice
AWS Billing Console, showing only the current month's bill
AWS Cost Explorer, which allows to visualize and analyze patterns of expenditure and use of AWS over time, with service/account/tag filters, and generate future cost forecasts based on history
questions.explanation: Correct. AWS Cost Explorer provides interactive visualizations of expenditures and usage over time, with detailed filters by service, account, tag, among others, besides generating future cost forecasts based on historical data.
questions.hint: Think of the service of AWS dedicated to the visualization and interactive analysis of historical expenses, with filters by service/account and generation of future cost forecasts.
optionRationales: Correct. AWS Cost Explorer provides interactive visualizations of expenditures and usage over time, with detailed filters by service, account, tag, among others, besides generating future cost forecasts based on historical data.
The AWS Budgets sends alerts based on defined limits, but the wide historical visualization, detail by service/account and forecasts described are functions of the Cost Explorer.
The Trusted Advisor provides recommendations for good practice in various categories — not designed for interactive historical visualization and cost forecasting.
The collection console shows a summary of the current invoice/coverage — not the capabilities of interactive historical analysis, filters and forecasting of the Cost Explorer.

questions.text: A startup with a limited budget wants to be notified automatically by e-mail whenever the monthly expenses of AWS reach 80% of a defined limit, and if again exceeded 100% of this limit, to avoid surprises in the invoice. AWS allows you to set these expense limits and set automatic alerts when they are reached or planned to be reached?
options: AWS Budgets, which allows you to set custom expense limits (budgets) and set automatic alerts by email (or SNS) where actual or projected expenditure reaches defined percentages of the limit
AWS Organizations, configuring expenditure limits per account
Amazon CloudWatch Billing Alarms, with no configuration in AWS Budgets
AWS Cost Explorer, configuring recurring reports
questions.explanation: Correct. AWS Budgets allows you to create custom budgets (value, use, RI/Savings Plans) and set up multiple automatic alerts — for example, in 80% and 100% of the limit — sent by e-mail or SNS, based on actual or projected expenditure.
questions.hint: Think of the service of AWS dedicated to defining custom expenditure limits and sending automatic alerts when actual or projected expenditure reaches percentages of those limits.
optionRationales: Correct. AWS Budgets allows you to create custom budgets (value, use, RI/Savings Plans) and set up multiple automatic alerts — for example, in 80% and 100% of the limit — sent by e-mail or SNS, based on actual or projected expenditure.
The Cost Explorer is focused on historical expense analysis and visualization — does not provide configurable proactive limits-based alerts.

The collection alarms of the CloudWatch support only a single static limit on the total estimated collections, without percentage-based alerts and forecast that the AWS Budgets offers specifically for this case.
The AWS Organizations manages the structure of accounts and policies as SCPs — it does not, by itself, provide expenditure limit alerts; this is the role of the AWS Budgets.

questions.text: A new application uses the Amazon DynamoDB, but the team is not sure what the volume of traffic will be in the first few weeks after the launch — it can vary from almost zero to sudden and unpredictable peaks, without a defined standard. The team wants to avoid the risk of providing insufficient reading/writing capacity (causing throttling) or excessive (generating unnecessary cost), preferring to pay only for actual requests made, without having to predict or adjust capacity. DynamoDB meets this initial requirement?
options: On-Demand capacity mode, which charges for reading/writing request performed, climbing instantly to meet unpredictable traffic peaks, without need to provide capacity in advance
Use Amazon RDS in place of the DynamoDB for this case
Capacity Mode Provided with Auto Scaling configured to react only after 1 High time of use
Provisioned Capacity Mode, configured with a high fixed value of RCU/WCU 'for safety'
questions.explanation: Right. On-Demand mode of DynamoDB collects only by the reading/writing requirements actually performed and instantly scales to accommodate unpredictable peaks, eliminating the risk of throttling by undersupply or unnecessary cost by oversupply.
questions.hint: Think about the capacity mode of the DynamoDB which collects by request performed and instantly scale for traffic peaks, without need to provide capacity in advance.
optionRationales: Right. On-Demand mode of DynamoDB collects only by the reading/writing requirements actually performed and instantly scales to accommodate unpredictable peaks, eliminating the risk of throttling by undersupply or unnecessary cost by oversupply.
Providing a high fixed value 'for safety' leads to paying for unused capacity during low traffic periods — exactly the unnecessary cost that the team wants to avoid.

The Auto Scaling in the provided mode reacts to usage metrics with some delay and is more suitable for loads with at least some basic predictable standard; for a totally unpredictable load, On-Demand avoids both the risk of throttling and the need to manage scaling policies..
Changing the database engine is not related to the capacity modes of the DynamoDB and does not specifically solve the issue of dealing with unpredictable reading/writing traffic in an economic way.

questions.text: An application in instances EC2, in private sub-networks, frequently access objects in Amazon S3 through a NAT Gateway (since the private subnet has no direct route to the S3). The volume of data transferred is large, and the team realized that the data processing rates of NAT Gateway they are generating a significant monthly cost only for this traffic destined to S3. Which configuration eliminates this data processing cost from NAT Gateway specifically for traffic with the S3, without compromising the security of the private subnet?
options: Make the sub-network public and assign public IPs to fora
Increase the size (capacity) of NAT Gateway
Compress the data before sending it to S3
Create a VPC Gateway Endpoint for the S3, allowing traffic between the private sub-network and the S3 be routed directly, without going through NAT Gateway and no data processing cost
questions.explanation: Right. VPC Gateway Endpoint for the S3 adds a direct route from the private subnet to the S3 through the network of the AWS, without passing through NAT Gateway — eliminating the data processing rate of the NAT Gateway for this traffic, without exposing the sub-network to the internet.
questions.hint: Think of the resource of VPC allowing the traffic from a private sub-network to the Amazon S3 be routed directly, without going through NAT Gateway and without generating your data processing rate.
optionRationales: Right. VPC Gateway Endpoint for the S3 adds a direct route from the private subnet to the S3 through the network of the AWS, without passing through NAT Gateway — eliminating the data processing rate of the NAT Gateway for this traffic, without exposing the sub-network to the internet.

The capacity of the NAT Gateway is not configurable in this way and, even if it were, this would not eliminate the data processing rate charged for the traffic intended for S3 — is the wrong mechanism for this problem.
Making the sub-network public exposes the instances to the internet, compromising the security posture of the private sub-network, which the requirement explicitly wants to avoid.

Compression may reduce the volume of data a little bit, but does not eliminate the data collection structure of the NAT Gateway for this traffic — the Gateway Endpoint avoids the NAT Gateway completely for this traffic.

questions.text: A company maintains a development environment and tests with several instances EC2 in one Auto Scaling Group. This environment is only used by the team during business hours, Monday to Friday (8h at 19h), and it gets completely idle during nights, early mornings and weekends — but continues to generate cost of instances EC2 Connected 24/7. The team wants to reduce these costs automatically, shutting down instances outside business hours and automatically reconnecting them before the start of the file, without daily manual intervention. EC2 Auto Scaling meets this requirement?
options: Increase the minimum size of the Auto Scaling Group to ensure availability
Scheduled scaling actions, configured to reduce the desired capacity of the Auto Scaling Group (for example: 0) at 19h and restore it before 8h, on weekdays
Target tracking (target tracking) based calibration, configured on the metric of use of CPU
Migrate development environment to Reserved instances
questions.explanation: Correct. Scheduled scaling actions allow to define, in advance, recurring times to change the desired capacity of a Auto Scaling Group — reducing it to zero outside business hours and automatically restoring it before the start of the dossier without manual intervention.
questions.hint: Think about the type of action of EC2 Auto Scaling which allows to define, in advance, specific times to increase or reduce the desired capacity of a group, on a recurring basis.
optionRationales: Correct. Scheduled scaling actions allow to define, in advance, recurring times to change the desired capacity of a Auto Scaling Group — reducing it to zero outside business hours and automatically restoring it before the start of the dossier without manual intervention.

Target tracking reacts to current load metrics; a leisurely dev environment at night would CPU close to zero, but use-based target tracking would not necessarily reduce capacity to zero following a predictable daily/weekly schedule.
Increasing the minimum size keeps more instances running all the time, increasing the cost instead of reducing it during idle periods.
Reserved Instances commits the continuous payment by capacity (1-3 the opposite of what is needed here..

questions.text: After months of operation, a team realizes that its bill of AWS includes volume charges EBS which are no longer attached to any body EC2 (left over from completed instances) and by Elastic IP addresses that are not associated with any running instance. These features do not provide any value, but continue to generate cost. AWS helps to automatically identify this type of idle/unused resource, so that the team can remove it and reduce unnecessary costs?
options: Amazon Macie, identifying sensitive data in S3
Amazon CloudWatch Logs Insights, running queries about application logs
AWS Shield, protecting against DDoS attacks
AWS Trusted Advisor, in the category of cost optimization, which identifies resources as volumes EBS not attached and Elastic IPs not associated, helping the team to remove them and reduce costs
questions.explanation: Correct. AWS Trusted Advisor, in its cost optimization category, checks the account in search of idle or unused resources — as volumes EBS Unattached and Unassociated Elastic IPs — and recommends removal to reduce unnecessary costs.
questions.hint: Think of the service of AWS which, in its cost optimization category, identifies idle or unused resources — as volumes EBS Unattached and Unassociated Elastic IPs — which continue to generate collections.
optionRationales: Correct. AWS Trusted Advisor, in its cost optimization category, checks the account in search of idle or unused resources — as volumes EBS Unattached and Unassociated Elastic IPs — and recommends removal to reduce unnecessary costs.
Logs Insights consults application/operation log data — it would neither invent nor signal idle billable resources, such as volumes EBS Unattached or Unassociated Elastic IPs.
The Shield is a protection service against DDoS, not related to the identification of idle/unused resources that generate cost.
The Macie discover and classify sensitive data in S3 — without relation to the identification of idle computing/network resources that generate unnecessary cost.

questions.text: A company stores secondary copies of backups in S3 — backups that already exist elsewhere (on-premises) and can be easily regenerated/restored from the primary source if lost. These backups are rarely accessed. The team wants to reduce the cost of storing these secondary backups in S3, accepting a slightly lower level of durability (data stored in a single area of availability), since the loss of this secondary copy would not be critical. S3 offers the lowest cost for infrequent data that do not need redundancy between multiple areas of availability?
options: S3 Glacier Deep Archive, with recovery time up 12 hours
S3 Standard, which stores data redundantly in multiple areas of availability
S3 One Zone-IA (Infrequent Access), which stores data in a single area of availability at a lower cost than the S3 Standard-IA, suitable for secondary or easily recreated data
S3 Standard-IA, which also stores data redundantly in multiple areas of availability
questions.explanation: Correct. S3 One Zone-IA stores data in only one area of availability, offering a lower storage cost than Standard-IA — suitable for secondary copies or data that can be easily recreated if the area is lost.
questions.hint: Think about the storage class of S3 which reduces costs by storing data in a single area of availability (rather than multiple), suitable for secondary data that can be recreated if lost.
optionRationales: Correct. S3 One Zone-IA stores data in only one area of availability, offering a lower storage cost than Standard-IA — suitable for secondary copies or data that can be easily recreated if the area is lost.
The S3 Standard offers the highest durability/availability with multi-AZ redundancy, but at a higher cost than is required for easily recreated secondary copies.
Standard-IA offers multi-AZ redundancy with an unusual access price, but One Zone-IA offers an even lower cost for data that does not require multi-AZ redundancy, as described in the scenario.

The recovery times of the Deep Archive (hours) can be very slow depending on the need for recovery, and the question specifically seeks the class that exchanges multi-AZ redundancy at lower cost in infrequent access data — this is the One Zone-IA.

questions.text: A company uses instances EC2 of different families and sizes, in addition to functions Lambda and tasks Fargate, and its use of types of instance EC2 changes frequently as the team adopts new generations of instances or migrates workloads between families (e.g. from M5 to M6g). The team wants a commitment of expenses that offers significant discount (similar to Reserved Instances), but that remains applicable regardless of future changes in the family, size, operating system, region or even the computer service used (EC2, Lambda, Fargate). What model of commitment of precision of AWS offers this flexibility?
options: Spot Instances, without any expenditure commitment

Computer Savings Plans, which offer discounts in exchange for a commitment to spend (USD/hour) by 1 or 3 years, automatically applicable to any use of EC2 (any family/size/region/SO), Fargate and Lambda
Reserved Instances Standard RIs, linked to a specific instance type
EC2 Forum Savings Plans, requiring commitment to a family of specific instance in a region
questions.explanation: Right. Savings Plans offer discounts in exchange for an hourly expense commitment, automatically applying to the use of computing in any family/size/SO/region of EC2, in addition to Fargate and Lambda — providing the maximum flexibility between the options of Savings Plans.
questions.hint: Think of the model of Savings Plans which applies to the use of computing in general (EC2 of any family/size/region, in addition to Fargate and Lambda), instead of restricting oneself to a family of specific instances.
optionRationales: Right. Savings Plans offer discounts in exchange for an hourly expense commitment, automatically applying to the use of computing in any family/size/SO/region of EC2, in addition to Fargate and Lambda — providing the maximum flexibility between the options of Savings Plans.

The EC2 Forum Savings Plans offer slightly higher discounts, but link the commitment to a family of specific instance in a Region — not offering the flexibility between families/regions/services described.
Standard RIs are linked to a specific instance/family/region with limited flexibility for change — the opposite of the flexibility requirement.
The Spot Instances do not involve spending commitment and can be interrupted — do not offer the discount relationship for commitment sought between multiple computing services.

questions.text: A company has a function that processes, on average, a few hundred requests per day, each taking a few seconds to complete, with long periods without any requests. Currently, this function runs in an instance EC2 dedicated, connected 24 hours per day, even if it is idle most of the time. The team wants to reduce the cost of this sporadic workload, paying only for the computing time actually used during the execution of the requests, without keeping a server always connected. What architecture approach meets this requirement?
options: Use Reserved Instances for the instance EC2 Current
Migration to an instance EC2 larger, to process requests faster
Configure Auto Scaling with a minimum of 1 instance always running
Migrate the function to AWS Lambda, charge based on number of summonses and execution time (in milliseconds), without cost while there are no requests to process
questions.explanation: Correct. AWS Lambda charges based on the number of calls and the execution time in milliseconds, without generating computational cost during long periods without requests — aligning the cost directly to the actual use of a sporadic workload.
questions.hint: Think about the computer service of AWS charging on the basis of the number of calls and the execution time in milliseconds, without cost for periods without requests — ideal for sporadic and short-term workloads.
optionRationales: Correct. AWS Lambda charges based on the number of calls and the execution time in milliseconds, without generating computational cost during long periods without requests — aligning the cost directly to the actual use of a sporadic workload.
An ever-connected and larger instance would increase, rather than reduce, the cost of an intermittent workload that gets idle most of the time.
Compromise with one Reserved Instance of 1-3 years for a server that gets idle most of the time still generates continuous collections, not aligning the cost to the actual sporadic use.
Keep a minimum of 1 instance in progress 24/7 it still generates continuous computer charges, regardless of the sporadic load and few seconds.

questions.text: A website hosted in instances EC2 behind a Application Load Balancer serves large volumes of static images and files directly from the source to users around the world. The monthly output data transfer invoice (data transfer out) of AWS is high, mainly because of repeated traffic to the same static files, which rarely change. Which configuration reduces both the cost of data transfer and the load at source, by storing copies of the files closest to users and serving repeated requests without returning to the source?
options: Increase the number of instances EC2 behind the ALB
Place a distribution of the Amazon CloudFront in front of the ALB/EC2, with cache enabled for static files, serving repeated requests directly from edge locations without looking again at the origin
Reduce resolution of all images from the site in 50%
Migrate instances EC2 for a region closer to users
questions.explanation: Correct. CloudFront with enabled cache stores copies of static files in edge locations close to users, serving repeated requests without looking again at origin — significantly reducing both the cost of data transfer and the burden on origin.
questions.hint: Think of the service of CDN of AWS which stores cached copies of static files in locations (edge locations) close to users, reducing both the transfer of data from the origin and the burden on it.
optionRationales: Correct. CloudFront with enabled cache stores copies of static files in edge locations close to users, serving repeated requests without looking again at origin — significantly reducing both the cost of data transfer and the burden on origin.
Adding more instances at source increases the ability to meet requests, but does not reduce the cost of data transfer from repeatedly serving the same files to users around the world.

Reducing image resolution may slightly decrease the size of each transfer, but it does not solve the fundamental problem of repeatedly transferring the same source files to global users — the cache on the edge resolves this.

A single region still cannot be 'next' to a global user base in the way that many edge locations of the CloudFront manage, and does not reduce the cost of repeated transfers like the cache on the edge.

questions.text: A company operates a database Amazon RDS of production that runs continuously, with a stable instance configuration, and plans to keep it operating in this way by the next 3 years. The team wants to reduce the cost of computing this database instance compared to the On-Demand price, knowing that the long-term commitment is acceptable given the continuous and stable use. Amazon RDS offers this discount in exchange for a commitment to use by 1 or 3 years?
options: Read Replicas RDS, configured to reduce the cost of the main instance
RDS Performance Insights, enabled in the instance
RDS Reserved Instances, which offer significant discounts in relation to the On-Demand price in exchange for a commitment to use 1 or 3 years for a specific database instance configuration
RDS Multi-AZ, enabled to reduce costs
questions.explanation: Correct. RDS Reserved Instances offer significant discounts in relation to the On-Demand price in exchange for a commitment to use 1 or 3 years for a specific database instance configuration — ideal for production banks with continuous and stable use.
questions.hint: Think about the precision option of RDS that, as well as the Reserved Instances of the EC2, offers significant discounts in exchange for a commitment to use 1 or 3 years for a specific database instance configuration.
optionRationales: Correct. RDS Reserved Instances offer significant discounts in relation to the On-Demand price in exchange for a commitment to use 1 or 3 years for a specific database instance configuration — ideal for production banks with continuous and stable use.
Multi-AZ is a feature of high availability (it actually increases the cost as it keeps a replica in standby) — does not offer price discount for compromised use.
Reading replicas add extra instances (and cost) to distribute reading traffic — they do not offer discount on the main instance computing price.
Performance Insights is a database load monitoring/diagnosis feature, unrelated to computer price discounts for long-term commitments.

questions.text: A company wants to be automatically alerted whenever there is an unusual expense pattern/anonymous in your account AWS — for example, a sudden and unexpected increase in cost in a specific service, even if this increase did not exceed a predefined fixed budget limit. The team wants this monitoring to use machine learning to learn the normal spending patterns and detect deviations, instead of relying only on a manually configured fixed value limit. AWS meets this requirement?
options: AWS Cost Explorer, with a monthly scheduled report

AWS Cost Anomaly Detection, which uses machine learning to learn the normal cost patterns of the account and generate automatic alerts when detecting anonymous cost patterns, without depending on a fixed value limit
AWS Budgets, set with a monthly fixed value limit
Amazon CloudWatch Anomaly Detection, applied to metrics of CPU
questions.explanation: Correct. AWS Cost Anomaly Detection uses machine learning to learn the normal patterns of spending per service/account and generates automatic alerts when detecting anomalous deviations, even if these deviations do not exceed a predefined fixed budget limit.
questions.hint: Think of the resource of AWS which uses machine learning to learn the normal standards of service/account spending and generate automatic alerts when detecting an anonymous cost pattern, without depending on a fixed value limit.
optionRationales: Correct. AWS Cost Anomaly Detection uses machine learning to learn the normal patterns of spending per service/account and generates automatic alerts when detecting anomalous deviations, even if these deviations do not exceed a predefined fixed budget limit.

A budget with monthly fixed limit only alerts when total spending crosses that specific value — does not use ML to learn normal standards per service and detect anonymous deviations regardless of a fixed limit being crossed.
The CloudWatch Anomaly Detection applies ML to operational metrics (as CPU), not specifically the collection/cost data of AWS.
The Cost Explorer provides historical visualization and reports, but does not proactively use ML to detect and alert about anonymous spending patterns automatically.

questions.text: A team wants to reduce the cost of performing its functions AWS Lambda, currently running in x86 architecture_64 and are already compatible (or can be recompiled to be compatible) with the architecture ARM64, without altering the logic of the function. AWS offers a processor architecture option for functions Lambda which usually reduces the cost (price per GB-second) in relation to x86_64 for the same amount of memory configured. Which configuration reduces this cost?
options: Reduce the timeout of the function
Increase the memory allocated to the function Lambda
Migrate the function to one Lambda Layer
Configure function architecture Lambda as arm64 (AWS Graviton2), which usually offers a price per GB-second lower than x86_64 for the same memory configuration, in compatible functions
questions.explanation: Correct. Functions Lambda configured for arm64 architecture (based on processors AWS Graviton2) usually have a price per GB-second lower than x86_64 for the same amount of memory, in compatible functions, without the need to change the logic of the function.
questions.hint: Think about the processor architecture configuration of a function Lambda which, for compatible functions, usually offers a price per GB-second lower than x86_64, without changing the logic of the function.
optionRationales: Correct. Functions Lambda configured for arm64 architecture (based on processors AWS Graviton2) usually have a price per GB-second lower than x86_64 for the same amount of memory, in compatible functions, without the need to change the logic of the function.

Increasing the allocated memory increases the price component by GB-second (although in some cases it may reduce the duration) — it is not the cost reduction based on architecture that the scenario asks for.
The timeout defines how long the function can run before it is closed — does not reduce the price rate by GB-Second underlying.
Lambda Layers pack code/shared dependencies for reuse between functions — do not affect the underlying computational price rate.

questions.text: A company has dozens of buckets S3 distributed in multiple accounts and regions, and wants to obtain organizational visibility on usage metrics and storage activity — such as the growth of storage over time, the distribution between storage classes, and which buckets/prefixes are consuming more space — to identify opportunities for cost optimization on a scale, without having to consult each bucket individually. S3 provides this aggregate visibility at organizational level?
options: Amazon CloudWatch Standard Metrics of S3, without any additional configuration
S3 Inventory, set up in each individual pocket
AWS Trusted Advisor, in the performance category
Amazon S3 Storage Lens, which provides organizational visibility on usage metrics and storage activity in all pockets and accounts, with panels and recommendations for cost optimization
questions.explanation: Correct. S3 Storage Lens provides organizational panels with aggregate usage metrics and storage activity on all pockets and accounts, including distribution between storage classes and growth trends, with cost optimization recommendations.
questions.hint: Think about the resource of S3 which provides organizational panels with aggregate usage metrics and storage activity in all pockets and accounts, with cost optimization recommendations.
optionRationales: Correct. S3 Storage Lens provides organizational panels with aggregate usage metrics and storage activity on all pockets and accounts, including distribution between storage classes and growth trends, with cost optimization recommendations.
The S3 Inventory provides a list of objects and their metadata for individual buckets — not the aggregate views and organizational trends that Storage Lens offers.

The standard metrics of CloudWatch for S3 provide basic metrics per request/storage bucket, not organizational aggregate visions, storage class division and cost optimization recommendations from Storage Lens.

The performance category of the Trusted Advisor check general items of good practice — does not provide detailed usage panels and storage activity S3 at the organizational level that Storage Lens offers.

questions.text: A statess web application, tolerant of interruptions, rotates in a Auto Scaling Group. The team wants to significantly reduce the cost of computing by combining On-Demand instances (to ensure a basic capacity always available) with instances Spot (for additional capacity, with discount, during traffic peaks), automatically distributing between various types of instance to reduce the impact of interruptions Spot. What's the use of EC2 Auto Scaling allows this combination of purchase types and instance types within a single group?
options: Create Two Auto Scaling Separate groups, one totally On-Demand and one totally Spot, without any combined policy configuration
Mixed instances policy in the Auto Scaling Group, which allows to combine instances On-Demand and Spot, in addition to diversify among multiple types of instance, within a single group
Use only AWS Fargate Spot for the whole application
Configure only Reserved instances in Auto Scaling Group
questions.explanation: Correct. The mixed instances policy of a Auto Scaling Group allows to define a base capacity On-Demand combined with instances Spot additional, in addition to diversify among multiple types of instance — reducing cost and the impact of interruptions Spot, all within a single group.
questions.hint: Think about the resource of EC2 Auto Scaling which allows to combine instances On-Demand and Spot, in addition to diversify among multiple types of instance, within a single group.
optionRationales: Correct. The mixed instances policy of a Auto Scaling Group allows to define a base capacity On-Demand combined with instances Spot additional, in addition to diversify among multiple types of instance — reducing cost and the impact of interruptions Spot, all within a single group.

Managing two separate groups requires additional orchestration to balance traffic and does not offer unified basic capacity management + Spot and the diversification of types of instance that the mixed instance policy offers in a single group.
Reserved Instances represent a charge discount for compromised use of On-Demand capacity — do not offer the combination On-Demand+Spot and the diversification of the types of instance described.
The Fargate Spot is a specific precision option for containers, not a resource of a Auto Scaling Group of EC2 combining On-Demand and Spot with multiple types of instance.

questions.text: A company creates daily snapshots of its volumes EBS for backup, but old snapshots are never automatically deleted — they accumulate indefinitely, generating an ever-increasing cost of storage of snapshots over time, even if the retention policy requires only the last ones to be maintained. 30 days of snapshots. What's the use of AWS automates the creation and exclusion (based on a retention policy) of snapshots EBS, no need for custom scripts?
options: AWS Backup, configured just to create snapshots, no retention policy
Increase volume size EBS of origin
Create a function Lambda custom scheduled to run 'aws ec2 create-snapshot' daily, no exclusion logic

Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager (DLM), automating the programmed creation of snapshots EBS and the automatic exclusion of snapshots that exceed the defined retention policy (e.g., keeping only the last 30 days)
questions.explanation: Correct. Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager automates both the programmed snapshot creation EBS the automatic deletion of older snapshots that exceed the defined retention policy, eliminating the need for custom scripts and controlling the indefinite growth of snapshot storage cost.
questions.hint: Think of the resource of AWS dedicated to automate both the programmed creation and the automatic deletion of snapshots EBS, based on a defined retention policy.
optionRationales: Correct. Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager automates both the programmed snapshot creation EBS the automatic deletion of older snapshots that exceed the defined retention policy, eliminating the need for custom scripts and controlling the indefinite growth of snapshot storage cost.

The scenario explicitly requires so much creation QUANTO automatic exclusion according to a retention policy; a backup configuration without a retention policy/life cycle would not solve the accumulation of old snapshots.
This is only about creation and explicitly does not have the exclusion logic necessary to apply the retention of 30 days and interrupt the indefinite accumulation of snapshots.
Increase volume size EBS of origin does not deal with the accumulation or retention of snapshots — does not relate to the problem of the life cycle of snapshots.

questions.text: A company wants to ensure that a junior developer can list objects in a pocket S3 specific, but cannot exclude or upload new objects. What is the correct way to grant this access to the IAM?
options: Create a IAM Policy with Allow for s3:GetObject s3:ListBucket in the specific Bucket feature, and assign it to the user IAM of the developer — the absence of permission for s3:Delete s3:PutObject implicitly denies these actions
Add the developer to the group of Administrators of IAM and then use the bucket policy of S3 to restrict access — the combination of the two policies ensures correct access
Create a IAM Policy with Allow for s3:GetObject s3:ListBucket, and also Deny explicit for s3:Delete s3:PutObject — Without the explicit Deny, exclusion actions would be allowed by default
Use AWS Organizations to create a SCP which limits the developer's access to S3 — SCPs are the correct tool to control granular permissions of individual users
questions.explanation: Correct. IAM, the standard principle is 'everything denied, unless explicitly allowed'. By creating a policy with Allow only for s3:GetObject s3:ListBucket, the user can only perform these two actions — s3:Delete s3:PutObject are implicitly denied because they are not on the permission list. It is not necessary to create explicit Deny rules for what is not allowed.
questions.hint: No. IAM, what is the standard behavior for actions that have no explicit permission — Allow or Deny?
optionRationales: Correct. IAM, the standard principle is 'everything denied, unless explicitly allowed'. By creating a policy with Allow only for s3:GetObject s3:ListBucket, the user can only perform these two actions — s3:Delete s3:PutObject are implicitly denied because they are not on the permission list. It is not necessary to create explicit Deny rules for what is not allowed.

Wrong. IAM, the pattern is 'everything denied' — it is not necessary to add Deny explicitly for each unauthorized action. Actions that do not have Allow are automatically denied. Adding Deny explicitly is unnecessary in this case and can complicate the maintenance of the policy.

Incorrect. Adding to the group of Administrators would give total access to the account AWS — Then trying to narrow it down via bucket policy would be complex and prone to mistakes. The principle of the lowest privilege guides you to grant only what is needed from the beginning..

Incorrect. SCPs (Service Control Policies) are applied to accounts within a AWS Organization to set maximum allowable limits for TODA the account (or OU) — are not used to control individual user permissions within an account. IAM Policies are the correct tool for granular permissions per user.

questions.text: A company has employees who need access to AWS Console for Different Functions — Some Manage EC2, others manage S3. The team wants to organize permissions in a scalable way. What is the recommended practice in IAM to manage multiple employee permissions?
options: Assign policies directly to each user IAM individually — this ensures precise control over each person's permissions
Create a single user IAM shared for each function (e.g.: 'user-ec2', 'user-s3') and share credentials among employees of the same function — this simplifies permission management
Use Access Keys for each employee instead of console passwords — Access Keys offer more granular control of permissions per action

Create IAM Groups by function (e.g. 'EC2Admins', 'S3Readers'), assign the corresponding policies to the groups, and add users IAM to appropriate groups — users automatically inherit group permissions, facilitating scale management
questions.explanation: Correct.. IAM Groups allow you to manage multiple user permissions efficiently: a policy is assigned to the group, and all group members inherit it automatically. When an employee changes function, just move the user between groups — no individual policies need to be modified. It is the recommended practice for scalability.
questions.hint: What's the use of IAM allows users to group with the same function and apply permissions to all at once?
optionRationales: Correct.. IAM Groups allow you to manage multiple user permissions efficiently: a policy is assigned to the group, and all group members inherit it automatically. When an employee changes function, just move the user between groups — no individual policies need to be modified. It is the recommended practice for scalability.

Incorrect. Share credentials IAM among multiple employees violates the practice of individual traceability security — it is not possible to know which specific employee carried out an action if everyone uses the same credentials. IAM for audit via CloudTrail.

Incorrect as scalable practice. Assigning policies directly to individual users works for few users, but becomes complex as the team grows — each change of permission needs to be made for each user individually. IAM Groups are the recommended practice for scalability.

Incorrect. Access Keys are for PROGRAM ACCESS (CLI, SDK, APIs) — do not replace console passwords for access to the web interface. Furthermore, the type of credentials (sign vs. access key) has no relation to the granularity of permissions — this is controlled by IAM Policies independent of the type of credentials.

questions.text: A developer has set up an instance EC2 to access a pocket S3. Instead of using key accesses stored in the instance, the architect recommended a safer approach. What is the recommended practice for an instance EC2 access services AWS without using static key accesses?
options: Create a IAM Roll with the necessary permissions for the S3 and associate this role with the instance EC2 via Forum Profile — the instance automatically receives rotating temporary credentials, without the need to store key accesses
Store key accesses as environment variables in the instance EC2 — environment variables are safer than storing in configuration files
Add instance IP EC2 to the policy of pocket S3 to allow IP-based access — no need for credentials IAM
Create a user IAM specific to the application and securely store key accesses in AWS Secrets Manager, accessible by the court
questions.explanation: Correct.. IAM Roles associated with instances EC2 (via Forum Profile) are the recommended practice. (IMDS) of the instance provides temporary credentials automatically rotated by STS — no permanent key accesses stored in the instance. It is safer because there are no keys to leak or forget to rotate.
questions.hint: What recourse? IAM may be associated with an instance EC2 so that she receives credentials AWS automatic temporary without needing to store access keys?
optionRationales: Correct.. IAM Roles associated with instances EC2 (via Forum Profile) are the recommended practice. (IMDS) of the instance provides temporary credentials automatically rotated by STS — no permanent key accesses stored in the instance. It is safer because there are no keys to leak or forget to rotate.

Incorrect. Although environment variables are better than text files, they are still static long-term credentials stored in the instance — the same risk of leak exists. IAM Roles with temporary credentials are the recommended safe approach.

Partially better than storing on disk, but still unnecessarily complex. Use IAM Role + Forum Profile completely eliminates the need for access keys — does not require managing the Secrets Manager for this case. IAM Roles are the simplest and safest solution for EC2.

Incorrect. IPs of instances EC2 may change (especially in Auto Scaling), making IP-based control fragile. Besides, IP-based control is not authentication — any origin with that IP could access the pocket. IAM Roles with cryptographic authentication are the right solution.

questions.text: A security team wants to make sure no bucket S3 in the account can be made public accidentally by developers. What configuration in the Amazon S3 prevent any attempt to make a bucket or public object?
options: Enable S3 Object Ownership with 'Bucket owner reinforced' — this ensures that all objects in the bucket are owned by the owner of the bucket, preventing public access
Configure the CloudTrail to monitor and notify when a bucket is made public — the notification allows the security team to quickly reverse the change
Create a SCP no AWS Organizations which he denies s3:PutBucketPolicy for all users IAM — without being able to modify bucket policies, developers cannot make buckets public

S3 Block Public Access at the account level — by enabling all four Block Public Access settings in the account, any attempt to create a bucket policy or ACL granting public access is blocked, regardless of setting up in individual bucks
questions.explanation: Correct. S3 Block Public Access can be set to two levels: account (apply to all the bucks) or individual bucket. Enabled at the account level, no bucket or object can become public — even if a developer tries to set up a bucket policy or ACL public, the Block Public Access configuration blocks. It is the recommended centralized protection for production accounts.
questions.hint: What is the functionality of S3 can be enabled at account level to lock PREVENTIVAMENTE any configuration that would make pockets or public objects?
optionRationales: Correct. S3 Block Public Access can be set to two levels: account (apply to all the bucks) or individual bucket. Enabled at the account level, no bucket or object can become public — even if a developer tries to set up a bucket policy or ACL public, the Block Public Access configuration blocks. It is the recommended centralized protection for production accounts.

questions.text: A company wants to ensure that data stored in buckets S3 are always encrypted. What is the simplest way to ensure that TODOS the new objects in a pocket are encrypted automatically, without the customer specifying encryption in each upload?

questions.text: A company uses AWS IAM and wants to understand the difference between a IAM Identity-based policy and resource-based policy. What statement correctly describes this difference?

questions.explanation: Authentication answers the question 'Who are you?' — the IAM check the identity via credentials (password, access keys, tokens). optionRationales: Authentication answers the question 'Who are you?' — the IAM check the identity via credentials (password, access keys, tokens). Incorrect. They are distinct and sequential concepts: first the authentic system (check who you are), then authorize (check what you can do). A user may be authenticated but not authorized for a specific action — will receive an AccessDenied (403) after successful authentication.

Incorrect — concepts are reversed. Authentication = verify identity. Authorization = verify permissions. Order is also wrong: always authenticate first (who you are), then authorize (what you can do)).

Incorrect. Authentication and Authorization do not describe CREATION of resources IAM — they describe verification processes in access time. They are safety concepts that apply to each call from API performed by the user.

questions.text: A company has customer data in a database RDS which need to be encrypted by compliance requirement (LGPD). The database was created without encryption. What is the process to enable encryption in a database RDS existing?
options: Access bank settings RDS not console AWS and enable the 'Encryption' option — the encryption will be applied during the next maintenance window without downtime
Use AWS Database Migration Service (DMS) to migrate data to a new bank RDS Cryptographed — or DMS does migration without downtime and ensures that all data is encrypted in the destination
Enable encryption at the application level (application-level encryption) before storing data in the database — this is equivalent to native encryption of RDS for the purposes of compliance

Cannot enable encryption directly in a bank RDS existing without encryption — it is necessary to create a snapshot of the database, create an encrypted copy of that snapshot, and restore a new database from the encrypted copy
questions.explanation: Correct. RDS is an unchangeable configuration after creation — cannot be enabled in an existing instance directly. The correct process is: (1) create snapshot of the current bank, (2) copy snapshot with enabled encryption (selecting a key KMS), (3) restore a new bank from encrypted copy, (4) This limitation is documented by AWS.
questions.hint: Cryptography at rest of RDS is unchangeable after creation. What two-step process (snapshot + ?) is needed to have a database RDS Encrypted from a non-encrypted?
optionRationales: Correct. RDS is an unchangeable configuration after creation — cannot be enabled in an existing instance directly. The correct process is: (1) create snapshot of the current bank, (2) copy snapshot with enabled encryption (selecting a key KMS), (3) restore a new bank from encrypted copy, (4) This limitation is documented by AWS.

Incorrect. There is no option to enable encryption in a bank RDS existing via console or maintenance window. Encryption is defined at the time of CREATION and cannot be changed later — the process of creating snapshot + encrypted copy is the only way.

Partially valid as a technical alternative, but is not 'equivalent' to native cryptography of RDS for all purposes. Encryption at application level encrypts DADOS but does not protect automated backups, transaction logs, and replicas that the RDS management — which would also be encrypted by native encryption. The snapshot + encrypted copy + restoration process is the complete solution.

Correct in concept (create a new encrypted database and migrate data) but incorrect in implementation. DMS is a continuous migration tool — it would work, but it is more complex and unnecessary for this case. Creating snapshot + encrypted copy + restoration is simpler and more direct to migrate to RDS encrypted.

questions.text: A company wants to understand what the AWS CloudTrail. IT manager asks, 'How do we know who deleted a bucket? S3 last week?' Which service would provide that information?

AWS Config — maintains a configuration history of all resources, allowing you to see who created and deleted resources over time
Amazon Inspector — performs account security assessments and detects when resources are deleted without authorization

AWS CloudTrail — records all calls from API made on account AWS, including who called, when, where (IP), what action was executed, and in what recourse — is the audit log that allows you to determine who deleted the bucket S3 and when
questions.explanation: Correct. CloudTrail records management events such as DeleteBucket, including: user/role who made the call (userIdentity), timestamp, IP of origin, region, and status of the request. It is the audit service of 'who did what and when' in AWS. By default, management events are retained by 90 days at CloudTrail event history.
questions.hint: What service AWS records all calls from API (including who called, when, and from where), being the account's 'audit log'?
optionRationales: Correct. CloudTrail records management events such as DeleteBucket, including: user/role who made the call (userIdentity), timestamp, IP of origin, region, and status of the request. It is the audit service of 'who did what and when' in AWS. By default, management events are retained by 90 days at CloudTrail event history.

Partially correct on the S3 Server Access Logging record ticket access events, but the S3 Server Access Logging Goes to Another Bucket S3 (no CloudWatch), and is separated from CloudTrail. For the question 'who deleted the bucket', the CloudTrail Management Events is the correct record — because the exclusion of BUCKET in itself is a call from API Management.
Incorrect. Amazon Inspector evaluates vulnerabilities in instances EC2, containers and functions Lambda — is not a log audit of shares and calls from API. Doesn't record who deleted a bucket S3.

Partially correct about tracking resource configuration changes, but AWS Config tracks changes in ESTADO of resources (e.g., 'this bucket existed and now does not exist'), not necessarily QUEM did the action via what call API. questions.text: A company is developing an application that needs to share a key to API with third parties so that they can use their services. AWS Key Management Service (KMS) — store the key API directly in KMS as key material
AWS Secrets Manager — store secrets (keys of API, passwords, tokens) encrypted, controls access via IAM Police, records every access to CloudTrail for audit, and supports automatic secret rotation

questions.explanation: Correct. questions.hint: What service AWS it was created specifically to store secrets (passwords, keys of API, tokens) securely, with automatic rotation support and audit?
optionRationales: Correct. Secrets Manager is designed exactly to store secrets (API keys, credentials, tokens) with: encryption via KMS, granular access control via IAM, Audit via CloudTrail of each access to the secret, and automatic rotation option. However, for keys of API with audit and automatic rotation requirements, Secrets Manager has richer functionalities (native rotation, audit of access to secrecy via CloudTrail specific). Parameter Store SecureString is more basic.

Incorrect. KMS management CHAVES OF CRIPTOGRAFIA (to encrypt and decrypt data) — is not a safe to store secrets as key API. The KMS is often used for CRIPTOGRAFAR secrets stored in Secrets Manager, but the two have different functions.

questions.text: One company found out that a former employee still has credentials IAM active and could access the account AWS After his resignation, what are the steps? IMEDIATOS which the administrator must take to revoke access to that user?

Disable or delete Access Keys from user IAM And disable the console password (or delete the user) immediately — active credentials (both access keys and console password) must be revoked to remove all access paths
Just remove the user IAM of groups IAM — without being part of groups, the user loses the inherited policies and can no longer perform actions in the account
Create a SCP no Organizations which blocks the user by name — SCPs may deny users access IAM specific by ARN
questions.explanation: Correct. To completely revoke the access of a former employee, it is necessary to eliminate TODOS the access paths: (1) Disable/delete Access Keys (programming access), (2) Disable/delete console password (web access). Ideally, delete user IAM also check if the user has roles that he or she can assume or active sessions.
questions.hint: There are two types of credentials IAM which allow access to the AWS — console password and program key accesses. What happens if only one of them is disabled?
optionRationales: Correct. To completely revoke the access of a former employee, it is necessary to eliminate TODOS the access paths: (1) Disable/delete Access Keys (programming access), (2) Disable/delete console password (web access). Ideally, delete user IAM also check if the user has roles that he or she can assume or active sessions.

Incomplete and potentially dangerous. Removing from groups removes inherited permissions from groups, MAS the user may still have policies IAM attached directly, and their credentials (keys access and password) would still be valid — someone with these credentials could try to invoke APIs. Disabling/deleteing credentials is the essential step.

Incorrect. Changing the password prevents access to CONSOLE, But the Access Keys are INDEPENDENTES A former employee with key accesses could still use the CLI/SDK to access the account even with the modified console password. Both credentials need to be revoked..

Incorrect. SCPs apply to entire accounts/OUs within an Organization — not to users IAM individual ARN user. The revocation of a user's access IAM specific should be done via IAM (Disable credentials, remove police, or delete user).

questions.text: A company uses Amazon VPC and wants to control network traffic between their internal sub-networks. Security Groups, which network control mechanism operates at the sub-network level (not the instance))?
options: Network Access Control Lists (NACLs) — apply entry and exit rules at the sub-network level, evaluating each (stateless) package in the numerical order of the rules, before traffic reaches the instances
VPC Endpoints — control which sub-networks can access services AWS specific, blocking traffic for unauthorized services
Route Tables — route tables control traffic between sub-networks, allowing or blocking communication based on configured destinations
Internet Gateway — filter the internet input traffic before it reaches the subnets, operating as a perimeter firewall of VPC
questions.explanation: Correct.. NACLs are firewalls at the sub-network level, complementing the Security Groups (level of instance). NACLs are statesss (each direction evaluated independently), evaluate rules in numerical order (first correspondence wins), and apply to any traffic that enters or exits the sub-network.
questions.hint: What network traffic control mechanism operates at the sub-network level (non-instance) and is statesss — different from Security Groups?
optionRationales: Correct.. NACLs are firewalls at the sub-network level, complementing the Security Groups (level of instance). NACLs are statesss (each direction evaluated independently), evaluate rules in numerical order (first correspondence wins), and apply to any traffic that enters or exits the sub-network.

Incorrect. Route Tables ROTEIAM traffic (determine where packages go) — do not block or allow traffic based on port/protocol rules like a firewall. Route Tables can redirect traffic to a Internet Gateway, NAT Gateway, VPN, etc., but they are not a safety control mechanism like NACLs.

Incorrect. VPC Endpoints create private connections between the VPC and services AWS specific (as S3, DynamoDB) without going through the internet — they are not a firewall mechanism to control traffic between sub-networks. VPC Endpoints is managed by endpoint policies, not by port/protocol rules.

Incorrect. Internet Gateway is a routing component that connects the VPC to the internet — does not filter traffic with port/protocol rules. There is no user-configurable access control list. Traffic control is done by Security Groups and NACLs.

questions.text: A company wants to use the AWS Configure to monitor if Security Groups The account has the door 22 (SSH) open to the world (0.0.0.0/0). What is the purpose of AWS Configure in this context?
options: The AWS Config continuously evaluates resource settings AWS against defined rules (such as 'restricted-ssh') and reports which resources are in compliance or not — is a control DETECTIVO which identifies incorrect settings, not a preventive control that blocks the action
The AWS Config performs daily a sweep of all the Security Groups and send a weekly security report by e-mail to compliance team
The AWS Config proactively blocks any attempt to create Security Groups with door 22 open for 0.0.0.0/0 — is a preventive control that prevents incorrect settings
The AWS Config is the tool for CRIAR the rules of Security Group — works as a centralized firewall rule editor for the entire account
questions.explanation: Correct. AWS Configur continuously monitors and evaluates resource settings. The restricted-ssh managed rule detects Security Groups with door 22 open for 0.0.0.0/0 and mark as 'NON_COMPLIANT'. It is a detective control — reports the problem but does not prevent the configuration from occurring. It can be complemented with automatic remediation to fix automatically.
questions.hint: The AWS Is config a detective or preventive control? It blocks actions or just checks and reports the status of settings?
optionRationales: Correct. AWS Configur continuously monitors and evaluates resource settings. The restricted-ssh managed rule detects Security Groups with door 22 open for 0.0.0.0/0 and mark as 'NON_COMPLIANT'. It is a detective control — reports the problem but does not prevent the configuration from occurring. It can be complemented with automatic remediation to fix automatically.

Incorrect. AWS Config is a control DETECTIVO — detects and reports configurations after they occur. It does not block real-time actions. To proactively block (preventive control), they would be necessary SCPs (no Organizations) or permissions IAM which deny the creation of Security Groups with specific rules.

Incorrect about the interval. AWS Config evaluates resources CONTINUAMENTE, not only daily — it is triggered by change-triggered configuration changes or periodically. Reports are not sent automatically by email — the results are visible on the console, integible with Security Hub, and notifications can be configured via SNS/EventBridge.

Incorrect. AWS Configure MONITORA existing resource settings — is not a tool to create or modify Security Groups. To create/modify Security Groups, use console EC2, CLI or SDK. config only checks if existing settings are in accordance with the rules defined.

questions.text: A company uses Amazon IAM and want to understand the concept of 'less privilege'. What better statement describes this principle in the context of the IAM?
options: Allowing access only to resources that have the tag 'Environment: Production' — production resources with more privilege are limited to those who have the correct tag
Ensuring that all users have the same permissions to facilitate management — uniform permissions is the implementation of the lowest privilege
Revoking all user permissions at the end of each day and requiring new requests daily — this ensures that no access is maintained beyond what is necessary for each session

Grant each user, role or service only the minimum permissions necessary to perform their specific tasks — without extra permissions 'to facilitate in the future' — limiting the impact if credentials are compromised
questions.explanation: Right. The principle of the smallest privilege means giving exactly what is needed and nothing else. If a developer needs to just list objects from a specific bucket, give permission to S3 Full Access would be a violation of this principle. This limits the 'blast radius' (potential damage) if credentials are compromised — the attacker would have access only to the minimum.
questions.hint: The principle of the lowest privilege is over QUANTIDADE permissions — which means 'minimum required' in the context of user functions and tasks?
optionRationales: Right. The principle of the smallest privilege means giving exactly what is needed and nothing else. If a developer needs to just list objects from a specific bucket, give permission to S3 Full Access would be a violation of this principle. This limits the 'blast radius' (potential damage) if credentials are compromised — the attacker would have access only to the minimum.

Incorrect. Matching permissions from all users to the highest common denominator would result in excessive permissions for most — the opposite of the lowest privilege. Each function should have only what it needs for its specific task.

Incorrect. Less privilege is not about which resources can be accessed by tag — it's about limiting actions and RECURSOS to the minimum necessary for each specific identity. Tags can be used as PARTE implementation of less privilege, but do not define the principle.

Incorrect. Less privilege does not mean to revoke and re-grant daily — it means to set the minimum scope of permissions that the user needs for his or her function. Repealing daily would be operationally unfeasible without adding significant security.

questions.text: A company uses Amazon S3 and wants to ensure that only its internal organization can access the objects of a pocket, but that users within the organization can access without having to authenticate themselves individually in the S3. Using aws:SourceIp, only IPs in the specified range can access. This restricts network-based access without requiring each internal user to have credentials IAM individual for S3.

optionRationales: Right. Bucket Policies may include conditions based on the source network. Using aws:SourceVpc, only requests that go through a VPC specific (or VPC Endpoint) are allowed. Using aws:SourceIp, only IPs in the specified range can access. This restricts network-based access without requiring each internal user to have credentials IAM individual for S3.

In addition, Presigned URLs grant access to a SPECIFIC object for a limited time — not suitable for general access to a newsletter by the organization.

Correct as functionality, but is not the most direct example for the beginner. S3 Access Points with VPC configuration is a valid and more modern approach, but the statement asks for the simplest way to restrict network access. aws:SourceVpc/SourceIp is the most directly taught approach at the beginner level.

questions.text: A company has a web application in EC2 and wants to ensure that, if one instance fails, another is automatically initiated to maintain capacity. AWS creates and manages instances automatically EC2 to keep a desired number of instances running?

Amazon EC2 Spot Instances — when an instance Spot is closed by AWS, a new instance Spot is automatically launched to replace it without user intervention
AWS Elastic Beanstalk — Automatically manage the infrastructure EC2, replacing failed instances without additional configuration

Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling — monitors the status of the instances and, when an instance is marked as unhealthy or closed, automatically replaces a new instance from a Launch Template, maintaining the desired number (desired capacity))
questions.explanation: Correct. EC2 Auto Scaling it is the service that maintains the desired capacity. If an instance fails in health checks, the Auto Scaling the brand as unhealthy, closes and launches a new one to replace. The Launch Template (or Launch Configuration) defines the features of the new instance. (AMI, type, SG, etc.).

optionRationales: Correct. EC2 Auto Scaling it is the service that maintains the desired capacity. If an instance fails in health checks, the Auto Scaling the brand as unhealthy, closes and launches a new one to replace. The Launch Template (or Launch Configuration) defines the features of the new instance. (AMI, type, SG, etc.).

Incorrect. CloudWatch Alarms detect metrics out of the ordinary and can trigger actions (via SNS, Lambda, or Auto Scaling police), but in themselves do not create or replace instances. Incorrect. Spot Instances are types of instances with lower price that can be closed by AWS when capacity is required — are not automatically replaced by default.
