questions.text: A company has a database RDS MySQL and wants to maximize availability. They want that if the database instance fails, the application automatically reconnects with the minimum downtime. RDS It's designed for that.?
options: RDS Read Replica — creates a read-only copy of the bench in another AZ; in case of primary failure, Read Replica is automatically promoted the new primary instance
RDS Proxy — the proxy is in front of the database and automatically redirects connections to a new instance if the primary fails

RDS Multi-AZ — o RDS automatically creates a synchronous replica in a different AZ; in the event of failure of the primary instance, the RDS does failover automatically for the standby replica (usually in less than 2 minutes) with automatic update of the endpoint DNS
RDS Automated Backups — Automatic backups ensure that, in case of failure, the seat is automatically restored to the latest state with minimal downtime
questions.explanation: Correct.. RDS Multi-AZ is a feature of high availability: it keeps an exact copy (synchronous) of the bank in another AZ. In case of failure (hardware, AZ, or maintenance), the RDS automatically promote standby to primary and update the endpoint DNS. The application uses the same endpoint — reconnects to the new primary automatically.
questions.hint: What is the functionality of RDS maintains a SINCRON copy of the seat in another AZ and performs automatic failure without manual intervention?
optionRationales: Correct.. RDS Multi-AZ is a feature of high availability: it keeps an exact copy (synchronous) of the bank in another AZ. In case of failure (hardware, AZ, or maintenance), the RDS automatically promote standby to primary and update the endpoint DNS. The application uses the same endpoint — reconnects to the new primary automatically.

Incorrect. Read Replicas are to scale LEITURA — distributes the load of reading queries. They use ASSINCRONA replication and are not automatically promoted in case of failure. Multi-AZ uses synchronous replication and automatic failover. A Read Replica can be promoted manually, but is not the mechanism of high automatic availability.

Incorrect. Automated Backups allow point-in-time RESTORATION (create a new bank from a backup) — it is not automatic failover. Restore a backup takes time (depending on the size of the bank) and requires manual intervention. Multi-AZ is the high availability automatic failover mechanism.

Partially useful but not the primary mechanism of HA. RDS Proxy is mainly for pooling connections (reducing overhead connections Lambda/serverless), does not replace Multi-AZ as a failover mechanism. Proxy can be useful in conjunction with Multi-AZ to speed up connections, but Multi-AZ is the direct HA functionality.

questions.text: A company uses Amazon S3 to store critical business data. A manager asks the architect about the durability of S3 — i.e., what is the chance of losing a stored object. Amazon S3?
options: Amazon S3 Standard has durability of 99.99% (4 nines) — this means that rare but possible data loss may occur, and regular snapshots are recommended for additional backup
Amazon S3 Standard-IA has durability of 99.999999999% (11 nine), but S3 Standard has lower durability than 99.99% not using geographical redundancy

Amazon S3 Standard has durability of 99.999999999% (11 — this means that, on average, an object stored in S3 is likely to be 0.000000001% if lost per year, equivalent to approximately 1 loss in 10 trillions of objects per year
Amazon S3 does not provide numerical guarantees of durability — durability depends on the storage class and number of redundancies configured by the user
questions.explanation: Correct. S3 Standard (and most classes S3) has durability of 99.999999999% (11 This is achieved by automatically replicating data on multiple devices in multiple locations within a region. It is considered practically impervious in practical terms..
questions.hint: The durability of S3 It's famous for having how many new' (9and what does that percentage mean in practical terms??
optionRationales: Correct. S3 Standard (and most classes S3) has durability of 99.999999999% (11 This is achieved by automatically replicating data on multiple devices in multiple locations within a region. It is considered practically impervious in practical terms..

Incorrect. 99.99% (4 nine) is the monthly availability of S3, not durability. The durability (probability of not losing data) is 99.999999999% (11 9) — much higher. Availability and durability are different concepts: availability = service is accessible; durability = data will not be lost.

Incorrect. AWS provides SLA of explicit durability for the S3: 99.999999999% for S3 Standard. Durability is not configured by the user — it is guaranteed by the multi-device internal multi-location architecture of S3.

Incorrect. S3 Standard S3 Standard-IA have the same durability as 99.999999999% (11 The difference between these classes is in availability and cost — not durability. Both replicate data in multiple locations within the region..

questions.text: A company has a web application and wants to distribute traffic among multiple instances EC2 to prevent a single instance from being overloaded. AWS performs this load distribution?
options: Amazon Route 53 — the service DNS distributes traffic between instances EC2 using round-robin DNS, sending alternate requests for each instance IP
Amazon VPC with multiple AZs sub-networks — the simple presence of instances in different sub-networks makes the AWS route them automatically to distribute traffic
Amazon CloudFront — distributes traffic between instances EC2 in different regions AWS, using the edge location closest to the user to route to the correct instance

Elastic Load Balancing (ELB) — distributes the inward traffic between multiple destinations (instances) EC2, containers, IPs) based on configurable rules, continuously checking the health of instances and sending traffic only to healthy ones
questions.explanation: Correct. ELB is the load balancing service of AWS. It receives customer requests and distributes them among registered instances (target group). Monitors the health of instances via health checks and stops sending traffic to unhealthy instances. It exists in three types: ALB (layer 7/HTTP), NLB (layer 4/TCP), and GWLB.
questions.hint: What service AWS it was created specifically to receive customer traffic and distribute it among multiple servers (instances of EC2), checking which ones are healthy?
optionRationales: Correct. ELB is the load balancing service of AWS. It receives customer requests and distributes them among registered instances (target group). Monitors the health of instances via health checks and stops sending traffic to unhealthy instances. It exists in three types: ALB (layer 7/HTTP), NLB (layer 4/TCP), and GWLB.

Partly possible (Route 53 has routing policies such as Weighted or Round Robin), but is not the answer to 'load balancing between instances EC2'. Route 53 level route DNS — does not check real-time health as the ELB, has no detailed instance health checks, and the customer DNS can cache the IP even if the instance becomes inactive. ELB is the specific load balancing service.

Incorrect. CloudFront It's a CDN (Content Delivery Network) which distributes static and dynamic content using edge locations — is not a load balancer between instances EC2 in the same region. CloudFront can use one ELB as origin, but does not replace the ELB for load distribution between instances.

Incorrect. Having instances in multiple AZs or different sub-networks does not automatically distribute traffic — each instance still has its own IP and URL separate. ELB (or Route 53 with routing policies) to distribute traffic between instances. Sub-networks in multiple AZs is a practice of HA, but requires a mechanism of traffic distribution above.

questions.text: A company uses Amazon RDS and want to understand the difference between Multi-AZ and Read Replica. A junior developer asks: 'When should I use Multi-AZ and when should I use Read Replica?' What answer is more accurate?
options: Multi-AZ and Read Replica do the same — both create copies of the bank that can receive read traffic and do automatic failover; the difference is that Multi-AZ is more expensive by using synchronous replication

Multi-AZ is for ALTA DISPONIBILIDADE (automatic failover, minimize downtime in failures) — the standby replica does not accept read traffic; Read Replica is for PERFORMANCE reading (scalar wantes) SELECT) — may be in another region but has no automatic failure
Read Replica should be used when the application needs high availability (failover), because a Read Replica is automatically promoted to primary in case of failure
Multi-AZ should be used when the application has many reading queries that are overloading the primary bench — the stand absorbs readings
questions.explanation: Correct. Multi-AZ: synchronous replication, standby replica does not accept read connections (it 100% to failover), automatic failover, even endpoint. Read Replica: asynchronous replication, accepts asynchronous SELECT (can relieve primary load), can be promoted manually, can be cross-region. They are complementary — many architectures use both: Multi-AZ for HA + Read Replicas for Scaling Reading.
questions.hint: Multi-AZ is for what purpose (HA or reading performance)? Read Replica is for what purpose? The replica of each accepts reading traffic?
optionRationales: Correct. Multi-AZ: synchronous replication, standby replica does not accept read connections (it 100% to failover), automatic failover, even endpoint. Read Replica: asynchronous replication, accepts asynchronous SELECT (can relieve primary load), can be promoted manually, can be cross-region. They are complementary — many architectures use both: Multi-AZ for HA + Read Replicas for Scaling Reading.

Incorrect. Multi-AZ and Read Replica have distinct purposes: Multi-AZ = HA/failover (reply standby does not accept reading), Read Replica = scalar reading (accepts queries from SELECT). The difference is not just cost — it is the case of completely different use.

Incorrect. Read Replicas DO NOT fail automatic — they need to be promoted manually. To fail automatic, Multi-AZ is the right mechanism. Read Replicas are for readability, not for high automatic availability.

Incorrect. The Multi-AZ standby does not accept reading queries — it is exclusive to failover. To distribute reading queries, Read Replicas are the solution. Multi-AZ is for availability in case of failure, not for reading scalability.

questions.text: A company has a critical application in EC2 They want the application to be available even if an entire Availability Zone (AZ) fails. What is the basic architecture recommended to tolerate failure of an AZ?
options: Using Dedicated Hosts instances in a single AZ — dedicated hardware instances are more reliable and not inaccessible if AZ has capacity problems

Introduce instances EC2 at least 2 Different availability zones within the same region, with a Application Load Balancer distributing traffic between them — if an AZ fails, the ALB Automatically redirect 100% from traffic to healthy AZ instances
Implanting all instances in the same AZ but in different sub-networks — different sub-networks within an AZ provide sufficient insulation against infrastructure failures
Create daily snapshots of instances EC2 and have an automated process to restore from snapshots in another AZ if the primary AZ fails — the restoration time is minutes
questions.explanation: Correct. Multi-AZ with ALB is the basic architecture of regional resilience. ALB monitors the health of the instances in each AZ and, if an AZ becomes unavailable, routes all traffic to the instances in the remaining AZs. This is called 'Multi-AZ deployment' or tolerance to AZ failures.
questions.hint: To tolerate failure of an entire AZ, the instances must be distributed in how many AZs, and which service distributes traffic between them automatically?
optionRationales: Correct. Multi-AZ with ALB is the basic architecture of regional resilience. ALB monitors the health of the instances in each AZ and, if an AZ becomes unavailable, routes all traffic to the instances in the remaining AZs. This is called 'Multi-AZ deployment' or tolerance to AZ failures.

Incorrect. Different sub-networks within the MESMA AZ does not provide tolerance for AZ failure. A Availability Zone is composed of one or more physical centers — if all AZ falls (energy disaster, for example), all instances in all subnets of that AZ are inaccessible. DISTINTAS.

Incorrect. Dedicated Hosts ensure that the instances run on physical hardware dedicated to the client (useful for compliance/licensing), but do not provide tolerance for AZ failure. If AZ fails, the instances in Dedicated Hosts in that AZ also become inaccessible. Multi-AZ is required for tolerance for AZ failure.

Incorrect for 'cannot have downtime'. Restore from snapshots takes time (create new instance, apply snapshot, register in LB) and results in downtime. For critical applications without downtime, architecture must have capacity ATIVA in multiple AZs — do not depend on reactive restoration.

questions.text: A company is learning about the shared responsibility model of AWS. In the context of resilience and backup, which is the responsibility of CLIENTE, and not from AWS?
options: Configure application data backups (e.g. enable RDS Automated Backups, create snapshots of EBS, configure S3 Replication) — a AWS provides the tools, but the client must configure them and set the retention policies for their own data
Ensuring the availability of regions AWS — the customer must monitor the AWS Service Health Dashboard and hire engineers from AWS to fix regional failures quickly
A AWS is responsible for TUDO Resilience — the customer only needs to use the services; AWS automatically backups, replication and recovery

Maintain physical redundancy of servers in data centers AWS — the customer must hire the AWS Support Enterprise to ensure that servers hosting your instances are replaced quickly in case of hardware failure
questions.explanation: Correct. AWS is responsible for the physical infrastructure (hardware, network, datacenters) and the durability of the storage platform (S3 has 99.999999999% durability). However, the data backup configuration of the APPLICATION — enable snapshots, set frequency, set retention, test restoration — is the responsibility of CLIENTE. A AWS does not backup client data automatically without configuration.
questions.hint: In the shared responsibility model, who configures and manages application data backups — AWS or the customer?
optionRationales: Correct. AWS is responsible for the physical infrastructure (hardware, network, datacenters) and the durability of the storage platform (S3 has 99.999999999% durability). However, the data backup configuration of the APPLICATION — enable snapshots, set frequency, set retention, test restoration — is the responsibility of CLIENTE. A AWS does not backup client data automatically without configuration.

Incorrect. The physical redundancy of data centers (hardware, energy, cooling, network) is 100% responsibility of the AWS — The customer has no visibility or control over which physical hardware his instances run. AWS Support doesn't change that responsibility.

Incorrect. The availability of regions and AZs AWS is the responsibility of the AWS — the customer cannot intervene in infrastructure failures of the AWS. The customer can PROJETAR for multi-region resilience, but is not responsible for maintaining the regions AWS operational.

Incorrect. The shared responsibility model clearly defines: AWS takes care of the underlying infrastructure; or CLIENTE takes care of the configuration of your resources, data, backups and resilience architecture (multi-AZ, multi-region, backup policies). Leave everything to the AWS would result in data without backup and default settings that may not meet business needs.

questions.text: A company wants its application to be resilient to hardware failures in EC2. The architect mentioned 'EC2 Auto Scaling Group'. What is the basic configuration of a Auto Scaling Group which ensures that at least 2 instances are always running?
options: Use EC2 Spot Instances with 'Auto Recovery' enabled — Auto Recovery from AWS detect hardware failures and automatically migrate the instance to new hardware
Configure the Auto Scaling Group with Maximum Capacity = 2 — the maximum number guarantees that exactly 2 instances are always running

Configure the Auto Scaling Group with Minimum Capacity = 2 e Desired Capacity = 2 — o Auto Scaling always keeps at least the minimum number (minimum) and tries to keep the desired number (desired), replacing instances failures to never stay below the minimum
Configure one CloudWatch Alarm that detects when the number of instances falls below 2 and shoot a script Lambda to launch new instances manually
questions.explanation: Right. Auto Scaling Group has three capacity parameters: Minimum (never falls below that), Maximum (never rises above that), and Desired (meta that the ASG Try to maintain). With Minimum=2, o Auto Scaling ensures that there will always be at least 2 instances — if one fails, a new one is launched to keep the minimum.
questions.hint: One Auto Scaling Group has three capacity parameters. Which one ensures that the number of instances NUNCA falls below a minimum value?
optionRationales: Right. Auto Scaling Group has three capacity parameters: Minimum (never falls below that), Maximum (never rises above that), and Desired (meta that the ASG Try to maintain). With Minimum=2, o Auto Scaling ensures that there will always be at least 2 instances — if one fails, a new one is launched to keep the minimum.

Incorrect. Maximum Capacity defines the TETO (o ASG Never climb above that) — does not guarantee that there will always be 2 With Maximum=2 and Minimum=0 or Desired=1, there may be moments with only 1 In order to guarantee PELO MENOS 2, the correct parameter is Minimum Capacity = 2.

Incorrect as recommended practice. Auto Scaling Group already monitors and maintains capacity automatically — no need to create alarms + Lambda For that, the combination CloudWatch Alarm + Lambda for instance recovery would be a much more complex and slow architecture than simply setting the Minimum in ASG.

Partially incorrect. EC2 Auto Recovery is to recover individual instances (migrate to new hardware), not to guarantee a minimum number of instances running. In addition, Auto Recovery does not work with Spot Instances. Auto Scaling Group with Minimum Capacity is the right mechanism to always keep N active instances.

questions.text: A company uses Amazon S3 to store important documents. They accidentally deleted a critical file. The administrator wants to know how to recover the deleted file. What functionality of the S3 allows you to recover accidentally deleted objects?
options: S3 does not maintain deletion history — once deleted without backup, the object cannot be recovered; the client must maintain external backups for recovery
S3 Object Lock — protects objects against accidental deletion by preventing any version of the object from being deleted during the configured retention period

S3 Versioning — when enabled in the pocket, or S3 preserves old versions of objects; an exclusion does not physically remove the object but creates a 'delete marker'; it is possible to recover the previous version by listing the versions and deleting the marker delete
S3 Cross-Region Replication — Automatically replicates deleted objects from one region to another, operating as automatic backup
questions.explanation: Correct.. S3 Versioning is the protection feature against accidental deletion. With enabled versioning: when you delete an object, the S3 creates a 'marker delete' instead of physically removing; the old versions remain. To recover: list versions of the object, delete the marker delete, and the previous version returns to the current version.
questions.hint: What is the functionality of S3 keeps historical versions of objects and allows you to recover deleted objects (via 'delete markers'')?
optionRationales: Correct.. S3 Versioning is the protection feature against accidental deletion. With enabled versioning: when you delete an object, the S3 creates a 'marker delete' instead of physically removing; the old versions remain. To recover: list versions of the object, delete the marker delete, and the previous version returns to the current version.

Incorrect. S3 Cross-Region Replication copies objects from a original bucket to a destination bucket in another region — does not 'recover' deletions. By default, deletion operations (delete markers) are also replicated to the destination region., S3 Versioning in the destination pocket is the correct mechanism.

Partially correct as a mechanism PREVENTIVO, but not used to recover deleted objects. S3 Object Lock (WORM) prevents deletion FUTURA during the retention period — you cannot recover what has already been deleted before the lock is configured. To recover an already deleted object, you need to have Versioning enabled ANTES of the deletion.

Incorrect. S3 has Versioning exactly for this purpose — maintain previous versions, allowing for recovery of accidental deletions. ANTES of the deletion, recovery is possible. That's why enabling Versioning in bulkes with critical data is a recommended practice.

questions.text: A company has an architecture with EC2 Auto Scaling and ALB. They realized that on Friday night traffic always increases a lot and want to prepare capacity before peak to avoid degradation. Auto Scaling is ideal for this predictable scenario?
options: Target Tracking Scaling — defines a target metric (ex.: CPU = 50%) and the Auto Scaling automatically adjusts the number of instances to maintain the CPU at this level during the peak of Friday
Simple Scaling — Sets a Single Alarm CloudWatch (ex.: CPU > 70%) which adds a fixed amount of instances when activated, being simpler to set up for the sixth peak

Scheduled Scaling — allows you to set scalability actions at specific times (e.g. increase to 10 cases every Friday at 18h and go back to 3 cases 22h), preparing the capacity before predictable peaks without expecting performance metrics to worsen
Step Scaling — creates multiple scales (e.g.: CPU > 50% add 2 instances, if CPU > 80% add 5 instances) for response proportional to the sixth peak
questions.explanation: Correct. Scheduled Scaling is the ideal policy when the load pattern is predictable and recurring (e.g. peak every Friday night, commercial time, weekly event). Auto Scaling increases proactively before peak, without waiting for existing instances to get overloaded and trigger alarms of CPU.
questions.hint: For a pre-dictable and recurring traffic pattern (every weekend), what kind of policy does the Auto Scaling increases capacity in pre-configured times, ANTES of the peak start?
optionRationales: Correct. Scheduled Scaling is the ideal policy when the load pattern is predictable and recurring (e.g. peak every Friday night, commercial time, weekly event). Auto Scaling increases proactively before peak, without waiting for existing instances to get overloaded and trigger alarms of CPU.

Correct as general policy of auto-scaling, but REATIVA — o Auto Scaling only adds instances when the CPU For the predictable Friday peak, this means that in the first few minutes of peak the application suffers degradation as the ASG wait for the CPU up and new instances are launched (process of 3-5 Scheduled Scaling anticipates the peak and avoids this degradation window.

Incorrect for the scenario described. Step Scaling is reactive (based on metrics that already indicate overload). For a predictable peak where you want to prepare ANTES, Scheduled Scaling is superior. Step Scaling would be complementary to deal with unexpected variations beyond the expected peak.

Incorrect as best option for predictable peak. Simple Scaling is reactive and has a cooldown period between escalations, making it slower. For predictable pattern (every sixth), Scheduled Scaling prepares capacity in advance without relying on alarms from CPU that only fire when there is degradation.

questions.text: A company has a web application hosted in a single instance EC2. The team wants to understand the risks of this design. What is the main problem of having only one instance EC2 without redundancy?
options: Reduced security — a single instance is more vulnerable to DDoS attacks by having only one IP to attack, while multiple instances distribute attacks

Single Point of Failure (SPOF) — if the only instance EC2 fail (hardware failure, OS problem, maintenance of AWS), all the application is unavailable; there is no redundancy to maintain the service while the problem is solved
Excessive cost — a single instance EC2 it costs more than multiple smaller instances distributed by AZs, for not being able to use volume discount of AWS
Traffic limit — a single instance EC2 you can't get more than 10.000 requests per second due to limitation of the AWS
questions.explanation: Right, one instance. EC2 is a Single Point of Failure: if it fails for any reason (hardware, OS, network, reboot maintenance of AWS), There is no alternative available and the application is completely inaccessible. The solution is to have at least 2 instances in different AZs behind a Load Balancer.
questions.hint: What is the concept of architecture that describes a component whose failure knocks down the whole system — and that a single instance EC2 represents?
optionRationales: Right, one instance. EC2 is a Single Point of Failure: if it fails for any reason (hardware, OS, network, reboot maintenance of AWS), There is no alternative available and the application is completely inaccessible. The solution is to have at least 2 instances in different AZs behind a Load Balancer.

Incorrect as the main problem. A single instance usually costs MENOS The main problem is not cost-effective, it is availability — the risk of SPOF. In practice, add redundancy CUSTA more, but it is necessary for availability SLAs.

Incorrect. There is no such specific limit of AWS of 10.000 req/s by instance — limits depend on the type of instance, application configuration, and network bandwidth. Furthermore, the main problem is not traffic capacity, but availability (SPOF). An instance can be dimensioned vertically (larger type) if the problem is capacity.

Incorrect. The number of instances does not determine the vulnerability to DDoS significantly — the attacker would aim at the ALB or DNS the application in any way. The main problem of a single instance is SPOF (availability), non-security.

questions.text: A company uses Amazon Route 53 for DNS of your website. The architect wants to configure the Route 53 so that, if the main server becomes inaccessible, the traffic is automatically redirected to a backup server. Route 53 allows this configuration?
options: Route 53 Weighted Routing — sets different weights (%) for each server; by reducing the weight of the primary to 0% and backup to 100%, traffic goes all to backup in case of problem
Route 53 Geolocation Routing — allows you to configure which server serves each geographical location; in case of failure, it serves as an automatic backup for locations without a configured server
Route 53 Latency Routing — by creating two registers in the same region, the Route 53 monitors latency and automatically redirects to registration with less latency when primary is slow

Route 53 Failover Routing — Sets up Two Records DNS: one as 'Primary' and another as 'Secondary', with Health Checks in the primary; if the health check detects that the primary is inaccessible, Route 53 automatically returns the Secondary IP in the replies DNS
questions.explanation: Right. Failover Routing no Route 53 It works like this.: (1) Create a health check that monitors the primary server periodically; (2) Create two records with the same name (e.g. app.example.com): a Primary and a Secondary; (3) If the health check fails, or Route 53 it's a failover mechanism. DNS automatic.
questions.hint: What is the policy of routing Route 53 uses Health Checks to detect primary server failure and automatically return the secondary server IP to the responses DNS?
optionRationales: Right. Failover Routing no Route 53 It works like this.: (1) Create a health check that monitors the primary server periodically; (2) Create two records with the same name (e.g. app.example.com): a Primary and a Secondary; (3) If the health check fails, or Route 53 it's a failover mechanism. DNS automatic.

Incorrect for automatic failure. Weighted Routing distributes traffic percently between multiple endpoints — but weight adjustment is manual. To fail AUTOMATICAL health check based, Failover Routing is the correct type. With Weighted Routing, someone would manually need to change weight when the primary falls.

Incorrect. Latency Routing chooses the endpoint with less network latency — doesn't fail when the primary is inaccessible. If the primary server is down but in the same region, Latency Routing wouldn't help. Failover Routing with health check is the correct mechanism for recovery of failures.

Incorrect. Geolocation Routing maps users by geographical location for specific endpoints — it is not a failover mechanism. It does not monitor server health to redirect in case of failure. Failover Routing with health checks is the specific mechanism for automatic failure recovery.

questions.text: A company has an environment AWS and you want to know the difference between RPO (Recovery Point Objective) and RTO (Recovery Time Objective) to plan your disaster recovery strategy. What definition is correct?
options: RPO and RTO are equal — both measure the maximum time of service unavailability after a disaster; are interchangeable terms in DR planning
RPO is the time to recover the service; RTO is the amount of data that can be lost — RPO determines the speed of recovery and RTO determines the backup frequency

RPO is the maximum amount of data that can be lost (in time) after a disaster — ex.: RPO of 1 time means that after a disaster, you can lose as much as possible 1 time of data; RTO is the maximum time to recover and put the service back online after the disaster
RPO is the estimated cost of recovery after a disaster; RTO is the number of backup instances required to ensure recovery within the SLA
questions.explanation: Correct.. RPO (Recovery Point Objective): how much data/time you can lose — determines the required backup frequency. Ex.: RPO=1h requires backups to each 1h. RTO (Recovery Time Objective): how long it takes to recover the service — determines the necessary recovery architecture..: RTO=4h means you have 4 hours to restore service after disaster.
questions.hint: RPO = Recovery POINT Objective (on DADOS: what point in the past you can go back?). RTO = Recovery TIME Objective (on TEMPO: How long it takes to recover?).
optionRationales: Correct.. RPO (Recovery Point Objective): how much data/time you can lose — determines the required backup frequency. Ex.: RPO=1h requires backups to each 1h. RTO (Recovery Time Objective): how long it takes to recover the service — determines the necessary recovery architecture..: RTO=4h means you have 4 hours to restore service after disaster.

Incorrect — Concepts Are Inverted. RPO = lost data (Recovery POINT = the point in the past as far as you can recover). RTO = Recovery time (Recovery TIME = how long it takes to recover). The way to remember: RPO It's about DADOS (past point), RTO It's about TEMPO Recovery.

Incorrect. RPO and RTO measure different things: RPO measures potential loss of DADOS (in time/volume), RTO It measures recovery time (as long as the service is down). One can be high and the other low — ex.: RPO=24h (accepts loss) 1 data day), RTO=1h (needs to be back in 1 time). Complementary metrics, not equivalent.

Incorrect. RPO and RTO are not about cost or number of instances — are time metrics that define recovery objectives: RPO=Maximum data loss (time)), RTO=maximum recovery time. Cost and number of instances are consequences of the choices of RPO/RTO, not the definitions themselves.

questions.text: A company has a bucket S3 with critical data and wants to protect them from accidental exclusion by any user, including administrators. S3 prevents objects from being deleted or overwritten for a specified period?
options: S3 Versioning with MFA Delete enabled — requires MFA to delete versions of objects; as administrators rarely have the MFA available, this effectively prevents deletions
S3 Intelligent-Tiering — by moving objects to layers of infrequent access storage, the S3 automatically protects objects against deletion for a minimum period of 30 days

S3 Object Lock in mode COMPLIANCE — once activated, NENHUM user (no root account) AWS) can delete or modify protected objects during the configured retention period, ensuring immutability for compliance (WORM)
S3 Bucket Policy with Deny for s3:DeleteObject — creating a policy that denies s3:DeleteObject for all users, no object in the pocket can be deleted
questions.explanation: Correct.. S3 Object Lock mode COMPLIANCE is the most restrictive: the object cannot be deleted or modified by NENHUM user during the retention period — neither administrators nor root. GOVERNANCE is less restrictive (special permission users can bypass it). Object Lock is used for data that need to be regulatively unchangeable. (LGPD, SOX, HIPAA).
questions.hint: What is the functionality of S3 implements the model WORM (Write Once, Read Many) — making objects immutable for a period, preventing deletion even by administrators?
optionRationales: Correct.. S3 Object Lock mode COMPLIANCE is the most restrictive: the object cannot be deleted or modified by NENHUM user during the retention period — neither administrators nor root. GOVERNANCE is less restrictive (special permission users can bypass it). Object Lock is used for data that need to be regulatively unchangeable. (LGPD, SOX, HIPAA).

Partially correct as protection, but insufficient for 'including administrators' — users with permission AdministratorAccess can modify or remove bucket policies. Object Lock in mode COMPLIANCE is technically impossible to be circumvented even by administrators, being superior to the described scenario of unrestricted protection.

Partially correct as additional control, but MFA Delete Still PERMITE deletion by whom you have MFA. The description 'rarely have the MFA available' is not a technical warranty. Object Lock in mode COMPLIANCE is the technical protection guaranteed — regardless of having MFA or not, the delete operation is denied during the retention period.

Incorrect. S3 Intelligent-Tiering is a storage class that moves objects between layers based on access patterns to optimize costs — it has no relation to deletion protection. There is no delete protection in any storage class of the S3 by itself (no Object Lock or Versioning).

questions.text: A startup uses AWS and wants to understand how the Amazon Route 53. A developer asks: 'What is a TTL in a record DNS And why does it matter?' Which explanation is correct?
options: TTL is the maximum number of hops (rotator jumps) that a package DNS can cross — when you reach zero, the package is discarded to avoid endless routing loops
TTL in DNS determines how long the instance EC2 the application is active — when the TTL expires, the instance is automatically restarted by Route 53 to maintain server health

TTL (Time To Live) is the time in seconds that solvers DNS will cache the response of a record — a TTL low (ex.: 60(s) means that changes in DNS Propagates rapidly (solvents consult more frequently), but generate more traffic; a TTL high (ex.: 86400(s) reduces traffic DNS but increases the time of propagation of changes
TTL is the maximum time the source server expects for a response DNS before timeout — one TTL low means that the server quickly gives up if the client does not respond
questions.explanation: Correct.. TTL defines how long solvers DNS Intermediaries (ISPs, browsers) will cache the answer. TTL low = rapid spread of changes, more consultations to Route 53. TTL high = less consultations (lower cost, lower latency DNS), but changes take longer to propagate. In deployments, it is common practice to reduce TTL hours before making a change of DNS.
questions.hint: TTL DNS And what happens when that time expires in the solvers who hid the answer??
optionRationales: Correct.. TTL defines how long solvers DNS Intermediaries (ISPs, browsers) will cache the answer. TTL low = rapid spread of changes, more consultations to Route 53. TTL high = less consultations (lower cost, lower latency DNS), but changes take longer to propagate. In deployments, it is common practice to reduce TTL hours before making a change of DNS.

Incorrect. TTL is not related to server connection timeout — is the cache time of the solvers. TTL is configured in the log DNS and determines how long the solvers save the answer before consulting again. It is a configuration on the side of the DNS, not from the application server.

Incorrect. The description of 'hops and discard in zero' is of TTL in IP packages (field in the IP header), not of TTL in records DNS. Though they use the same name, TTL DNS has a completely different meaning: is the cache time of the record DNS, measured in seconds.
Incorrect. TTL DNS has no relation to instances EC2 or rebooting of servers. Route 53 does not restart instances. TTL is exclusively about the cache time of records DNS in intermediate solvers.

questions.text: A company has a microservices architecture where several services need to communicate. They want a messaging system where producer services can send messages without having to wait for consumers to process — consumers process at their own pace. AWS is more suitable for this disconnection?
options: Amazon SQS (Simple Queue Service) — is a managed message queue where producers send messages to the queue and consumers process them independently; messages stay in the queue until they are processed (or expired), completely decoupling the rate of consumption production
Amazon SNS (Simple Notification Service) — allows producer services to publish messages to multiple consumers simultaneously, decoupling consumption production in real time
Amazon API Gateway — allows services to communicate via APIs REST synchronous; using long timeout, the producer can wait for the response anointingly
Amazon ElastiCache — instances temporarily store messages in the Redis/Memcached cache, allowing producers and consumers to operate at different speeds
questions.explanation: Correct.. SQS is the line service of the AWS for asynchronous decoupling. The producer sends to the queue and continues his work without waiting. The consumer pulls messages from the queue at his own pace. If the consumer stays slow, the messages accumulate in the row without loss. It is the most common asynchronous decoupling pattern.
questions.hint: What service AWS is specifically a FILA of managed messages — where producers put messages and consumers withdraw them at their own pace, without the producer having to wait?
optionRationales: Correct.. SQS is the line service of the AWS for asynchronous decoupling. The producer sends to the queue and continues his work without waiting. The consumer pulls messages from the queue at his own pace. If the consumer stays slow, the messages accumulate in the row without loss. It is the most common asynchronous decoupling pattern.

Partially correct for pub/sub, but SNS is for immediate delivery (push) — does not buffer. If a consumer is not available at the time of publication, you may lose the message. SQS makes the real time disconnection (message stays in line). SNS is often used in conjunction with SQS: SNS does fan-out for multiple rows SQS.

Incorrect. API Gateway is for SINCONA communication (request-response) — the customer awaits the answer. Even with long timeouts, it is not the same as asynchronous processing via row. For asynchronous uncoupling where the producer does not have to wait for the consumer, SQS is the correct solution.

Incorrect. ElastiCache is a data cache (Redis/Memcached) to speed up access to data — it is not a messaging system with guarantees of delivery, visibility, retention and DLQ (Dead Letter Queue) as the SQS. Using cache as a message queue would be a fragile solution without the guarantees of a managed queue service.

questions.text: A company wants to ensure that its application is resilient to regional failures of the AWS. Which disaster recovery strategy offers the smallest RTO (recovery time) in case of a region failure AWS?
options: Warm Standby — maintains a reduced version of the application running in another region ready to scale; the RTO is of 0 seconds because the servers are already fully initialized

Multi-Site Active/Active — the application runs simultaneously in multiple regions with active traffic in all; in the event of a failure of a region, the Route 53 or Global Accelerator redirects traffic to healthy regions without perceptible downtime

Backup and Restore — Makes regular backup of data to S3 in another region and, in case of failure, restores the complete infrastructure from the backup; this is the fastest method because the S3 instantly restores
Pilot Light — keeps critical components (databank) in another region and scales the other components (EC2) where necessary; or RTO it is instantaneous because the servers are already preheated
questions.explanation: Correct. Multi-Site Active/Active has RTO close to zero because there is no 'failover' — traffic simply stops going to the region fails and continues in the others that are already active. It is the most expensive but least expensive DR strategy RTO. Other strategies (Backup/Restore, Pilot Light, Warm Standby) have progressively smaller RTOs but still have some recovery time.
questions.hint: What DR strategy results in RTO close to zero — because the application is already running with active traffic in multiple regions simultaneously, not requiring 'failover''?
optionRationales: Correct. Multi-Site Active/Active has RTO close to zero because there is no 'failover' — traffic simply stops going to the region fails and continues in the others that are already active. It is the most expensive but least expensive DR strategy RTO. Other strategies (Backup/Restore, Pilot Light, Warm Standby) have progressively smaller RTOs but still have some recovery time.

Incorrect. Backup and Restore has the MAIOR RTO ((h) DR strategies — the entire infrastructure of the zero must be created and the data restored (which may take a long time)). S3 does not restore infrastructure EC2/RDS 'Instantly.' It's the cheapest but least agile strategy in recovery..

Incorrect about RTO Pilot Light keeps the minimum active (usually the bench) and scales the rest during the DR. The time to scale additional components (launch instances) EC2, configure ALB, update DNS) results in RTO of 10-60 minutes — not instant. Multi-Site Active/Active has the lowest RTO.

Incorrect about RTO of 0 Warm Standby has reduced capacity that needs to be scaled to production in case of failure (scaling EC2, adjust database, update DNS) — resulting in RTO Multi-Site Active/Active has RTO close to zero because nothing needs to be done — traffic is already being distributed to all regions.

questions.text: A company uses Amazon ELB (Elastic Load Balancer) with instances EC2. The administrator realized that some instances are receiving traffic even when they are in trouble and not responding correctly. ELB determines if an instance is healthy to receive traffic?
options: ELB Health Checks — o ELB periodically send verification requests (HTTP/HTTPS for one URL specific, or TCP for a door) for each instance; if the instance does not respond with the correct status code (ex.: 200 OK) for a configurable number of consecutive times, the ELB the brand as unhealthy and stops sending traffic to it
The ELB uses Status Checks from EC2 (System Status Check and Mechanism Status Check) — if any of these checks fail, the ELB automatically replaces the instance
The ELB monitor the status of the instances EC2 way AWS Systems Manager — if the agent SSM not responding, the instance is considered unhealthy
The ELB monitor the use of CPU of the bodies CloudWatch — cases with CPU above 80% are considered unhealthy and removed from traffic rotation
questions.explanation: Right. ELB Health Checks are configurable: protocol (HTTP, HTTPS, TCP), path (e.g. /health), port, check interval, timeout, health check threshold/unhealthy. An instance marked as unhealthy does not receive new requests until it is healthy again. The application must have an endpoint /health that returns 200 when working.
questions.hint: Like the ELB check whether an instance EC2 is responding correctly — what type of request it sends, and what criterion it uses to mark the instance as 'unhealthy''?
optionRationales: Right. ELB Health Checks are configurable: protocol (HTTP, HTTPS, TCP), path (e.g. /health), port, check interval, timeout, health check threshold/unhealthy. An instance marked as unhealthy does not receive new requests until it is healthy again. The application must have an endpoint /health that returns 200 when working.

Incorrect. ELB does not use CPU as a criterion of health — high CPU may indicate high load (working instance normally) or problem. The health criterion is RESPOSTA the health check requests (the instance answers correctly?). CPU 100% may still be serving requests correctly and would be considered healthy.

Incorrect. ELB does not depend on AWS Systems Manager to determine health. Health Checks are made directly by ELB by means of requests HTTP/HTTPS/TCP for the court itself — independent of any installed agent. SSM is for operational management (remote commands, patches), not for health checks of ELB.

Incorrect. ELB Health Checks EC2 Status Checks are independent mechanisms. EC2 Status Checks check hardware and SO integrity — ELB does not use them to decide about traffic. ELB uses your own health checks application. You can configure the Auto Scaling for use ELB health checks (which then replaces instances), but the decision-making mechanism of ELB are your own health checks.

questions.text: One company implemented a multi-AZ architecture with EC2 and ALB. The architect realized that when an AZ becomes overloaded, traffic is not rebalanced for less busy instances in the other AZ. What configuration of the ALB ensures more uniform load distribution between all instances in all AZs?
options: Sticky Sessions (Session Affinity) — when enabling sticky sessions, the ALB ensures that requests from the same client always go to the same instance, distributing different users to different instances in a balanced way
Increase the number of registered AZs ALB of 2 for 3 — with more AZs, the traffic is distributed more granularly between the nodes of ALB, resulting in better balance
Configure target groups with the same weight between AZs — when balancing target groups weights, the ALB uniformly distributes traffic

optionRationales: By default, ALB route traffic between AZ instances where the request arrived. S3 Standard is for frequently accessed data (higher storage cost, no recovery cost); S3 Standard-IA is for rarely accessed data (minor storage cost, but has additional cost per GB recovered/accessed) — decision depends on frequency of access to minimize total cost
S3 Standard-IA has access latency greater than S3 Standard — data in Standard-IA takes minutes to become available after a request for access
S3 Standard-IA is for data in transit (in active use), while S3 Standard is for permanently stored data — the AI in the name means 'In Active' (use)'
questions.explanation: Correct.. S3 Standard: storage cost ~$0.023/GB/month, no charge per retriival. Incorrect. 'IA' means 'Infrequent Access', not 'In Active use''. S3 Standard-IA is for rarely accessed stored data — the opposite of 'active data'. Both are persistent storage classes.

questions.text: A company uses Amazon CloudWatch to monitor your instances EC2. The team of operations wants to be notified by email when using CPU stay above 80% for more than 5 which two features of the CloudWatch are necessary for this?

One CloudWatch Dashboard + one CloudWatch Events Rule — the dashboard displays a CPU in real time and Events Rule sends email when the CPU exceeds the thread configured in the panel
One CloudWatch Log Group + one CloudWatch Log Metric Filter — by filtering log CPU of the EC2 and create a custom metric, you can set alerts for when the metric exceeds 80%
One AWS Settings + Amazon SNS — when creating a Config Rule that detects CPU above 80%, the Config publishes the violation in SNS for notification by email
questions.explanation: Correct. For notification of CPU: (1) Create CloudWatch Alarm: metric EC2 CPUtilization, threshold > 80, period 5 minutes, evaluate 1 period; (2) Link the alarm to one SNS Topic with email subscription (email needs to be confirmed). CPU is above 80% by 5 min, the alarm changes state ALARM and publishes no SNS, sending the email.
questions.hint: To send email when a metric exceeds a thread in CloudWatch, two resources are needed: CloudWatch monitor the metric and fire, and which message service sends the email?
optionRationales: Correct. CPU is above 80% by 5 min, the alarm changes state ALARM and publishes no SNS, sending the email.

Incorrect. CloudWatch Dashboards are for VISUALIZATION (do not send notifications). CloudWatch Events (now EventBridge) reacts to resource status change events (not metrics exceeding thresholds). For METRIC-based notification with threshold, CloudWatch ALARM is the correct remedy.

Incorrect for this case. CPUutilization is a native metric of EC2 no CloudWatch — is not a log. To use Log Metric Filters, it would be necessary to export metrics for logs and process them, which is unnecessarily complex. CloudWatch Alarm with metric EC2 pattern is the direct and correct path.

Incorrect. AWS Config assesses CONFIGURES of resources (e.g.: Security Group There's a door. 22 Open?') — does not monitor real-time performance metrics like CPU. For monitoring metrics and threats-based alerts, CloudWatch Alarm is the right service.

questions.text: A company wants to understand when to use a Application Load Balancer (ALB) versus a Network Load Balancer (NLB). What statement correctly describes the difference between the two?
options: ALB only supports HTTPS (encrypted traffic); NLB only supports HTTP (Unencrypted traffic) — the choice between the two depends on whether the application uses SSL/TLS
ALB and NLB are identical in functionality — the only difference is that the ALB has native support to Amazon WAF for protection against web attacks

ALB operates in the layer 7 (HTTP/HTTPS) and can route based on URL path, hostname, or headers (ex.: /api/* goes to one target group, /images/* goes to another); NLB operates in the layer 4 (TCP/UDP) with ultra-low latency, ideal for non--HTTP like games, VoIP, and loads that need static IPs
ALB is for high load production environments; NLB is for development and testing environments — the NLB It's cheaper and has less functionality
questions.explanation: Correct.. ALB (Application Load Balancer): layer 7, You understand? HTTP/HTTPS, supports content-based routing (path, hostname, headers, query strings), WebSocket, built-in authentication. NLB (Network Load Balancer): layer 4 (TCP/UDP), latency in the order of milliseconds, supports static elastic IPs, ideal for protocols not-HTTP and high performance network requirements.
questions.hint: ALB operates in which layer of model OSI (and understands which protocol)? NLB operate in which layer? Which has support for routing by URL path?
optionRationales: Correct.. ALB (Application Load Balancer): layer 7, You understand? HTTP/HTTPS, supports content-based routing (path, hostname, headers, query strings), WebSocket, built-in authentication. NLB (Network Load Balancer): layer 4 (TCP/UDP), latency in the order of milliseconds, supports static elastic IPs, ideal for protocols not-HTTP and high performance network requirements.

Incorrect. ALB how much NLB support encrypted traffic (HTTPS/TLS). The difference isn't about encryption — it's about the operating layer and intelligent routing capacity. ALB operates in the layer 7 (application), NLB in the layer 4 (transport).

NLB may have even more throughput than ALB for certain loads ( ultra-low latency design). The choice is based on the type of application and routing requirements, not in the environment.

Incorrect. ALB and NLB have fundamental differences in architecture and case of use (chamber 7 vs 4, routing by content vs. connection TCP pure, latency, etc.). ALB have integration with WAF and NLB do not have (because WAF It's a layer 7 and NLB It's a layer 4), that's just one of the many differences — they're not identical.

questions.text: A company uses AWS and wants to understand what is an Availability Zone (AZ) and how it differs from a Region AWS. What statement correctly describes the region → AZ hierarchy?
options: Regions and AZs are synonymous terms in AWS — both refer to physical data centers where servers are hosted; the difference is only terminology per team.

A Region AWS is a set of geographically separated AZs in the same location (e.g. us-east)-1 = Northern Virginia); each AZ is composed of one or more physically separated centers with independent energy, networks and cooling — physical separation ensures that failures in one AZ do not affect others in the same Region
A Region AWS is a unique data center; an AZ is a server room within the data center — multiple AZs within a Region share the same energy and network infrastructure for efficiency

An AZ is a cluster of servers EC2 within a sub-network VPC; a Region is composed of multiple sub-networks in different geographical locations of the world — each Region may have AZs in up to 5 different continents
questions.explanation: Right. AWS: Regions > Availability Zones > data centers. One Region (e.g. us-east)-1) has multiple AZs (e.g. us-east)-1a, us-east-1b, us-east-1(c) which are physically separated but connected by low latency high-speed network. AZs are isolated from each other so that a failure (natural disaster, electrical problem) in one AZ does not cascade to the other.
questions.hint: A region contains multiple AZs. What is the goal of physical separation between AZs — why they have independent energy, network and cooling?
optionRationales: Right. AWS: Regions > Availability Zones > data centers. One Region (e.g. us-east)-1) has multiple AZs (e.g. us-east)-1a, us-east-1b, us-east-1(c) which are physically separated but connected by low latency high-speed network. AZs are isolated from each other so that a failure (natural disaster, electrical problem) in one AZ does not cascade to the other.

Incorrect. AZs are not cluster EC2 are not related to sub-networks VPC — are physical places (data centers) within the same geographical area (city/ metropolitan area). The AZs of a Region are in the same country/geographic area — not on different continents. Each Region has nearby AZs (ms of latency)).

Incorrect. A Region is not a single data centre — it is a collection of geographically scattered AZs. INDEPENDENTE (energy, network, cooling), not shared. The goal is exactly that a failure (energy, for example) in one AZ does not affect the others.

Incorrect. Region and AZ are distinct hierarchical concepts: a Region contains MULTIPLES AZs. A Region is a geographical group (e.g.: 'us-east')-1' = Northern Virginia), while an AZ is a specific physical site within that region (e.g. 'us-east-1a'). Not synonymous.

questions.text: A company has a web application with many static images that are served by Amazon S3. Users in Brazil complain of slow access to the site hosted in us-east-1. How to improve image loading time for global users without migrating data to other regions?
options: Increase Bucket Size S3 and enable 'requester countries' to reduce latency — bucks with 'requester countries' configuration have dedicated bandwidth from AWS
Migratory or Bucket S3 for the sa-east region-1 (São Paulo) — by hosting the data closest to users, latency will be automatically reduced for Brazil
Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration — using the backbone network of AWS for uploads and downloads, the transfer of objects S3 is accelerated for users anywhere in the world

Configure the Amazon CloudFront as CDN in front of the pocket S3 — o CloudFront distributes the content to edge locations around the world; users in Brazil will be served by edge location in São Paulo, drastically reducing the latency of delivery of static content
questions.explanation: Correct.. CloudFront is the CDN (Content Delivery Network) AWS. When a user in Brazil first accesses the image, the CloudFront Bucket search S3 (us-east-1) and cached in the edge location of São Paulo. Subsequent requirements are met directly from the edge (São Paulo → user), eliminating the latency of a full trip to EUA.
questions.hint: To reduce static content latency for global users without moving data, which service AWS distributes content to geographic locations close to users (edge locations)?
optionRationales: Correct.. CloudFront is the CDN (Content Delivery Network) AWS. When a user in Brazil first accesses the image, the CloudFront Bucket search S3 (us-east-1) and cached in the edge location of São Paulo. Subsequent requirements are met directly from the edge (São Paulo → user), eliminating the latency of a full trip to EUA.

Works for Brazilian users, but harms other global users (European, Asian would have higher latency). CloudFront serves all global users of edge location closer without needing to migrate data. Migrating the bucket is a partial solution that creates a new problem for users from other regions.

Incorrect. S3 Transfer Acceleration UPLOADS for the S3 (send data by backbone AWS instead of the public internet) — not a CDN for downloads. CloudFront is the correct service to speed up content delivery to end users.

Incorrect. 'Requester Pays' is a configuration of BILLING who makes the object accesser pay for the transfer costs (instead of the owner of the pocket) — has no connection with latency or dedicated bandwidth. CloudFront is the performance solution for static content.

questions.text: A company has a database RDS MySQL that is being overloaded with reading queries (SELECT). You want to write (INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE) how to improve reading performance without increasing the size of the primary instance?
options: Increase IOPS provided by the RDS (Provisioned IOPS SSD) — more IOPS increases the bank's reading throughput, allowing you to want more SELECT are processed simultaneously
Enable RDS Multi-AZ — the standby bench in another AZ absorbs reading queries to distribute the load between the two instances

Create one or more RDS Read Replicas — read replicas receive an asynchronous copy of primary data and may serve as a query SELECT; by redirecting most readings to replicas, the load in the primary instance is significantly reduced
Enable RDS Performance Insights — Performance Insights automatically analyzes and optimizes slow reading queries, improving performance without architectural changes
questions.explanation: Correct.. RDS Read Replicas are created with asynchronous replication from the primary bank. SELECT (read) — the application needs to be configured to use the replica endpoint for readings. The primary continues to receive written. 5 read replicas for MySQL/PostgreSQL.
questions.hint: What is the functionality of RDS creates copies of the bench that can serve reading queries (SELECT), distributing the load between multiple reading instances?
optionRationales: Correct.. RDS Read Replicas are created with asynchronous replication from the primary bank. SELECT (read) — the application needs to be configured to use the replica endpoint for readings. The primary continues to receive written. 5 read replicas for MySQL/PostgreSQL.

Incorrect. Multi-AZ standby bench does not accept read queries — it is exclusive to failover. Multi-AZ is for high availability, not for read scalability. Read Replicas are the correct mechanism for distributing read load.

Partly useful to improve I/O throughput on disk, but it is a vertical solution (better the existing instance). If the reading load continues to grow, it will reach the limit again. Read Replicas are a horizontal solution (scale adding more reading instances) more efficient and economical for the described scenario.

Incorrect. RDS Performance Insights is a tool for MONITORAMENTO and DIAGNOSTIC — shows which wants are slower and consume more resources. It does not automatically optimize wants. To reduce the reading load in the primary, the correct architectural solution is Read Replicas.

questions.text: A company has an application that often searches for the same data from a relational database, causing repeated queries that increase latency. How to implement a cache layer to reduce the amount of queries to the database?
options: Configure the RDS Multi-AZ — with two synchronised benches, it is possible to distribute reading queries between primary and standby, reducing by half the load of repeated queries

Implement Amazon ElastiCache (Redis or Memcached) between the application and the database — the application first checks the cache; if the data is (hit cache), returns from ElastiCache in milliseconds; if it is not (miss cache), search the bank and store in the cache for future accesses
Enable MySQL native query cache on RDS — MySQL has an internal cache query that automatically caches the results of SELECT, without the need for external services
Use Amazon DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) instead of ElastiCache — the DAX is more suitable for relational banks (RDS/MySQL) because it was created by AWS specifically to speed up cherries SQL
questions.explanation: ElastiCache is the in-memory cache service of AWS. Redis and Memcached are the available engines. The default 'cache-aside' (lazy loading) is the most common: application checks cache → hit: returns direct; miss: searches the bank → stores in the cache → returns. Reduces drastically latency and loading in the database for frequently read data.
questions.hint: What service AWS provides in-memory cache (Redis or Memcached) to store query results and reduce the number of database accesses?

Reduces drastically latency and loading in the database for frequently read data.

Incorrect. DAX (DynamoDB Accelerator) is a specific cache for the DynamoDB (NoSQL) — cannot be used with relational banks (RDS MySQL). To speed up access to data from RDS, ElastiCache (Redis or Memcached) is the correct in-memory cache solution.

Incorrect as recommended solution. MySQL's query cache was REMOVIDA no MySQL 8.0 because of performance problems with multiple threads (excessive lock containment). In addition, the internal cache query has much lower scalability than ElastiCache. AWS recommends ElastiCache for caching applications.

Incorrect. RDS Multi-AZ does not accept reading queries — it is exclusive to failover. To reduce repeated queries to the bank, an external cache like ElastiCache is the correct approach. Even if they were Read Replicas (which accept reading), they would still want to the bank — the in-memory cache completely avoids access to the bank for cached data.

questions.text: A company has an application that uploads images to S3 and then you need to process them (resize, convert format). The current processing is done in an instance EC2 how to use a serverless architecture to optimize this processing?

Incorrect. questions.text: A company has a web application with unpredictable traffic peaks. The team wants to use instances EC2 which climb rapidly during peaks and reduce during quiet periods. EC2 offers automatic scalability and charge per second of use?

Dedicated Hosts are for compliance and licensing (physical hardware dedicated to the customer) — are the least flexible for scalability, because the capacity is fixed and you pay for the entire host. For simple operations by primary key (get item, put item)), DynamoDB overcomes relational banks in latency and scalability.

Incorrect. Amazon Neptune is a GRAFOS (for data with complex relationships, such as social networks, knowledge graphs) — is not a general use bank for simple high-speed operations., DynamoDB is the optimized solution.

questions.text: A company has an application that serves static files (HTML, CSS, JS, images) of a server EC2. The team wants to optimize for better performance and reduce load on the server. What is the best performance approach to serve static content on AWS?
options: Enable EC2 Placement Groups (Cluster) to reduce the instance's network latency — instances in group cluster placement have high speed network that improves the performance of serving static files

Host static files in Amazon S3 with S3 Static Website Hosting + CloudFront as CDN forward — the S3 is highly scalable to serve static files, and the CloudFront distribute them to edge locations close to users, with less latency and without overloading the EC2

questions.explanation: Right. For static content, the highest performance standard is: S3 (highly available and scalable storage for files) + CloudFront (CDN for delivery from the nearest edge). EC2 to serve statics, improving performance so much (CDN) the capacity of the EC2 (which can focus on dynamic content).

Incorrect as best approach. Increasing the instance is vertical scalability — eventually reaches limits and still maintains latency based on geographical distance. Incorrect. ALB has no built-in content cache — it is a load balancer, not one CDN. The ALB Redistribute traffic between instances but does not store static content. CloudFront (CDN) is the service with edge cache. Add ALB no CloudFront does not improve static content performance.

Incorrect. EC2 Placement Groups Cluster put physically close instances for low latency instance-to-instance communication (useful for HPC, database clusters). questions.text: A company has an e-commerce application with relational database. During seasonal sales, reporting queries (analytics) are very slow because they compete with sales transactions by the same bank. How to separate analytical workloads from transactions?

Use Amazon Redshift to completely replace the RDS — o Redshift is a columnar data warehouse that processes transactional and analytical queries much faster than the RDS
Enable RDS Multi-AZ and redirect analytical queries to the standby in another AZ — the standby will have less load because it is less accessible, resulting in faster analytical queries

Increase database size using Amazon Aurora Global Database — the Aurora Global Database replicates data in multiple regions, and analytical queries can be executed in the secondary region without impact on primary
questions.explanation: Correct. Read Replica dedicated to analytics is a standard set to separate OLTP (Online Transaction Processing) OLAP (Online Analytical Processing). The primary is focused on transactions (INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE + critical readings), while the replica serves intensive reporting queries without impacting transactions. questions.hint: To perform analytical queries without impacting the transactions of the primary instance, which functionality of the RDS creates a read copy that can receive heavy reporting queries?
optionRationales: Correct. Read Replica dedicated to analytics is a standard set to separate OLTP (Online Transaction Processing) OLAP (Online Analytical Processing). The replica may even have a type of instance optimized for memory (e.g.: r5.4xlarge) for analytical queries.
