Incorrect. The Multi-AZ standby does not accept reading queries — it is exclusive to automatic failover. It is not possible to redirect queries to the standby. Read Replicas (not Multi-AZ standby) are the solution for distributing reading load/analytics.

Correct in concept of separation (secondary region for analytics) but incorrect as basic solution. Aurora Global Database is an advanced solution for disaster recovery cross-region and edge reads — not the first solution to separate analytics from OLTP in the same region. Read Replica in the same region is simpler and more direct.

questions.text: A company uses AWS Lambda for event processing. One developer realized that the first invocations of a function Lambda after a period of inactivity are slower than the subsequent ones.?
options: Throttling — o AWS Lambda limits the number of summonses per second; first calls are lined up and delayed until capacity is available, causing slowness in the first summonses

Cold Start — when a function Lambda is inactive for a sufficient time, the container that the execution is dislocated; in the next invocation, the AWS needs to allocate a new container, load the runtime and function code before running, adding latency (typically 100ms-1s depending on the language and size of the package)
Lack of memory — the first invocations use more memory because they need to load libraries, causing swapping that increases latency; subsequent invocations already have libraries in memory RAM

Timeout of connection — in the first invocations, the Lambda needs to establish new connections TCP with external services (data bank, APIs), which have delayed handshake; subsequent invocations reuse cached connections
questions.explanation: Right. Cold Start is the phenomenon where the first invocation (or after inactivity) of Lambda has additional latency for: (1) supply delivery container, (2) load runtime (Java is slower than Node.js), (3) run the boot code out of the handler. Subsequent invocations (warm) reuse the container and are much faster.
questions.hint: What is the term for additional latency in PRIMEIRAS Invocations of a function Lambda after inactivity — caused by the need to allocate a new execution container?
optionRationales: Right. Cold Start is the phenomenon where the first invocation (or after inactivity) of Lambda has additional latency for: (1) supply delivery container, (2) load runtime (Java is slower than Node.js), (3) run the boot code out of the handler. Subsequent invocations (warm) reuse the container and are much faster.

Incorrect. Throttling occurs when you EXCEDE the limit of competition (default) 1000 by region) — is not what happens in 'first invocations after inactivity'. Cold Start is specific for the first invocation after inactivity, not for high load. Throttling would result in errors 429 (TooManyRequestsException), not just slowness.

Partially correct that establishing connections is part of the cold start, but the root cause of the cold start is the allocation of CONTAINER execution — not just connections TCP. Moreover, re-use of connections between invocations is not guaranteed (depending on how the Lambda is programmed) and is not the main concept here. Cold Start encompasses all the cost of environmental startup.

Incorrect. Lambda does not use swap — if the function exceeds the assigned memory, it is closed with error OOM. The cold start is not caused by swapping but by the initialization of the running environment (container). Lambda (which also increases CPU (proportional) may REDUZIR the cold start when speeding up the initialization, but the cause is the provision of the container, not lack of RAM.

questions.text: A company has an application that makes many queries to the database RDS to recover data from a rarely changing 'system configurations' table. The team wants to eliminate these unnecessary queries to the bank. What is the most efficient solution?
options: Implement caching in memory with Amazon ElastiCache Redis — when loading system settings to Redis with a TTL long (ex.: 1 time), the cache search application instead of the bank; as settings rarely change, the cache will almost always have the updated data (hit rate close to 100%)
Create a RDS Read Replica dedicated to configuration wants — by separating configuration wants from main traffic, they will not affect the performance of the primary bank
Increase Database Connection Pool — By reusing existing connections, configuration queries run faster without overhead establishing new connections
Use Amazon DynamoDB to store system configurations — the DynamoDB has native sub-millisecond latency for get operations by key, eliminating the need for additional caching
questions.explanation: Correct. For data that rarely changes (such as system settings), ElastiCache Redis with TTL long is ideal: high rate of cache hit (data rarely expires without change), sub-millisecond latency, and drastic reduction of queries to the bank. When settings change, the application invalidates the cache and it is recharged from the bank.
questions.hint: For data that 'rarely change' and are accessed frequently, which cache-in-memory approach completely eliminates repeated queries to the database?
optionRationales: Correct. For data that rarely changes (such as system settings), ElastiCache Redis with TTL long is ideal: high rate of cache hit (data rarely expires without change), sub-millisecond latency, and drastic reduction of queries to the bank. When settings change, the application invalidates the cache and it is recharged from the bank.

Incorrect as the best solution. Read Replicas still want to the bank (now in another instance). For data that rarely changes, the cache in-memory avoids COMPLETAMENTE the query to the bank after the first loading. ElastiCache is much more efficient than Read Replica for this access pattern.

Partly correct that DynamoDB It would be faster than RDS for simple operations by key. However, migrate data to DynamoDB involves changing architecture and code. The simplest and most immediate solution to 'eliminate unnecessary queries to the existing bank' is to add ElastiCache in front of the current bank — no data migration.

Incorrect for the problem described. Connection pooling optimizes the OVERHEAD Connection TCP/TLS, But he's still doing the quirky. VOLUME of repeated and unnecessary queries to the bank — not the speed of each query. ElastiCache eliminates repeated queries (cache hit = no query to the bank), while connection pooling still makes them.

questions.text: A company uses Amazon S3 and needs to process very large files (multi-GB) efficiently. S3 often fails by timeout or unstable connection. What functionality of S3 solve this problem?
options: S3 Transfer Acceleration — using the backbone network of AWS globally, Transfer Acceleration increases upload speed to large files without timeout risk

Multipart Upload — divides the file into parts (minimum 5 MB on the other hand, except the last), uploads each part independently (could be in parallel), and ends with a 'complete' operation that combines the parts; if one part fails, only it needs to be re-sent, not the entire file
S3 Presigned URLs with long expiration (24 hours) — when using one URL with long term, the connection does not expire before finishing the upload of the large file
Increase connection timeout in instance EC2 which makes upload — when setting up a larger timeout in the application, large files have more time to complete upload without fail
questions.explanation: Right. Multipart Upload is the recommended mechanism for files above 100 MB (mandatory for files above 5 GB in a single operation PUT). Benefits: parallel upload of parts (better throughput), resilience (failure in one part does not restart the entire file), and possibility to pause/retrieve uploads. AWS SDK can configure multipart upload automatically.
questions.hint: What is the functionality of S3 divides large files into smaller parts that can be sent in parallel and individually redirected in case of failure — without restarting the entire upload?
optionRationales: Right. Multipart Upload is the recommended mechanism for files above 100 MB (mandatory for files above 5 GB in a single operation PUT). Benefits: parallel upload of parts (better throughput), resilience (failure in one part does not restart the entire file), and possibility to pause/retrieve uploads. AWS SDK can configure multipart upload automatically.

Partly useful to improve the speed of long-distance uploads (use edge locations of AWS to get into the backbone network faster), but does not solve timeouts/connection failures in large files. Multipart Upload is the specific solution for failure resilience in large file uploads.

Partly useful to give more time to upload, but Presigned URLs are about AUTENTICATION (URL (i) not about resilience to network failures. URL presigned still expires and upload should start from scratch. Multipart Upload is the solution for network failure resilience in large uploads.

Incorrect as a real solution. Increasing timeout is a fragile solution — in unstable connections, a larger timeout does not solve the root cause. Furthermore, for multiple GB files, maintaining a single connection TCP for hours is unreliable. Multipart Upload divides risk into smaller parts — each part is a smaller separate upload.

questions.text: A company has a web application that serves dynamic content (generated by the server, based on the logged in user) via Amazon CloudFront. They realized that all users are receiving the same cached content, even if the content is customized per user. What is causing this problem?
options: The CloudFront is ignoring cookies and session headers by default — without setting the cache policy to include authentication cookies in the key cache, CloudFront handles all the requests of the same URL as equal and serves the cached content of the first user for all
The TTL of the CloudFront is set very low — when the cache expires quickly, the CloudFront search for new content but uses the latest database data that has not yet been updated to the specific user
The S3 of origin does not support dynamic content — for personalized content, CloudFront must use a function Lambda as origin, no S3
The CloudFront only supports static content and cannot serve dynamic content generated by the server — it is necessary to use the ALB directly to personalized content
questions.explanation: By default, CloudFront does not include cookies or headers in the key cache — handles all requests for it URL for custom content per user (based on session cookie), you need to set up a Cache Policy that includes the authentication cookie in the key cache, or disable the caching for that type of content (using 'no-cache' in headers)).
questions.hint: For custom content per user (based on session/cookie), what needs to be included in the 'cache key' of CloudFront so that the content of one user is not served to another?
optionRationales: By default, CloudFront does not include cookies or headers in the key cache — handles all requests for it URL for custom content per user (based on session cookie), you need to set up a Cache Policy that includes the authentication cookie in the key cache, or disable the caching for that type of content (using 'no-cache' in headers)).

Incorrect. CloudFront can serve dynamic content (directs the request to the source when there is no cache or when configured not to cache). The problem described is not about technical impossibility, but about incorrect key cache configuration that ignores authentication cookies.

Incorrect. TTL low would do the CloudFront search for origin more often — the problem described is the OPOSTO (users receiving cached content from another user). TTL high with incorrect key cache (ignoring session cookies) is the cause of the problem, no TTL low.

Incorrect about S3 as cause. The problem is not about the source type — it's about the key cache configuration in CloudFront. Even with Lambda or EC2 as origin, if the key cache does not include authentication cookies, different users would receive the same cached content.

questions.text: A company has instances EC2 that process a lot of data from a pocket S3. The team realized that data transfer costs are high. How to reduce costs and latency of access to the S3 without crossing the public internet?
options: Configure CloudFront as CDN in front of the S3 — by cache the data from S3 no CloudFront, the instances EC2 search for edge location location instead of S3, reducing transfer costs
Use S3 Transfer Acceleration — Transfer Acceleration uses the backbone network of AWS for internal data transfers, reducing transfer costs between EC2 and S3
Move instances EC2 for the same AZ of the pocket S3 — when they are in the same area of availability, the traffic between EC2 and S3 no data transfer costs between AZs

Create a S3 Gateway Endpoint at VPC — the Gateway Endpoint creates a private route in the route table of the VPC for the S3, allowing for instances EC2 access the S3 via the network of the AWS without data transfer cost and without going through the internet
questions.explanation: Correct.. S3 Gateway VPC Endpoint creates a private route on VPC for the S3. Benefits: (1) Traffic doesn't go to the internet — it stays on the network AWS; (2) No cost of NAT Gateway (which would be necessary for private sub-networks to access S3 via internet); (3) No data transfer cost EC2→S3 in the same region. Gateway Endpoints to S3 and DynamoDB are GRATUITOS.
questions.hint: What type of VPC Endpoint creates a route GRATUITA and private between instances EC2 and the Amazon S3 (without going through the Internet or NAT Gateway)?
optionRationales: Correct.. S3 Gateway VPC Endpoint creates a private route on VPC for the S3. Benefits: (1) Traffic doesn't go to the internet — it stays on the network AWS; (2) No cost of NAT Gateway (which would be necessary for private sub-networks to access S3 via internet); (3) No data transfer cost EC2→S3 in the same region. Gateway Endpoints to S3 and DynamoDB are GRATUITOS.

Incorrect. S3 Transfer Acceleration is to accelerate uploads of FORA of AWS for the S3 (using edge locations), And there's CUSTO additional per transfer. Not suitable to reduce transfer costs EC2→S3 within the same region. VPC Endpoint is the free solution for this case.

Incorrect. S3 is not 'in a specific AZ' — it is a regional, not zonal service. EC2 and S3 'in the same AZ'. In addition, the transfer cost EC2→S3 in the same region is usually zero (even without VPC Endpoint), but cross the public internet (via NAT Gateway) It's costing.. VPC Endpoint eliminates this cost of NAT.

Incorrect. CloudFront is for delivery of content to USERS FINAIS (internet), not for communication EC2→S3 within the VPC. Create a CDN for internal access would be an unnecessarily complex and costly architecture. VPC Endpoint is the direct solution for access EC2→S3 without internet.

questions.text: A company has a database DynamoDB and realized that their writing system is being limited (throttled) in some partitions during peaks. They have a low cardinality partition key (minus distinct values). What causes throttling and how to mitigate it?
options: The DynamoDB needs to be migrated to an On-Demand mode — the On-Demand mode automatically scales without throttling, regardless of partition key distribution

Hot Partition — when the partition key has low cardinality, most writings go to few partitions, overloading these partitions with more requirements than the provided capacity; the solution is to use a partition key with high cardinality or add a random suffix to distribute the load
The DynamoDB does not support high-speed writing — for high-rate writing workloads, the bank should be migrated to Amazon RDS Aurora which has greater throughput of writing
Total provisioned throughput is insufficient — by increasing the WCUs DynamoDB, throttling disappears independent of partition distribution
questions.explanation: Correct.. DynamoDB distributes data and throughput by partitions based on the partition key. With low cardinality (e.g. status: 'active'/'inactive'), many items go to the same partitions. The throughput provided by partition has limit — excessive writing on the same partition generate throttling even if the general throughput is not exhausted. Solutions: use key with high cardinality (user_id, order_id), write sharding (add random shard)).
questions.hint: When many writings DynamoDB go to the same few partitions because of the low cardinality of the partition key, which term describes this problem — and what design change solves it?
optionRationales: Correct.. DynamoDB distributes data and throughput by partitions based on the partition key. With low cardinality (e.g. status: 'active'/'inactive'), many items go to the same partitions. The throughput provided by partition has limit — excessive writing on the same partition generate throttling even if the general throughput is not exhausted. Solutions: use key with high cardinality (user_id, order_id), write sharding (add random shard)).

Partly incorrect. Increasing total WCUs may help temporarily, but does not solve the Hot Partition problem — the DynamoDB distributes the throughput equally between partitions. Increase total WCUs increases the limit per partition, but with low cardinality, the hot partition will still receive all the load. The root of the problem is the unequal load distribution.

Partially incorrect. DynamoDB On-Demand reduces (but does not eliminate) the risk of throttling in Hot Partitions — each partition still has a per-partition throughput limit. Very hot partitions can still be limited. The fundamental solution is to improve the partition key design for more uniform distribution.

Incorrect. DynamoDB is designed exactly for writings of very high speed — when well modeled, it supports millions of requests per second. The problem is not inherent limitation of the DynamoDB, but a schematic design problem (partition key with low cardinality). With the correct design, DynamoDB exceeds relational banks in throughput of writing.

questions.text: A company has a web application that serves an increasing volume of users. They want to improve overall responsiveness without increasing the number of instances EC2. The development team realized that you want the database are the main gargalo. What is the first recommended optimization step before scaling horizontally?
options: Add more instances EC2 to Auto Scaling Group — Horizontal scaling distributes the burden of queries among more instances, improving overall responsiveness
Enable Multi-AZ No RDS — having a standby seat in another AZ, the RDS distributes the queries automatically between the two instances, doubling the throughput of queries

Analyze and optimize queries SQL — using RDS Performance Insights or EXPLAIN QUERY in the database to identify queries without indexes, full table scans, and N+1 cheries; creating appropriate indices can reduce cheries from seconds to milliseconds without any infrastructure change
Migrate immediately to DynamoDB — banks NoSQL are always faster than relational and will solve the performance problem without the need for optimization of desires
questions.explanation: Correct. Queries optimization is the first step (following Amdahl's Law: improve the gargalo). Queries without indexes in large tables do full table scan (millisseconds with index → minutes without). RDS Performance Insights identifies top-N queries for time of CPU. Adding an index can have an impact 10-100x greater than adding more instances — and without additional infrastructure cost.
questions.hint: Before scaling infrastructure, what is the first recommended optimization step for ' slow database queries' — which can have the greatest impact at the lowest cost?
optionRationales: Correct. Queries optimization is the first step (following Amdahl's Law: improve the gargalo). Queries without indexes in large tables do full table scan (millisseconds with index → minutes without). RDS Performance Insights identifies top-N queries for time of CPU. Adding an index can have an impact 10-100x greater than adding more instances — and without additional infrastructure cost.

Incorrect as PRIMEIRA step. Add instances EC2 does not help if the gargalo is the database (which does not scale horizontally with EC2). If the cravings are slow due to lack of indexes, have 10 cases EC2 making slow wants only increases the load on the bench. First optimize the wants, then climb if necessary.

Incorrect. DynamoDB is a significant architectural change that should not be made without analysis — and 'NoSQL is always faster' is a myth. The problem can be solved with indices in the existing relational bank. DynamoDB without solving the root cause of slow cravings does not guarantee improvement.

Incorrect. The Multi-AZ standby does not accept queries — it is only for failure. It does not double the throughput. The first step of optimization should be analysis and optimization of existing queries (indexes, rewrite of queries), not addition of infrastructure.

questions.text: A company uses Amazon EC2 and wants to understand the types of volumes EBS (Elastic Block Store) available. For a production database that needs high performance I/O (IOPS), what type of volume EBS is recommended?
options: st1 (Throughput Optimized HDD) — optimized specifically for relational databases, st1 has minimum latency and IOPS maximum of all types of EBS, being the type recommended for production

gp3 (General Purpose SSD) or i2 Block Express (Provisioned IOPS SSD) — gp3 offers up 16.000 IOPS with good cost/benefit ratio for most databases; io2 Block Express offers up to 256.000 IOPS for critical mission databases that need IOPS ultra-high and durability of 99.999%
sc1 (Cold HDD) — is the type of EBS with higher storage capacity by cost, ideal for production databases with large volumes of data
standard (magnetic) HDD) — magnetic volumes have greater throughput than SSDs for random I/O operations, being preferable for databases with many small queries
questions.explanation: Correct. For production database: gp3 is the type recommended for most cases (up to 16.000 IOPS, 1.000 MB/s of throughput, configurable regardless of volume size). IOPS much higher (Oracle), SAP HANA, Critical applications), i2 Block Express supports up 256.000 IOPS. Both are SSD and have low latency.
questions.hint: For high production database IOPS, which family of volumes EBS (SSD vs HDD) And what type of gp_ or io_ within this family offers the best cost-benefit for most cases?
optionRationales: Correct. For production database: gp3 is the type recommended for most cases (up to 16.000 IOPS, 1.000 MB/s of throughput, configurable regardless of volume size). IOPS much higher (Oracle), SAP HANA, Critical applications), i2 Block Express supports up 256.000 IOPS. Both are SSD and have low latency.

Incorrect. st1 is a HDD optimized for THROUGHPUT (MB/s) on sequential access workloads (big data, logs, data warehouses) — not for transactional databases that need to IOPS Highs with random access. HDD has a latency greater than SSD. For transactional production database, gp3 or yo2 (SSD) are the right types.

Incorrect. sc1 is the cheapest type per GB but has the PIOR performance (designed for cold data, rarely accessed). For production database with high performance requirement of I/O, sc1 would be a catastrophic choice — would be extremely slow. gp3 or i2 are the correct types.

Incorrect. Magnetic volumes (EBS Magnetic/standard) are the oldest and worst performing generation — smaller IOPS, higher latency, and replaced by SSDs in all cases of use. SSDs (gp3, io2) have much superior performance for databases with random I/O, which is exactly the standard of typical access of transactional banks.

questions.text: A company uses Amazon EC2 The team wants to understand what kind of instance to use for a machine learning application that needs to be GPU. What family of instances EC2 provides GPUs for ML workloads?
options: C family instances (e.g., c6i) — C instances are optimized for machine learning by having the highest number of vCPUs available per dollar, being more efficient than GPUs for ML

For instance, for the P family (e.g. p3, p4d) and G (e.g. g4dn, g5) — for the P family, the P family is optimized for HPC and ML training (GPUs) NVIDIA Tesla/A100), while G instances are optimized for ML inference and graphical rendering (GPUs) NVIDIA T4/A10G)

For instance, in the case of the M family (general purpose, e.g. m6i) — for instance, the M family has a balance sheet. CPU, memory and GPU, being the versatile choice recommended by AWS for ML workloads
Fora of the R family (memory-optimized, e.g.: r6i) — machine learning requires large amounts of RAM to load models, making the R instances optimized the correct choice
questions.explanation: Correct. AWS has families of specific instances with GPU: P = Parallel computing (Deep Learning training, HPC); G = Graphics (ML inference, gaming, rendering)..2xlarge has 1 GPU Tesla V100 with 16 GB HBM; g4dn.xlarge has 1 GPU T4 with 16 GB. For ML training of large models, family P; for inference, family G is more cost-effective.
questions.hint: For machine learning with GPU the AWS, which letter identifies the families of instances EC2 specialized in parallel computing (training) and graphic inference?
optionRationales: Correct. AWS has families of specific instances with GPU: P = Parallel computing (Deep Learning training, HPC); G = Graphics (ML inference, gaming, rendering)..2xlarge has 1 GPU Tesla V100 with 16 GB HBM; g4dn.xlarge has 1 GPU T4 with 16 GB. For ML training of large models, family P; for inference, family G is more cost-effective.

Incorrect. C instances (compute-optimized) have only CPUs — no GPUs. For ML (especially deep learning), GPUs are magnitude orders more efficient than CPUs for parallel matrix operations. P and G family instances are the correct ones for ML with GPU.
Incorrect. M instances are of general use (General Purpose) with CPU and balanced memory — no GPUs. Not recommended for ML that requires GPU. P and G families have specialized GPUs for ML.

Incorrect. R instances are memory-optimized (very RAM, no GPU), useful for in-memory databases (Redis), SAP HANA). For ML with GPU, P and G families are the right ones — they have so much RAM as specialized GPUs. A model of ML in CPU even with too much RAM would be much slower than in GPU.

questions.text: A company wants to understand how Amazon CloudFront One developer asks: 'What is a hit cache in CloudFront and how does it improve the user experience?' Which explanation is more accurate?
options: Hit cache no CloudFront means that the request was successfully authenticated by IAM — 'hit' is the term for successful authentication in the security system of CloudFront

Cache hit occurs when a edge location of the CloudFront already has the content requested in cache — the request is served directly from the edge (next to the user) without having to search at the source (S3, EC2); this reduces the latency of hundreds of ms (travel to origin) to milliseconds (the local edge))
Cache hit occurs when the user has visited the site before — the browser uses the user's local cache to load the page without making new requests to the server
Cache hit occurs when the CloudFront find an instance EC2 healthy to send the request — 'hit' indicates that the load balancing was successful in finding a server available
questions.explanation: Correct.: edge location has the object → immediately serves the local cache (very low latency). Miss cache: edge does not have the object → search at source (High latency, once) → stored in the edge → serves. The higher the hit ratio (% of requests served from the cache), the lower the average latency and the lower the load at source.
questions.hint: A hit cache in CloudFront means that the edge location it already has the content stored. What happens in the cache hit (cache miss) — and why the high hit rate is desirable?
optionRationales: Correct.: edge location has the object → immediately serves the local cache (very low latency). Miss cache: edge does not have the object → search at source (High latency, once) → stored in the edge → serves. The higher the hit ratio (% of requests served from the cache), the lower the average latency and the lower the load at source.

Incorrect. This describes cache of NAVEGADOR (browser cache), no cache of CloudFront. No. CloudFront, the cache is in edge locations (servers of AWS close to the user) — not in the user's browser. Even if the user deletes the browser cache, the CloudFront still serves the edge location (server cache).

Incorrect. 'Cache hit' is exclusively about content cache — has no connection to authentication or IAM. Hit = content found in cache; Miss = content not found, search in origin. It is standard terminology of caching in computer science.

Incorrect. Cache hit is not about load balancing or server availability. It's about the CloudFront serve content from your cache without having to contact the source. Load balance is function of ELB — CloudFront is about cache and content distribution.

questions.text: A company uses AWS Lambda and realized that some functions have timeout before completing. The maximum time limit configurable for a function Lambda is of 15 minutes. If one function needs to perform for more than 15 minutes, which approach is recommended?
options: Use an instance EC2 Spot to perform the long-term work — Spot Instances have no time limit and are 70% cheaper than On-Demand, being ideal for long processes

Use AWS Step Functions to orchestrate multiple functions Lambda in a workflow — each function Lambda performs part of the work within the limit of 15 minutes; or Step Functions keeps the state between the steps and orchestrates the sequential or parallel execution of functions
Increase function memory Lambda for maximum (10 GB) — more memory increases proportionally to CPU and allows the function to complete in less time, within the 15 minutes
Split function Lambda in smaller parts and call Lambda recursively — the function is self-invoked when it reaches 14 minutes, passing the state as a parameter to continue the work
questions.explanation: Correct.. Step Functions is the orchestrator of the serverless workflows of AWS. The pattern 'Lambda Orchestration' allows to divide long works into smaller steps, each within the limit of 15 min. Step Functions management status, retry, error handling and timeouts between the steps. It is the serverless approach to long-term jobs.
questions.hint: For work exceeding 15 minutes, which service AWS allows to orchestrate multiple functions Lambda in sequential steps, maintaining status between the steps?
optionRationales: Correct.. Step Functions is the orchestrator of the serverless workflows of AWS. The pattern 'Lambda Orchestration' allows to divide long works into smaller steps, each within the limit of 15 min. Step Functions management status, retry, error handling and timeouts between the steps. It is the serverless approach to long-term jobs.

Partially correct that more memory = more CPU = faster execution. FUNDAMENTALMENTE needs more than 15 minutes (e.g. file processing of 100 GB), more memory may not be enough. Step Functions divide the work to not depend on the timeout limit.

Right. EC2 has no limit of 15 min. But, Spot Instances can be closed with 2 minutes of warning — terrible for long work that does not tolerate interruption. EC2 On-demand or Fargate (without timeout limit) would be computational alternatives for long work, but Step Functions + Lambda is the preferred serverless approach.

It works technically but is an unrecommended practice — 'recursive' Lambda' is fragile, difficult to debug, without visibility of the state, and can cause unexpected costs if the loop does not finish. Step Functions is the official and recommended solution to orchestrate works that exceed the timeout limit of the Lambda.

questions.text: A company has an application that serves global users. They want to minimize latency for all users, regardless of where they are. AWS improves network latency by routing traffic through the global backbone of AWS instead of the public internet?
options: Amazon CloudFront — by distributing content to edge locations global, o CloudFront automatically route traffic through the backbone of AWS, reducing latency for both static content and connections TCP dynamics

AWS Global Accelerator — uses the global private network of AWS (backbone) to route traffic from users to the nearest endpoint, and after the AWS for the final destination; reduces latency and jitter by avoiding unpredictable jumps of the public internet, besides providing static IPs anycast global
Amazon VPC Peering among all regions AWS — by creating peering between regional VPCs, the traffic of global users passes through the private network AWS between regions, reducing latency
Amazon Route 53 with Latency Routing — when using latency routing policy, the Route 53 directs users to the endpoint with lower latency DNS, automatically optimizing the network path
questions.explanation: Correct.. AWS Global Accelerator has two main components: (1) static anycast IPs that direct users to edge location AWS nearest immediately; (2) Route traffic through the backbone of AWS (private network, less jumps, more predictable latency) from edge to destination endpoint. CloudFront (CDN which hides content), Global Accelerator is a network accelerator TCP/UDP no caching.
questions.hint: What service AWS uses anycast IPs and routes traffic through the global private backbone AWS — other than one CDN, without caching, focused on reducing latency of REDE for TCP/UDP?
optionRationales: Correct.. AWS Global Accelerator has two main components: (1) static anycast IPs that direct users to edge location AWS nearest immediately; (2) Route traffic through the backbone of AWS (private network, less jumps, more predictable latency) from edge to destination endpoint. CloudFront (CDN which hides content), Global Accelerator is a network accelerator TCP/UDP no caching.

Partially correct (CloudFront also uses the network of AWS and improve latency via caching), but the question specifically describes 'minimize latency of REDE when routing through the backbone of AWS' — That's the AWS Global Accelerator. CloudFront is mainly for content caching. For applications TCP/UDP no caching (such as games, VoIP, dynamic APIs), Global Accelerator is the correct solution.

Incorrect. Route 53 Latency Routing chooses the ENDPOINT less latency (which region responds faster), but does not change the CAMINHO network — traffic still goes through the user's public internet to the endpoint. Global Accelerator changes the network path to use the private backbone of AWS, reducing latency and jitter independent of the endpoint.

Incorrect. VPC Peering connects VPCs from AWS (private communication between resources) AWS) — is not a solution to reduce latency of external internet users for applications AWS. Global Accelerator is the service to optimize the network path of external users to endpoints AWS.

questions.text: A startup AWS or reduce the cost of their instances EC2 of development, which run only on the working days of 8h at 18h. What is the simplest way to reduce costs without changing the type of instance?
options: Enable EC2 Hibernation in the Fora — Hibernation Maintains the State of RAM when shutting down, reducing the cost of computing to zero while preserving the working state of the developers
Move instances to Spot Instances — Spot Instances cost 70-90% less than On-Demand and AWS closes them only when you need the capacity for other customers
Convert instances to Reserved Instances (RI) of 1 year — RIs provide discount of up to 75% and automatically pause the instances when they are not in use at business hours

Use EC2 Scheduler Forum or AWS Systems Manager Automation to stop instances automatically at 18h and start them at 8h — cases EC2 stops do not generate computer charge (only volume EBS associated), reducing the cost of ~10h/day of day use for 0h outside business hours

questions.text: A company is optimizing costs of AWS Lambda. The developer realized that some functions have timeout configured to 15 minutes, but in practice they complete in 30 seconds. How set timeout time affects the cost of Lambda?

questions.explanation: Correct.. AWS Lambda payable by GB-computational seconds: real duration × assigned memory. If the function completes in 30 seconds, you pay for 30 seconds — the timeout of 15 min does not increase the cost. The timeout is a 'safety cap' to avoid functions stuck in infinite loop, not a charged time. However, a very long timeout can cause high cost if the function actually stops.

Incorrect. Lambda is active only while the function is running code — the Lambda does not 'wait' for the timeout in idle. When the function returns (even if it is 30s before the timeout), the container is in 'warm' state (not charged) until it is dislocated by the system. The timeout has no cost while the function is not active.

Incorrect. No additional charge per configured timeout — Lambda does not charge for timeout, charges for real execution. 1 min vs 15 min has the same cost if the function always completes in 30 seconds. The timeout only sets the maximum limit, not an additional cost.

CloudFront reduces the number of requests to origin via caching, further reducing the cost of data transfer from origin. The result is total cost of transfer smaller with CloudFront than without.

questions.text: A company wants to start using AWS The financial manager asks: 'There is a minimum contract or membership fee to start using AWS?' What is the basic model of precision of the AWS?
options: A AWS requires a minimum contract of 1 year with fixed monthly payment — the value is calculated on the basis of the estimate of use provided at the beginning, and any excesses are charged to the part

A AWS use pay-as-you-go model (pay for what to use) — no membership fee, no minimum contract for On-Demand services; you create a free account and pay only for what to consume, you can stop using at any time without penalties (except for commitments such as Reserved Instances and Savings Plans that you optionally chose)
A AWS use a subscription model per service — each service has a fixed monthly price that you pay regardless of use, similar to a SaaS subscription plan
A AWS charges an accession rate of $200 to create an account, but this value is reversed as credits AWS in the first month of use
questions.explanation: Correct. AWS does not require minimum contract for On-Demand services — you pay for use (per hour, per second, per GB). Creating an account is free; costs start when you use the services. This is different from Reserved Instances/Savings Plans, which are optional commitments that the customer chooses to obtain discounts.
questions.hint: What is the fundamental price model of the AWS — there is adherence rate, minimum contract, or is based on actual consumption without commitments (for On-demand services))?
optionRationales: Correct. AWS does not require minimum contract for On-Demand services — you pay for use (per hour, per second, per GB). Creating an account is free; costs start when you use the services. This is different from Reserved Instances/Savings Plans, which are optional commitments that the customer chooses to obtain discounts.

Incorrect. AWS does not require a minimum contract of 1 On-Demand service year. There is no mandatory 'premium usage estimate'. The standard model is pay-as-you-go without commitment. Long-term contracts (Enterprise Agreements) exist, but are optional for large customers who want to negotiate discounts — they are not mandatory.

Incorrect. No membership fee to create an account AWS — it is completely free to create an account. New customers can have access to Free Tier, but there is no 'adherence rate' charge of $200 or any value.

Incorrect. AWS does not use subscription model per service for most services. The standard model is pay-per-use (per hour, per second, per GB, per request). Some services have fixed components (ex.: NAT Gateway has a cost per hour of provisioning), but it is not a 'fixed monthly subscription per service' that you pay regardless of use.

questions.text: A company uses AWS and want to understand how the data transfer cost works. What is the general rule about data transfer collection in AWS?
options: Data from the AWS for the internet (Data Transfer Out) are collected; data that enter in the AWS Internet (Data Transfer In) are free; transfer between services in the same region and the same AZ is free for many service pairs; transfer between AZs within the same region has cost ($0.01/GB)
Only the transfer between regions AWS different is charged — within a region, any data transfer (between AZs, services, instances) is completely free
All data traffic in AWS is free of charge — AWS includes data transfer on all service plans at no additional cost to encourage the use of the platform
All data traffic in AWS is charged uniformly to $0.09/GB independent of origin and destination — both entry and exit, both between regions and within the same region
questions.explanation: The general rule of data transfer collection AWS: (1) Internet → AWS (Inbound): $0 (free of charge); (2) AWS → Internet (Outbound): charged by GB (various by region), ~$0.09/GB for the first 10 TB Of us-east-1); (3) Same AZ: $0 for many pairs; (4) Between AZs in the same region: ~$0.01/GB (go back and forth)); (5) Between regions: charged as outbound. These rules have exceptions (CloudFront→internet has its own table, etc..).
questions.hint: Which direction of data traffic is charged (entry or exit from the AWS for internet)? And the transfer between AZs within the same region has cost?
optionRationales: The general rule of data transfer collection AWS: (1) Internet → AWS (Inbound): $0 (free of charge); (2) AWS → Internet (Outbound): charged by GB (various by region), ~$0.09/GB for the first 10 TB Of us-east-1); (3) Same AZ: $0 for many pairs; (4) Between AZs in the same region: ~$0.01/GB (go back and forth)); (5) Between regions: charged as outbound. These rules have exceptions (CloudFront→internet has its own table, etc..).

Incorrect. The data transfer fee on AWS is not uniform — varies greatly according to route: internet → AWS = $0, same AZ = $0, between AZs = ~$0.01/GB, AWS → internet = ~$0.09/GB (for us-east-1). Apply $0.09/GB for everything would overestimate the costs of internal transfer.

Incorrect. Data transfer to the internet (outbound) It is charged and can represent a significant part of the invoice for applications that serve a lot of content. This cost is real and should be considered in architecture (e.g. use CloudFront to reduce direct transfer costs of S3).

Incorrect. Transfer between AZs within the MESMA region TEM cost (~$0.01/GB in each direction). This is relevant for Multi-AZ architectures that make a lot of communication between AZs (ex.: EC2 in AZ-reading from RDS in AZ-b) Designing to minimize traffic between AZs can reduce costs.

questions.text: A company manages multiple accounts AWS from different teams in the same organization. They want to have a single consolidated invoice and possibility to share discount volumes between accounts. AWS provides that capacity?
options: AWS Control Tower — by creating a Landing Zone with the Control Tower, a AWS automatically configures billing consolidation and sharing of Reserved Instances among all accounts created by Landing Zone
Amazon Cost Explorer with Cross-Account Reporting — enabling cross-account reports in Cost Explorer, multiple account invoices are automatically unified into a single monthly invoice

AWS Organizations with Consolidated Billing — when creating an organization with a master account, all member accounts have consolidated invoices in a single; the usage volumes of all accounts are aggregated to reach the discount bands per volume more quickly (ex.: S3 and CloudFront have prices per piece of land)
AWS IAM with Multi-Account Access — when setting up cross-account access in IAM, a AWS automatically consolidates the invoices of accessible accounts, facilitating financial management
questions.explanation: Correct.. AWS Organizations with Consolidated Billing: (1) A single invoice for all the accounts of the organization; (2) Use aggregation for Tier Pricing — if an account uses 5 TB of S3 and another uses 8 TB, the 13 TB combined in the consolidated invoice can place the total use in a cheaper price range; (3) Sharing of Reserved Instances and Savings Plans between accounts (optional)).
questions.hint: What service AWS allows you to create a multiple account organization with a single consolidated invoice — where the use of all accounts is aggregated to take advantage of discount bands per volume?
optionRationales: Correct.. AWS Organizations with Consolidated Billing: (1) A single invoice for all the accounts of the organization; (2) Use aggregation for Tier Pricing — if an account uses 5 TB of S3 and another uses 8 TB, the 13 TB combined in the consolidated invoice can place the total use in a cheaper price range; (3) Sharing of Reserved Instances and Savings Plans between accounts (optional)).

Incorrect. Cost Explorer is for cost-VISUALIZATION — does not unify invoices. Cost Explorer may show data from multiple accounts of an organization, but actual billing consolidation is done by AWS Organizations (Consolidated Billing). These are complementary tools: Organizations does the consolidation, Cost Explorer does the analysis.

Incorrect. IAM multi-account access is for access to resources between accounts (via roles and trust policies) — has no relation to bill consolidation. AWS Organizations is the service for managing multiple accounts and consolidated billing.

Partly correct that the Control Tower use AWS Organizations Internally (and therefore has Consolidated Billing). Control Tower is for multi-account governance (security, compliance, guardrail configuration) — is not the service directly responsible for Consolidated Billing. The underlying mechanism is the AWS Organizations.
